lines.st: In Ursine mythology, long before the Crystal Age—or perhaps a far earlier age still—
there once lived a giant named Zheuzhyk.
The giant was so tall, the humans could not see him with their eyes. Each slight movement of his sculpted the shapes of the lands.
The Barton Plains are the tracks of his footsteps. The endless Rudokny Mountains were just barely enough to serve as a pillow when he slumbered.
The giant in the legends could not definitively be described as good or evil. He was simply a big, simple existence that the masses below could look up to.
What is difficult to explain, however, is that references to gigantic beings like Zheuzhyk are often found in different mythologies across the land.
These similar stories might perhaps reflect a common characteristic in all human subconscious:
No matter when and where, from the bottom of their hearts, humans seek some kind of a greater power—an enormous being, abstract or specific, that stands in contrast to their minuscule existence.
Mankind is accustomed to worshipping great beings conjured in the imagination, and seeking their projections in reality.
Yet when such a being finally presents itself before the masses in some shape and form—
It never fails to crush their genial fantasies.

lines.x: You know, Boris really is a nutjob.
You saw his arrogant shit face when he met the Marshal too, didn't you? He made a bit of coin these past few years and it gave him a big head.
Get him a few more coins and he won't even bow to the tsar.

He figures the Marshal doesn't have the balls to try anything funny. Hell, if the Marshal can't scrape together a decent price? He'd probably turn around right there and side with the Third Army instead.
Heh, that's how anyone would play it, with a decent way out.
A short-sighted businessman sitting on a treasure like this is only ever gonna think about how to use it to fill his pockets. He's never given a single thought to its true worth!
No wonder he doesn't give the Ursine military the respect we deserve. He can't understand what our land is built on. Really, nobody gives us our due respect!
If I were the Marshal, I would've slit that coward's throat and stamped my fingerprint on the contract in his blood.
Heh, if I were the Marshal... I'd order the army to fight to the end, until every Ursine learned to respect us. Not like now... with everyone looking down on us.
Gah... enough of that nonsense!
Do you seriously think the Marshal ever actually backed those morons in the Sixth and Eighth Armies?

With everything they've been up to? They were destined to fail. One does not simply provoke a rebellion in Ursus, especially not with so few guns and battleships... or even with ten times what they had.
They're no different from any of those businessmen. They don't even know where Ursine pride comes from—but the Marshal had it figured out long ago.
So count yourself lucky. You still get to grumble while you're out on a mission, instead of being sent to the Far North to turn to stone with the Infected.
The hell are you doing?
What I was ordered to do. Making sure everyone's dead.
We could've at least had him find the others!
Let's not waste more time. We wouldn't even be here today if these white coat bastards had half a mind to cooperate.
There, found one. Hiding under the desk there.
No! No! Let me go!
Please! Please don't kill me! I'll tell you whatever you want—
What do we do? He's willing to cooperate.
Trust me. It'll be faster if we just do this ourselves.
Keep looking. There has to be more of them.
And get a head count. Remember. No one gets out of this place alive.
I'm starting to get a little annoyed too. This place hardly has any ventilation, and it reeks of blood. Ugh, it's getting my boots all sticky.
Oh... Found one.
There's another here.

lines.st: An ancient Minoan philosopher once said that 'Man is, by nature, a creative animal.'
By his works, man accumulates experience he then uses to create—in concrete or abstract—and solve the problems he faces.
Such creations fulfill man's needs and assuage his fears. At the same time, they reflect his aesthetics and morals.
Each and every one of mankind's creations is a manifestation of its own traits—
Perhaps it was the same process by which the Creator created mankind.
And among all of mankind's creations, the one that best reflects its innate nature, for good or for evil—
The concept of the 'nation' undoubtedly takes the crown.

lines.x: Director! They've made it into Area D!
I heard... the sound of fighting... Are they... are they killing people?
Ilia, how much longer?
Forty minutes.
We've done all we can, but it'll take forty more minutes to complete the lockdown procedure.
Do we really have to wait till it's completely locked down?
What else can we do?! Do you want me to hand this thing over to the army completely intact, and let it fall into the butchers' hands, letting them effortlessly massacre even more people?
Blyat! I've lived my whole life as a failure. I refuse to be an accomplice to these murderers even in death!
It's too late...
But how could the butchers work out all our secrets so quickly...?
We have a traitor in our midst... Director, somebody must've sold us out.
Sergei, maybe? I should've known when he kept probing me with all those questions.
Blyat! It must be him... Why? He could have been a good man...
Calm down, Ilia. Thinking like this will not do us any good right now.
Focus on the task at hand. We still have a chance to salvage something.
Director... It's too late for us... isn't it?
You got my warning. You shouldn't have come back. Even with you here, we still won't finish in—
Ilia, take the others and go.
Go? Where could we possibly go?
To Taymyr, in the north. It's close to the Third Army's territory. Andrian wouldn't dare launch a manhunt there.
Hide there and stay far away from the cities. Avoid contact with any factions of the government, and do not believe any promises of protection the Third Army gives you.
Go now. I will stay.
Ilia?
No... I will stay behind.
Ilia.
I won't run. I can't. You shouldn't be entrusting our colleagues' lives to a man like me!
Director Kal'tsit... No, my teacher. The land needs you far more than it needs me. You should go, not me. You should never have come back at all!
Even if you find a way to hide the Originium on your skin, they will find out that you're Infected. Then you will suffer a fate a hundred times worse than a quick and easy death—
Besides, only you can lead our innocent colleagues to safety. You can't say no.
But you, too, have a reason to live... Think about Lyudmila, your daughter—
Please, care for her.
Take her away from here, away from this country, and as far away as you can... Heh, I was hoping she would get to study under you for much longer, but it is what it is.
Don't tell her what happened here today. Nothing good will come of it. Let her explore the land in her own way.
I promise you. I will take her far away from Ursus. Until she is able to care for herself, she will be safe.
And I promise you this. You and your colleagues' work will not go to waste.
That's more than enough for me...
...It's an intriguing thought. We chose to open this Sarcophagus before, and now we choose to keep it dormant. Which was the right choice?
We did what we thought to be correct. As for the answer, perhaps it is up to Lyudmila... or even her children to determine.
I guess you're right... Now go.
Goodbye, Ilia.
So you're the last one?
The last what?
The last one alive in the lab? Yes. The last one in this country to despise its savagery? Somehow, I doubt it.
You stayed behind. What did you do to the Sarcophagus?
Oh, about ten seconds ago, the Sarcophagus's core function completely locked down. You want to reactivate it? It'll take you lot a century.
You—what are you, vanguards of the murderous Fourth Army? Go back and tell Andrian that his plans to use this beast as a weapon of territorial expansion have just gone belly-up.
Too bad, the glorious Marshal Andrian has failed again and again. His army couldn't conquer a tiny laboratory, or, hell, even a lone, miserable researcher.
Alright, you may exercise your authority to take my life now.
Hm, not bad, for a hard-headed shit...
We'll do it your way.

lines.st: For the Empire of Ursus, or perhaps even for all the lands, the Sarcophagus was a groundbreaking discovery, possibly meant for a different era.
I, too, once had ill-timed expectations for it. The tragedy that unfolded before my eyes, in the end, was my punishment.
The innocent sacrifice of the talented researchers in the institute...
No doubt that was a punishment to this country for its hubris.
Even if the effects of this punishment may not be fully realized until much, much later.
In this moment of time, I can offer only a small piece of advice.
If you no longer wish to be dragged into this endless cycle of political conflict and revenge...
If you believe that there yet remains something precious on these lands worth protecting from the mandibles of the manglerbeasts—
Then I ask you to keep this letter and to stop the armies' pursuit of the laboratory's survivors.
This is neither a threat nor a plea.
I simply hope that you will make the right decision based on your interests and conscience.
To Marquess Sheremetyevo Boris
In 1077, a bloody incident occurred in the southeastern corner of Ursus. For an empire that had just suffered a devastating civil war, it was hardly a noticeable incident.

Perhaps it will take a hundred years—when historians revisit these turbulent times in their piles of old writings—for everyone to truly understand that what happened at the research institute in Chernobog was both emblematic of its era and a seed.
Even if, at this moment in time, it is buried deep under the Ursine permafrost, waiting for its time to sprout.

lines.x: Where am I?
What happened to the court martial? What happened to due process?
Why did you bring me here? And where are my men?
Shut up.
You would have to kill me.
You're on death row. It doesn't make a difference whether we kill you now or later.
Too bad for you, the bigwigs don't have time to deal with seditious leadership like yourself, so...
You'll just have to hold up here. Listen to how your men in the other rooms stay quiet?
I'm a soldier, not a criminal. The same goes for my men!
From the moment you worked up the arrogance to rise against the Marshal, your entire formation ceased to be a part of the glorious Fourth Army.
I did the right thing, and all the warriors you have dismissed as traitors, and in fact all Ursines of conscience, know that this is the right thing to do.
No, Captain Yakov Petrov.
What you did was the foolish thing to do, and you dragged your family and your friends into this mess.
Mother, please, sit down first... You're shaking.
The people from the army have already gone.
Army... Yakov...
Is that you, Yakov?
You are back?
But the apple trees have yet to blossom... It's too soon for your summer vacation.
Has Marshal Andrian been treating you well? Has he been bringing you on his adventures? What about the clothes I had them bring to you? Did they fit?
I can't see well, so I couldn't sew your name onto them... but Sofia helped. You've always loved her handicrafts—
Sofia?
Mother.
You're not Sofia.
Nor am I Yakov. I am neither Brother nor Sister.
Who are you? Why are you in my home? Somebody—
Mother, I'm Tulin, your young son who has been away for a long time. You remember me, do you not?
The servants have been dismissed, and the butler has left.
What are you saying?
Yakov is in prison. Sofia is married, but she is busy scrambling about in Deity Grypherburg, desperately trying to get him out. She needs money to resolve some issues, and we must help.
Moreover, we cannot embroil the innocent in a fate they do not deserve, can we?
*sigh...*
No matter the case, please listen to what I have to say, Mother. You may never have heard these things, but this letter was written by Yakov in prison.
Let me read it for you...
The boy says and opens the envelope, only to find a blank sheet of paper.
In an instant, his face turns as white as the sheet in his hands.
Yakov... Isn't Yakov in the army?
The army has been here, Mother.
The boy folds the sheet of paper in half, bit by bit, as if needing the time to slow down and process the truth.
Then, he puts the small and neatly folded square into his breast pocket, normally occupied by a handkerchief, to keep it close to his heart.
They said that because of the role that Yakov played in the Fourth Army's mutiny...
The Petrovs have been stripped of nobility and are now mere commoners... to be exiled to the Northern Tundra Mines, Mining Zone No. 9.
We set out tomorrow.
Old Peter's buried. It's time for us to go.
First, it was our children, then our wives, and then our parents... How many more bodies will we have to bury?
What are you doing, writing a letter? Is it to your mother?
No... Not a letter. I'm just trying to put everything I see into words. If the chance ever comes, I hope people will come to know all that has happened.
You still have the strength for that? I must say, I really envy you.
I can't walk very far, and we still have yet to make it to the Northern Tundra.
It's only been three months since we left Omska.
It'll probably be spring again by the time we make it to the mines.
Spring... Haha! Spring!
My sweet summer child. You think there is spring in the tundra...?
Right, spring. As long as we make it there.
Your mother was spared because she's blind and off her rocker.
She doesn't have to suffer the pain of exile, and you are spared from having to bury her like a nameless woman. Thanks to that, you are so optimistic, you might as well be a lunatic.
But... what gives you the right?
What gives you the right?

You, too, are an exiled criminal, and yet someone like you gets special treatment. You don't have to watch as every member of your family slowly takes their last breaths, as their bodies slowly turn cold.
Is it because I was only a dime-a-dozen porter before I turned into an Infected?
What did I do wrong? And what did you do right?
The Infected murmurs. He wants to scream the thoughts in his mind out loud more than anybody, but he is trapped under the watchful gaze of the guards.
The boy shakes his head and moves up closer toward the Infected.
I was privileged, yes... And it wasn't because of my own hard work. For that, I feel ashamed.
But the question you posed is one that I am seeking the answer to myself.
What?
Why are some of us born privileged, while others are born disdained? Why do we stand in opposition to each other, even though we are all humans? What can we do to break free of the status quo?
I will tell you. I don't know.
But my instinct tells me that we need to at least survive and stand back up.
It's only when we stand together and combine our strength that we are able to keep thinking about where the problem lies and figure out a way to change something.
What are you talking about—
The boy suddenly lifts his head and looks into the Infected man's perplexed eyes.
Just pretend I'm talking nonsense.
The way I see it, people like you with nothing to their name are the true masters of the land.
For the time being, please, climb onto my back. At the very least, I still have some strength in me. I can carry you for a while.

lines.loc: Mining Zone No. 9, Northern Tundra, Ursus Winter 1099

lines.st: '...In Iberia, people almost never turn their gazes upon one another, as if making eye contact were sinful, and as if doing so would violate a deeply held creed.
'I have also witnessed similar behaviors in the mines of Ursus, the slums of Leithanien, and the underground factories of Victoria.

'At first, I surmised that they feared seeing in their soot-covered faces the same despair they felt in their hearts. It was only later that I realized it was because, their eyes had little room for anything beyond the urgency of survival.

'That being the case, who could blame them for their silence and for failing to notice their fellow man, for failing to look to a future even further away, for failing to stand together to rise against their oppressors?'

'The land sprawls far and wide. I traveled throughout Ursus, and then made my way to even farther lands. On my way, I continued to tell those who had lost everything—or perhaps have never truly had anything: You are the true masters of the land.

'As things currently stand, and we have yet to see any real change, my words feel like little more than mockery, yet I need to keep telling them. It is only by planting these seeds that they may subconsciously realize the truth behind my words and let them sprout within their hearts.
'When one truly has nothing, one has nothing to lose, granting the most resolute of resolves. The same truth lies within us all.'

lines.x: Boss!
We're all packed up, ready to go. How about you?
Hm...
Boss?
Uh... Oh! Right. Let's get going.
Thanks for coming to get me. I'm all packed up too—
Uhh.
You dug out all this stuff again? What a mess... Here, I'll help you pack up.
Thanks!
I came to the mines late, I've never seen the one who sent you the letters. Did they really leave the mines and keep on writing to you?
Yes.
First time I've ever heard of anyone missing life in the mines so much.
Perhaps it's not the mines that he misses, but the people.
As I remember, when the news of political prisoners getting pardoned first got here to the Northern Tundra, his first reaction wasn't one of joy. It was worry.
He was worried that we wouldn't be able to leave like him, and that his theories would never be proven...
But he still left in the end.
Of course. He said he'd travel all across Ursus, and now we're leaving this place behind too, aren't we?
Then let's get going, Boss.
Right, I started calling you 'Boss' because that's what everyone here calls you, but I've been thinking, you've got to have an actual name, right?
Huh, have I really never told you?
Hm... Tulin. You can call me Tulin.
Hell yeah, 'Tulin.' Good name. Here, I'll help you up.
Thank you...
Yeah, let's hurry and get out of here.
While the snow is still calm, and before the ones in the warm houses change their minds.

lines.loc: Great Hall Corridor, The State Council of the Ursine Empire, Deity Grypherburg, Ursus Winter, 1102

lines.st: '...Investigation shows that the extremely provocative messages left behind by the instigators are all quotations from Yakov Petrov, a war criminal who got what he deserved during the Great Rebellion.
'While on death row, he wrote a will...'
'Whose fault was the Katorga Uprising? What should we do now? How do we save these young people who know nothing but rebellion?'
'While the Chairman's condition is now stable, the fiend behind the assassination attempt remains at large.
'The Deity Grypherburg Police call on everyone to stay indoors after nightfall to avoid arousing suspicion and interfering with the search operation.'

lines.x: (Flips through the newspaper)
(Closes the newspaper)
Zdravstvuyte, gospodin. Could you fetch me a fresher newspaper?
Uh. I-I'm afraid that will require prior approval.
This lounge's newspapers and reading material are maintained daily by a page. I can't just conjure up one out of thin air for you.
Besides, you are an Infected. You may have been let in, but I don't know if you really have authorization to read this—
*cough*!
Gospodin Gorchikov—I mean, General!
You may call me Vice Chairman here. Thank you for your help. I will handle the rest.
What? Could that be... is this your guest?
Bozhe moy... I'm so stupid! Please accept my sincerest apologies, gospodin, for my words—
So it goes. What you said is the truth.
Indeed, I am an Infected.
The newspaper. You, I... I—
*sigh...* Just do as I said, and let me handle the rest!
'General?'
Please, don't tease me... You know better than anyone whether or not I will become general.
You weren't so hard on yourself before, Vasily.
And you weren't this easy to talk to, for an officer of the army.
The man who stands before you now is a mere Infected warrior, no longer an Imperial Guard instructor.
You still remember my name, do you not? Call me Hellagur.
Very good, Gospodin Hellagur. How does it feel to return to Grypherburg? This is hardly a time for sightseeing, but still.
It's a lot quieter than I expected. A lot of things have changed, so much so that hardly anything from times gone by still remains.
Right. So much has changed, and who could say whether these changes are for the better or worse?
The businessmen have gotten richer. Thanks to that, the city has become a more beautiful place. At the same time, modesty and all our other virtues are now valued less.
Perhaps you've heard already. His Imperial Majesty is going to build a so-called 'citizens' forum' and hand over all decision-making to the common folk of Grypherburg.
And now, we can all say that the nobles have finally given up on the one job they still had and handed it over to the commoners.
It sounds like you don't agree with this at all.
It's not up to me to agree or disagree, but if there's someone out there who can solve all these problems facing society, it doesn't matter who that person is.
This doesn't sound like something the vice chairman, with all his authority, would say.
I've never been one eager to put my power on full display. You know that better than anyone.
Come to think of it, I'm surprised they didn't confiscate your blade when you entered the city.

Oh, this. All they did was make a note of it. I didn't receive too much... special treatment. This is only a replica, and one that hasn't been sharpened. It's as lethal as a piece of scrap metal. Perhaps that's why.
Where's the real one?
I gave it to someone I trust.
Someone you trust...
I understand you have a daughter.
Yes, I do. If we find the time later, I would love to introduce you to her. She has heard many stories of your achievements, and she respects you deeply.
And it's not just her. Many in today's Imperial Guard still remember your name.
It's been some years since we hung up our hats, but those stories yet fly over the Imperial Guard Academy like a banner. At your convenience, I'd like to take you for a visit.
You have my thanks for keeping those sacrifices so close to your heart, but I truly have no intention of serving as a banner ever again.
I am here for another reason. Surely you must already know that Rhodes Island has established an office here in Grypherburg.
I am well aware. I even signed a few documents in the Chairman's stead.
*sigh...* Even if our stance on the Infected has relaxed, the conflicts regarding them remain as sharp as ever.
Still, if we're speaking of you personally—I would be happy to take this chance to restore your honors in Grypherburg.
I don't need the empire to restore my identity or honor.
Then what do you need?
Simply put, what Rhodes Island needs is precisely what I need.
More specifically, you mean—
'Please inform Chairman Witte that the designated Rhodes Islanders have departed for Deity Grypherburg.'
If my timing is right, they should have already made it to the office.
Oh...
Chairman—
Is the Chairman here?!
I am the vice chairman. What's the matter?
I... I have a report!
Th-The First Army—
The soldier tries his best to get a noun out of his mouth, but he finds himself frozen when he spots Hellagur standing to the side.
Vasily shakes his head to signal that there is nothing to worry about.
What of the First Army?
The new weapon of mass destruction that the First Army has been developing... The firing test was successful!
And, what's the problem?
The problem is... the weapon doesn't use Originium... or any energy source that we've ever employed!
What?
I understand the situation.
My concern is, will this information also cross the desk of the General Chamber of Commerce as we are speaking?
I expect so. Something on this scale cannot be covered up completely. The G.C.C. will find out.
Intel from multiple sources indicates a high likelihood that something abnormal is happening to the Kolossal Prime Vein, and that Ursus is facing an energy crisis.
This is corroborated by the recent movements of the First Army on the border... it's certainly cause for concern.
We do not know if the energy issues will spread to other regions, nor how Ursus may react.
Has there been any official communication from Grypherburg?
In the face of such a crisis, the empire's first reaction is to hide the truth, rather than seek cooperation. Their stance is clear as day.
A dying beast is a dangerous one. Even without its energy advantage, the Ursine war machine remains terrifying.
We have defeated many foes. We are not afraid of war. But we must be even more vigilant about threats from within.
You are concerned that the G.C.C. will use this as leverage against the Adeptus?
Even they must know the threat we will face if Ursus chooses to expand at this time. Kazimierz cannot afford another incident!
Do not underestimate the merchants' thirst for profit.
They're already making their move. The invisible war already began when they framed their first innocent campaign knight.
Fetch me Liam. Quickly.
And where is the scion of Nearl these days?

lines.loc: Eastern Mines, Fifth Army Territory Dec 1101

lines.x: Enough! Stop blowing it up! Do you want the whole mountain to collapse?!
Don't you understand, mudak? There's nothing here! Not even one chunk of Originium! It's all dried up! Gone!
Shut your trap! We must keep digging! This isn't the Far North... the ore in the east isn't gone! We just need to get it out first—
'Find the Originium'! Those are our orders!
Well, you can hang us all then, because those orders aren't happening!
Ivan's gone blind and I'm deaf in one ear! Better to hang than have all my organs turned to mush by the bombs!
Turn us Infected and bury us in the mountains for all I care! Maybe you'll get the Originium growing again that way!
Gosudar-batyushka... have mercy on us... have mercy on Ursus...
...That concludes my report.
Intercepted communications indicate that the Third Army has received news and announced a ceasefire with the Seventh. Only mobile units remain on standby.
Where was the explosion?
In the wilderness of Central, roughly 2300 km in a straight line from our front lines with the Fourth Army, with no nomadic cities making their winter transit nearby.

But the scattered settlements in the area were not evacuated in advance. Rumors are that the people and animals were annihilated instantly, leaving behind only strange-colored soil and ash... it must have been incredibly powerful.
Has the First Army really developed such a terrible weapon?
Stand by for further instructions from Command.
The Marshal will make the right decision. Until then, as soldiers of the 6th Artillery Regiment of the Second Army's 2nd Division...
We will continue to stand against the traitors outside Grypherburg.

lines.loc: Upper Deck, Flagship of the Fourth Army's main fleet 12 Jan 1102

lines.x: ...Here ends the Grand Duchess's message.
The last batch of supplies has been delivered, and what information we have on the First Army's new weapon is included in the letter.
Her Imperial Highness wishes to communicate that this is the full extent of the help that the Far North can provide to the Fourth Army.
We have fulfilled our end of the bargain. We pray that you do not forget yours, even in the current stalemate with the Second Army.
I understand. But I hope Her Imperial Highness sees the present situation clearly.
The conservatives maintain an iron grip over the Council. Backed by the First Army's research, they deny our legitimate claims, our desire to make Ursus great again.
Time is precious. We will be handing over the nation if the Fourth Army does not achieve the expected aim, and Bresk will hardly be immune if that happens.
It is not my place to respond on behalf of Her Imperial Highness, but I shall deliver your message faithfully to her.
Perhaps I could also tell you an old fable, on her behalf.
The north wind and the sun made a wager on who could get a passing traveler to remove his cloak—
Escort the honorable herald out.
Make sure she leaves the base and delivers my message to Bresk safely.
I'm afraid I have another important matter to attend to on this trip, and will not be returning to Bresk immediately.
I wish you the best of luck. For the glory of Ursus.
For the glory of Ursus.
Get lost...
Get lost!
Hah... you brought this on yourself.
You can blame your own insolence.
The young man kicks away the body of the soldier whose throat he just cut, and walks toward the depths of the command center.
The path leading from the deck is littered with bloody bodies, some of which are still twitching. None of the onlookers dare come any closer.
Anatoliy.
Footsteps. The crowd quickly disperses.
Against the crowd, a pair of boots steps through puddles of blood, stopping only at the sound of metal clanging against blade.
The soldier gazes down at the young man.
Are you done fooling around?
Then put your sword down.
As I've told you before, while you're free to punish those who anger you, showing your rage is simply showing your weakness.
It is disgraceful, Anatoliy.
But you've imprisoned me here. While I'm in pain and life has lost all meaning, you just keep me locked up here!
You would not even allow me to witness the birth of Kushkina.
It's for your own safety.
Safety? Hah, safety!
I'm in the heart of the First Army's territory under your great leadership, Marshal Buterina! Is there any place in Terra that is safer?
Yet you would not allow me to step out, not even onto the deck...
Have I become your prisoner just because I have Oripathy? Am I no longer your son, no longer a glorious soldier of Ursus?
Nothing has changed, Anatoliy. I treat you as I always have.
Then let me go! I want to go to Zelgrad. I want to patrol and watch over my city as I always have—as you promised!
Silent again. You're going back on your word, aren't you?
Get someone to clean up, Yasha. As usual.
Yes, madam.
Mother!
Yes, synochek, I promised you that Zelgrad will be yours. But not yet.
You must not leave my sight until your condition is stable. Do you understand?
No, I don't!
If you won't let me go, I'll keep killing with this sword that you gave me until there's no one left to guard me. These kozyols wouldn't dare raise a finger against me anyway—
I said, until your condition is stable. Once it is, you can go and do whatever you want to do.
You're playing word games now. Have those handsome Grypherburg bureaucrats changed how you feel about words?
I should have killed them all.
I captured that Cautus who claims to heal Oripathy.
What?
Her companions were all Infected, as the rumors say. They feel no pain and show no symptoms.
I think it is worth seeing her, even if she's a fraud.
You would show my pain and weakness to a fraud?
Of course not.
The soldier touches the blade at her chest with her finger. Trembling, the young man finally lowers his sword.
Then, the mother pulls her son into a tight embrace.
If she is truly a fraud, then neither she nor her companions will leave here alive. But if she can truly stabilize your condition, even heal it...
Then I shall embrace her, as I embrace you now.
A lowly Cautus who came from nothing will become a member of the glorious First Army. Because she helped you.
Mama...
Wipe your tears, synochek. Our guest will be here soon.
Bring her, Yasha.
The blood and gore is quickly cleaned up, and the floor once again sparkles as new.
Heavy, orderly footsteps approach, but there is discordance in the order. A lighter footstep, decidedly out of place, causes everyone to look up.
Its source soon reveals itself.
What—
Neither a middle-aged man raggedly dressed in self-styled piety, nor a well-dressed charlatan.
Just a girl with a delicate frame and eyes wide open, herded along the dark carpet like a burdenbeast.
Uh...
She's the one?
What could she possibly do? A stiff breeze could blow her over. She wouldn't even make good firewood.
Do not be deceived by appearances. She is indeed the leader of those vagrants.
My personal guard found her surrounded by adoring vagrants, as at the Grypherburg trial over two years ago.
It made our removal of her from the crowd seem shameless and preposterous, just like that trial.
You would compare her to the Yurodstvo?
Enough of that. As long as she can help you, I do not care what she is, whether she's a peasant or the Yurodstvo.
Come forward.
The girl shakes her head hesitatingly without moving her feet.
Uh...
Are my companions being taken care of?
I want to make sure of that.
You certainly have nerve.
I only hope to protect my companions.
You must recognize that you are in no position to bargain.
This is your last chance. Come forward.
The Cautus seems to recognize the situation and comes forward as instructed, but Anatoliy begins backing off hastily.
Anatoliy?
She's Infected! Why doesn't she heal herself, if she can heal the Infected?
She's a fraud, Mother. I don't want to waste time on such fruitless endeavors. I don't have time—
Take it back.
Mother?
Take it back! You must not say such things. You have time. You'll get better. You must.
The tall woman turns to the girl and peers into her eyes.
You will heal my son, as you have healed those vagrants.
If you can heal him...
I, Svetlana Ulyanova Buterina, Marshal of the First Army, vow that the First Army shall protect you and your companions for the rest of my days.
I have to assess his condition, but my presence seems to bring him discomfort?
How can I heal him if I can't even touch him?
As if a little distance would be a problem if you really had the power to heal Oripathy!
The young man turns his head, as though trying to hide the Originium crystals on his cheeks in his hair, refusing to even look at the girl, much less approach her.
The Cautus girl seems to make up her mind. She takes one look at the commander who forcibly 'invited' her here, then approaches the young man.
I take you at your word, madam...
Stay away from me, peasant!
If you take one more step towards me—

lines.st: Detest the Infected, do you?
Then you will become what you hate the most.
You trampled upon what little dignity we had left, Generalik, just because you have a marshal for a mother, never tasting the mud and blood of true battle...
You should have paid for your arrogance long ago!

lines.x: Get away! Get away from me!!
Anatoliy, put down the sword—
The Cautus does not stop. The blade grazes her neck, leaving a small wound.
The young man stumbles backward, covering his face with his hand, as though he is the one wounded.
A sudden, violent flare-up of Oripathy, or just painful memories awakened by the sight before him?
I'm not—I didn't—
...Please, calm down...
It'll be over soon.
The young man has no room to back off further. When he is about to fall, the girl reaches out and takes the taller youth in her arms.
Both of them fall to the ground. The young man's trembling hands let go of his sword; no more angry words come from his pale lips.
The pain has overcome him.
Argh—
Your condition is serious...
And you're starting to hyperventilate.
Ugh...
Follow the rhythm of my breathing, and let my words help you rediscover the feeling of full lungs.
The Cautus touches his cold, tense fingers and sees the black crystals emerging from flesh, hard and sharp as their host.
She puts her hand on the young man's forehead, her voice soft and gentle as she guides his breathing.
*exhale*
'Believe. Believe in our life.'
'Believe in our body and mind, believe in every beat of our heart, believe in every inhale and exhale.'
'Believe that we...'
'...are the source of all strength.'
*cough* *cough*!
You are just someone in pain.
I... I don't need your pity—
I don't need the pity of an Infected, of all people...!
This is not pity, only sorrow.
For I cannot cure your Oripathy.
...Fraud...
The only thing I can do...
Is soothe your pain in this life.
As the black Originium on the surface of the young man's body fades and changes, the menacing expression on his face softens.
His eyes remain closed, but his heaving chest has calmed.
Hence, we pass over to the other side.
Where there is no pain, no sorrow.
The land of eternity.
A land of eternity without suffering... The ultimate hope for the future, spoken of in ancient legends.
But nobody could have foreseen that when we gazed upon the border of the universe, we would realize asking for a future was the unreasonable part of the demand.
Dr. Doctor... The you you are now, the you who has seen the devastation plaguing this planet for yourself—
What sort of future do you still hope for?
*sigh*...
PRTS's functionality is limited, the PCS system is completely destroyed, and DWDB-221E is also lost... There are not many tools we can use left.
Did you expect things to turn out this way?
Friston, Ed, Lu...
I cherish the time we worked together. I was greatly looking forward to seeing what hopeful answers you could find.
But it is a shame. Time has shown just how futile your efforts were, how fruitless they turned out... though they are still worthy of respect.
...How I regret that things have come to this.
Allow me to borrow your legacy one last time. My plans for the future never did obtain your complete approval, but at the very least, we can still have a future.
Perhaps, in this future, we shall meet again.

lines.st: Accessing 'Celestial Fulcrum' central network...
Administrator ID:
AMa-10

lines.loc: New Rhodes Island, Operator Dormitory Early December, 1101

lines.x: It is the deep of night.
Amiya silently sits on the edge of her bed, unable to sleep.
The room is brand-new, the air exceedingly fresh.
The narrow space is laid out almost exactly the same as its original. She has no need to change any of her minute, unconscious habits that have built up over the years.
But ever since she moved in, she has not enjoyed a good night's sleep.
A faint sigh.
Amiya...
Theresa? No, I wasn't calling for you...
...Did... Did you hear me earlier?
I live in your consciousness, Amiya. There is no need for you to lie to yourself.
It is rather late. Shouldn't you be asleep?
Mon3tr and Closure, they're... They're doing the last bit of theory-testing before we bring back Dr. Kal'tsit.
There's nothing I can do to help directly, but I also can't get any rest like this... Though I did promise the Doctor I would.
But...
I am always around if you need to get things off your chest, Amiya.
I know everyone's working their hardest to bring Dr. Kal'tsit back. I need to stay strong too.
It's a strange feeling. The day the incident happened, I thought we had lost her forever.
But then Mon3tr appeared, and she told us there was still a possibility of bringing her back, a sliver of hope...
It feels just like... that first time in the ruins of Londinium... when I saw Theresa.
I still remember it clearly. What I felt at the time was certainly not joy...
I'm sorry, Theresa.
It's alright, Amiya.
We have already said our farewells to Theresa, have we not?
Right...
I'm not too sure, and I dare not believe... If we really do manage to 'bring back' Dr. Kal'tsit, will the person who returns be her?
You should know, Amiya, that Kal'tsit is different from everyone else.
Mon3tr said Kal'tsit has been through this sort of thing before.
Perhaps what we consider a miracle truly can come to pass?
But after all our time together, Dr. Kal'tsit's basically a part of my family. I can't even imagine how she could be any different from us.
Theresa, can you tell me one of your stories about you and her? From long ago.
I want to know what sort of person she is in your eyes.
I can only tell you about the memories Theresa has of Kal'tsit, Amiya. I am unqualified to tell you a story in her stead.
I do not believe that is what you want, either.
You're right. Maybe... Maybe I just want to hear Dr. Kal'tsit's voice again...
She's taken care of me for so long, and taught me so much... but when I think about it, I know very little about her.
I had so many questions I wanted to ask her and Theresa... but they were all such serious questions. I couldn't give them any more burdens to bear.
Maybe... when they thought the time was right, they would've told me of their own accord.
But the right time never came.
I understand. Theresa and Kal'tsit were both very important to you.
You do not need to hide your emotions from me, Amiya, nor should you bear everything alone. Go and tell Closure and Mon3tr, and the Doctor.
No matter how things may turn out, you should not leave behind any regrets, alright?
You're right... I'll be fine, Theresa. Once I step out of this room, I'll be back to normal.
Don't worry. No matter what comes to pass, I won't let Closure and Mon3tr see any dismay on my face.
But I cannot help but worry about you, Amiya.
You have had far less sleep than usual this past month. You must get more rest.
You should also be aware that ever since you used the Black Crown's power in Ursus, your vital signs have all been very abnormal.
Not only that, but you have been avoiding routine Rhodes Island medical checkups ever since Kal'tsit left us.
I can also tell that... some changes started even before that.
When the Doctor and I were exploring Civilight Eterna, we discovered a model from the Slumber Bridge project, and borrowed its power to fight Priestess.
I don't fully understand it yet, but I can sense that this model seems to have linked me even closer to the Black Crown.
I can use the power of the Lord of Fiends more easily, I can sense emotions more intensely. Sometimes, I can even hear voices, and I can't shut them out.
It's like... I'm back to before Dr. Kal'tsit gave me these rings.
I am detecting that the connection between you and the Black Crown is deepening at a rapid pace. This is unprecedented in the entire line of the Kings of Sarkaz.
I cannot explain its cause, but it is not something to take lightly, no matter what it may be.
You must take care, Amiya. I believe you should let the Doctor know as soon as possible.
Right... I understand.
I promise I'll pay close attention to my condition, but is it okay if we don't tell the Doctor right now?
Was that Closure's workstation?
Have they finally gotten results...?
Alright, after squashing I-don't-know how many bugs, I can finally say with certainty that there's no problems in the entire dataset.
Here goes! I'm praying this is the last simulation we have to run!
This time, it'll be a success...
Aye dun dink dere'll be enny broblems et al—
Hey, Mon3tr, don't move, or the data cables on your head will fall off!
Keep her still, Warfarin, then help me inspect the simulation life pod's cables, make sure they're all connected properly.
Alright, alright...
You seriously think I understand any of this...? Never had to deal with this sort of stuff in Medical.
Look, I had to start from scratch too when I was studying all that data from Mon3tr! Forget it, all systems green here, no need to check!
Alright, everyone ready?
Here goes—

lines.st: Biological model construction—————100%
Physiological function simulation—————100%
Neuron data upload—————98%

lines.x: One minute, two minutes... Ten minutes pass, each one an eternity longer than the last, all without any warning pop-ups or worrying flashes of red.
Cmoncmoncmoncmon—
Don't...
(Deep breath)
No, it will make it!

This is all based on reasonable assumptions and a carefully calculated foundation, and it's in accordance with that 'life-phase transition' stuff she was going on about, so even if all we can get is a glimmer...
...Even if all we can see is a glimmer of hope, I'll be happy.
The Vampire's red eyes stare at the monitor, unblinking. The fluorescence reflects off Closure's pale face as a series of pinpricks of light, the process's various readings constantly in flux.
The progress bar on the monitor stops, just as it is about to reach the end.
It's—
...Working?

lines.st: Neuron data upload—————Error
Physiological function activation—————Error
Data fitting failure.

lines.x: Failure. Again.
After so many failures, she should already have gotten used to seeing this result, yet defeat still weighs heavy on her heart.
Closure looks towards the scarlet glare, subconsciously trying to use the naked eye to pick out the true cause of the issue from the morass of data.

But what made her despair the most was the fact that she had checked over every key snippet of code countless times over. If every step was performed correctly, but still didn't result in success, then doesn't that mean...
Where's the problem this time? This shouldn't be happening—
Don't look so glum.
Nobody's done bioengineering this complicated before. We must've missed a spot somewhere.
Calm down, keep looking, and you'll definitely find it.
I know, I'm not giving up yet.
Drone No. 6, begin recording progress reports 1860 to 1864.
Project: Sarcophagus Resurrection Experiment. Progress: 0.
But why...?

Our last two attempts should've succeeded. Even if Kal'tsit severed the connection between us, there are other methods we can theoretically use to replace the gemini cycle's information transmission function.
I stored all the memories Kal'tsit encoded as energy strings inside. Every single one of the Sarcophagus's parameters is correct.
Using 'Oka', blank Originium, as the base of Kal'tsit's reconstructed body is theoretically feasible...
But where's the issue? What are we missing...?
Maybe...
The same thought floats through everyone's minds, but none of them dare say it out loud.

opts: Maybe what we're missing is...
The part that makes Kal'tsit Kal'tsit.

lines.x: Doctor? You're here!
Sorry, we couldn't—

opts: It's alright. We expected to run into difficulties.
Though this outcome is a little disappointing.

lines.x: Don't... Don't lose heart just yet, Doctor!

Rhodes Island's best engineer hasn't given up! With Terra's genius hacker on your side, making sense of the data Kal'tsit left behind is a done deal! On the honor of my spot in the Kazdel's Elite 100—
I will find a way to bring Kal'tsit back!

opts: If that's how you feel, I've got nothing to worry about.
Wasn't I meant to be the one giving the pep talk?

lines.x: I mean, you did look a little disappointed just now.
I promised Kal'tsit I wouldn't let you or Amiya handle all the pressure by yourselves anymore.

opts: Thank you, Closure.
Rhodes Island still needs Kal'tsit.
We're all hoping she can come back to us.

lines.x: Yeah!

opts: By the way, news from Ursus.
Crownslayer found more clues about the Sarcophagus.
It's time to set off again.
Maybe once we actually find it...

lines.loc: Rhodes Island Temporary Treatment Center, Odoyev Raion, Deity Grypherburg January 1102

lines.x: You see... This w-wounded joint... If you... set it like this... It won't hurt.
Spasibo, Vetochki! I'm feeling better already!
I learned... it from Rhodes... Island's d-doctors.
Speaking of, this Deity Grypherburg place sure is something, having stoves like these we can warm ourselves with. No wonder those nobles can sit pretty in the cities without caring about winter.
Can we really settle down here, Vetochki?
It's... okay. Raidian said sh-she'd protect us.
Now... we don't... need to be afraid.
Good grief, it's absolutely freezing here...
Can't you add a little more firewood—My apologies. What I meant to say is, if you are still lacking in firewood, I will be happy to help.
Is she... Imperial Guard? What're the Imperial Guard doing here?
D-Don't be scared!
She... Sh-She helped us before... Don't you remember?
Thank you, Vetochki. Thank you for speaking up for me, and thank you for remembering me.
*sigh*... And after we forged a friendship in the fires of egress, too. I think my heart's beginning to break.
You only have your conspicuous uniform to blame, 'Sergeant'.
I'm terribly sorry, but I am no lord with the time to change outfits for every single errand. I need this uniform as my free pass through other parts of Grypherburg.
It's been a while since I last dropped by to say hello. Everything still going smoothly? How are your medicine stocks?
Hmm, our other supplies are just barely enough, but you know it's nearly impossible to obtain anti-Oripathy medication in the capital, and we're too far from our headquarters to transport more here.
If it wasn't for the matter of the Originium vein, the construction of Grypherburg's Oripathy medicine production line would've been on the agenda.
Who would have thought...
Well, whatever the case, thank you for offering us this shelter.
I did make a promise. And it is simply an idle factory owned by my family. Even then, it still can't fit everyone inside... It is far too cold here.
Although the paperwork to shelter the Infected has been sorted out, now is not a good time for any of you to wander about the city.
I regret to say that... as things stand, I have no way of offering you better conditions.
I know they're only allowed to stay in Grypherburg as key witnesses to the tragedy of the Far North... even though this trial has not yet manifested itself.
This does not change the fact that there is nowhere in this nation for them.
...That may change, sooner than you think.
Sorry, did you say something?
No, nothing. Let's shelve this discussion for later. I came to Rhodes Island today for another matter.
Where is that 'Doctor' of yours right now?

lines.loc: Rhodes Island Deity Grypherburg Branch Office, Ursus

opts: Zelgrad?

lines.x: Yep. Based on your team's intelligence, we can assume Ursus is secretly researching the Sarcophagus somewhere near Grypherburg.
And according to Crownslayer's info, we've found a few clues that can validate this assumption.
Despite Ursus's critical Originium shortage, there's a delivery of vast amounts of Originium from the city to the outskirts, same time, every day. Always in the same direction.

Their Originium logistics channels are well-hidden, and it's a bad idea for us to chase them too closely. But we've checked all the satellite cities around the capital, and none of them have the sort of industry that needs this much Originium.
None except the satellite city where the First Army is stationed. Zelgrad.
But the moment any lead we have points here, it's cut off. Guess Grypherburg is putting a lot of effort into hiding the flow of energy.

opts: Nobody's mentioned this city to us during our time in Grypherburg.

lines.x: You're not the only ones in the dark. Most Ursines are barely even aware Zelgrad exists.

opts: Ursus must have a good reason to keep a secret like that.

lines.x: We can also assume that, if large quantities of Originium go missing at a time like this, there's probably industry magnates who aren't too happy about it.
What's more, the Fourth Army's pretty much at the gates. They definitely have spies watching every move happening in Grypherburg.
But that's the reason why one thing really stands out.
Zelgrad is supposed to be a closed-off special district, but it's recently been advertising itself as 'a safe haven for the Infected'.

Their public statement is that the First Army firmly denounces the tragedy that happened in the Far Northern mines, so they are willing to shelter those Infected who lost their homes during the unrest.
'As a show of the absolute kindness the tsar has for the Infected.'
Naturally, the first reaction everyone had on hearing this news was suspicion. We've been unable to get any information about any Infected who enter Zelgrad.

We've also found some issues with the records Crownslayer found in the district gates. Once you factor out the outsourced materials being used as cover, imports of pharmaceutical products and raw materials are almost nil.
None of this is concrete evidence, though. If we really want to know the truth, I'm afraid our only choice is an on-site inspection.
That's all the clues my side can offer you at the moment. We'll keep up our work at the edges of Grypherburg, and get as much information as we can into your hands.
Oh, right. Don't forget to tell the little USSG cubs what good work they've done next time you see them, Doctor.
Not just for their information-gathering skills. They were amazing during the recent crisis in Grypherburg. They're all bona-fide, grown-up Rhodes Island operators now.

opts: I will. Everyone did great.
You're all the best of Rhodes Island's operators.
Thank you, Dur-nar.
Remember to tell Zima and her crew to stay safe.

lines.x: Kal'tsit sealed away the Sarcophagus's core when she was in Chernobog. Theoretically speaking, Ursus's current technological know-how isn't enough for them to restart it.
What's stranger is, shouldn't Ursus be trying to turn it into an energy source at a time like this? Why do the opposite and consume tons of Originium? What are they actually trying to do?
Doctor, what I'm most worried about is Zelgrad accepting the Infected.
I know this isn't a rational assessment, but... I find it very hard to believe the First Army is letting them in out of the goodness of their hearts.

opts: An incredibly suspicious act.
Our top priority is gathering even more intelligence about Zelgrad.
Closure...?

lines.x: What are you doing, Closure?
Ah, sorry, just a sec, nearly done. Let's see what secrets this website is hiding.
Wait... Are you hacking into an Ursine government website?
Nonono, no hacking involved. The site I'm looking at is the 'Ursus State Council Executive Department Website'. The service-level news is for the public.
Government news, Catastrophe warnings... Ah, there it is, Zelgrad's notice saying they'll shelter Infected. Man, too many network fluctuations, filtering and download speeds are real slow.
But what's obvious is that a lot of this is just fake news to keep up with appearances.
Check this city migration schedule, for example. If this info is true, it means there's been three nomadic city collisions near Grypherburg just last month!
This sort of forgery definitely means they're hiding something. Just need to dig a little deeper...
Are you sure you're not crossing a line here, Closure?
I'm not! Well... Maybe a little?
But whoever kludged together this website clearly isn't very good at network security. The website's server is directly connected to their internal database.
Nothing too important in here, all just basic info on city routes. But Zelgrad's urban identification code is in here, as well as their public logistics and transportation records.
Okay, give me three minutes, and ZOOT will calculate the optimal route from Grypherburg to Zelgrad.
I won't leave any tracks behind, guaranteed!
But all we have is a lock on the satellite city's position. How are we meant to get in?
A direct attack? I don't have any issues with that, honestly...
If the Sarcophagus is in the hands of the First Army, that means it'll be heavily guarded. A direct attack is out of the question.
Doctor, I'm wondering if we can take advantage of Zelgrad admitting Infected—

opts: A heads-up from Raidian—
Take care. Looks like someone's here.

lines.x: Raidian... and Lieutenant Gorchekova?
I happened to run into her. She says she has something to discuss with the Doctor, face-to-face.
It's been quite a while, my friends.
Though I do not believe I have met you before, Gospozha... Vampire?
Y'know, it's been so long since anyone's mentioned it that I practically forgot I am a Vampire.

opts: Her name is Closure.
She's an amazing engineer.
She's an amazing hacker.

lines.x: It is my honor to meet you, Gospozha Closure.
It is clear that you are an excellent... Hmm...
Hmm...?
Eloysius turns to Raidian, choosing to communicate using sign language.
'Is this place safe?'
I don't detect any signals of dubious origin. Closure can also guarantee we are free to speak here.
Wha? Sorry, I don't understand sign language—
Everything here was wired by us, correct?
Yeah?
(Quietly) Does this mean nobody is monitoring us right now...?
Oh, definitely not. You don't have to worry about that sort of thing when I'm here.
Just act like you're back on the ship—err, back at HQ. You're welcome, by the way.
Spasibo. Then let us get down to brass tacks. Our last discussion ended on the topic of the Sarcophagus's whereabouts.
In regards to intelligence on the matter, I have made some... not-so-small headway.

opts: Thank you for being willing to share it with us.

lines.x: Yet another promise of mine. All part of our cooperative agreement.
Besides, even if I did not share this information with you, I'm sure you would already be trying all sorts of ways to get into Zelgrad, as is typical for you Rhodes Islanders.

opts: We will abide by the laws of Deity Grypherburg.
I assure you, we won't do anything illegal.

lines.x: Eep..!
A beep on the terminal draws Amiya's attention as the Vampire instinctively covers the screen. The young Imperial Guardswoman looks, but makes no comment.
Very well. I know full well just how difficult it is to establish a relationship built upon trust.
But I insist on recommending Rhodes Island secure a legitimate status for your operations... for there will be many bumps on the road ahead.
She's right. Rhodes Island must be well-prepared.
Are you... General Khratov?
Just Hellagur is fine.
According to the Doctor's instructions, I have attempted to contact, and succeeded in contacting a Vice Chairman of the State Council, Vasily Gorchikov.
In Grypherburg's eyes, Rhodes Island is on sound legal footing.

So it was your idea all along. I was wondering why...
Wait, how did you know he would be able to meet with the vice chairman—with Father?

opts: It's simple. Because we could.
It was Operator Hellagur who suggested it in the first place.

lines.x: It seems I have been underestimating the intelligence and contacts Rhodes Island has access to this whole time...
If that's the case, I have no more worries. Allow me to formally pass on this invitation to Rhodes Island.
An invitation from His Imperial Majesty Fyodor Vladimirovich.
This is why I have come here today. Now, allow me to escort you to the audience chamber.
You're here.
Do your clothes fit? Come closer, and let me see.
Hmm. At least they fit you better than your old clothes.
Thank you. They fit fine, and they're comfortable.
You are my guest. This is the least of what I can provide you. If there is anything else you need, please do not hesitate to ask my adjutant.
How is Anatoliy, Yasha?
The Generalik is currently choosing his retinue for the next operation.
He simply cannot wait, can he? Remind him to pick strong young recruits, no more wily old soldiers.
I already have, ma'am.
Very good.
What is your name? I cannot be calling you 'child' the entire time.
Hierda. I'm called Hierda, ma'am.
Well then, young Hierda.
As I must remain here to maintain discipline, I need you to accompany my son to Zelgrad as his 'doctor'.
He is going there to patrol, and look after the city. In turn, I hope you can look after him.

You should know that Ursus has recently run into misfortune. The unrest continues to spread unabated, and the number of people who want him dead rivals the number who want to snatch my authority away from me.
I want you to stay by his side and protect him, and once all the dust has settled, bring him back to me safe and sound.
...'Once all the dust has settled'?
You need only reply. Can you do this?
I need to know where my companions are first, and if they are safe.
How careless of me. I forgot to tell you that they have already headed onwards.
'Onwards'?
To Zelgrad. The city is now open to both the public and the Infected. Your companions are the first lucky few to be accepted by this new policy.
Once you go there, you may meet with them.
...What's this?
I'm sure I was here earlier, but he's not here.
(This ship is too large. Where am I supposed to find the young general?)
Hmm...
...drat...
Ah, someone's there.
Hello, may I ask—
...Everyone knows being one of his bodyguards is a death sentence. Who's still willing to go?
And now he's actually managed to figure out he just needs to pick some nobody greenhorns who don't know what they're getting into—
How shameless!
(Quietly) Shh, keep it down! Let's talk somewhere else, I know where we can avoid the cameras.
I had to let it all out today.
(Quietly) I get it, I get it, bratan. This is why we need to keep getting our people into his personal guard, even if it means sending them to the slaughterhouse.

(Quietly) The marshal's clearly lost her ability to judge the situation. She thinks that with the new weapon, we can sleep peacefully at night, but she doesn't know the real problem was on the inside all along.
(Quietly) Letting a useless boy play toy soldiers with the army just to earn some cheap glory, waving a live blade around like it's an emperor's scepter!
(Quietly) She even lets him randomly execute the men without penalty... It's absolutely ridiculous.
She keeps going on about how we have to do it for Ursus, but today's killing was certainly not for Ursus!

(Quietly) And if things keep going on like this, how're we supposed to deal with rebels? There was a Corporal Andrei in my barracks, all he did was follow the Marshal's orders to stop him, and he got his throat slashed open for it.
(Quietly) Andrei wasn't even part of that 'Death Squad'. I had a look at his corpse, his eyes wide open, just a kid with a confused look on his face under the mortician's sheet...
We've got to do something already!
(Quietly) You're right...
We need to act.
'Act'?
What do they mean by...?
Act?

opts: Hff... brr...
It's cold...

lines.x: Are you still cold, Doctor? I should've reminded you to bring heavier clothes.
Amiya clutches your fingertips. Her palm is cold too.
Hang in there for a while. Things will be better in Tsarevgrad.

opts: I thought this would be another solo audience.
I thought the Tsar would be more wary of us.

lines.x: On the contrary, His Imperial Majesty was very impressed by Rhodes Island's feats in the Far North. He is eager to see you.
Especially after hearing that the leader of Rhodes Island is so young.
I didn't do very much...
Now is not the time for humility. Make the most of the good first impression—it can only be a good thing for the meeting.
There are a few things about Grypherburg that I must communicate before we meet His Imperial Majesty.
First... I'm sure you're not oblivious as to why the Tsar has chosen to grant you an audience.

opts: While His Majesty is known for his benevolence—
He would not give us access to the Sarcophagus for no reason.

lines.x: You want the secrets of the Sarcophagus. So do we.

We hope that this meeting will result in mutually beneficial cooperation.
You understand the most pressing matter facing Ursus...
Or at the very least, Grypherburg.

It has been two months since the Fourth Army began pressing toward Grypherburg. Now they remain in a tense standoff against the Second Army along the eastern shore of Lake Neva, with the occasional skirmish.
They have not gone any further for now, but we can ill-afford to be optimistic.
They continue to petition the State Council, demanding full support for the war that they intend to start.

opts: Most curious.
If the Fourth Army's intention is to start a war of conquest—
They should be on the borders of Ursus, not the outskirts of Grypherburg.

lines.x: Hah... everyone knows what these traitors are planning. They continue their despicable attacks on the Council.
There was an attempt on Chairman Witte's life the day after the Fourth Army's First Division was routed. The assassin's methods bore clear associations with those of the Fourth Army.
Yet in the face of such provocation, the Royal Guard somehow failed to capture or kill the assassin.
There is also reason to believe that the assassin's accomplice, or accomplices, remain at large in the city.

opts: The Fourth Army is only the most immediate issue.
At the end of the day, Ursus must confront the reality of ore exhaustion.

lines.x: Exactly. Most see two paths before the empire, war or peace, yet neither is sufficiently convincing to everyone.
His Imperial Majesty places his hopes in the Sarcophagus, currently under the First Army's control.
A breakthrough in this direction may represent the empire's last hope for a solution, absurd as it may sound.
Even so...

opts: Research into the Sarcophagus is not going smoothly.
The Council faces issues beyond research progress.
We were not invited as scholars.
We're here at the invitation of the Council, not the First Army.

lines.x: Astute as always, Dr. Doctor.
However, I would recommend against such overt astuteness during your audience with the Tsar.
It appears that the First Army is indeed hiding something... though it's better for you to hear from His Imperial Majesty himself.

opts: What do you think of the Tsar?

lines.x: Even in a private setting like this, such a question is bound to raise suspicions.

opts: I just want to hear your thoughts.
I just want to be prepared.

lines.x: You must have heard rumors about him from various channels. It's not my place to try to change opinions. All I can do is answer truthfully.
If there is anyone in Ursus who will fight to the bitter end for her, it is His Imperial Majesty.
For he has nothing, save Ursus.
...Off-limits...
This place is off-limits! Go away!
Please, sir, I'm not Infected! The new pass—see here, the pass! We bought it, we're law-abiding citizens...
We must deliver these goods in time! The nobles won't take them otherwise, even if they're unspoiled, and we'll be ruined!
We can't afford heat anymore, and our child is sick in bed... please, have mercy and let us pass—
Tsarevgrad Raion is currently under lockdown. Not even a pass made of gold will buy you passage.
Take your things and leave. An announcement will be made once the lockdown is lifted.
Is that a roadblock?
Stay in the vehicle. I'll check it out.
Didn't you hear me? This place is off-limits—
Zdravstvuyte.
(Salutes)
What do you need, ma'am?
His Imperial Majesty wishes to meet these good people.
Tsarevgrad Raion is on lockdown. Even deliveries of necessities must be met by someone from inside.
By order of the Tsar.
You're doing your duty, I understand.
But I'm curious, what do you do when His Imperial Majesty's orders contradict themselves?
Because I'm operating by order of the Tsar myself. In fact, I have his edict right here.
The young Imperial Guard unrolls a piece of paper with a bright red seal on the bottom corner.
It is the Tsar's administrative seal.
I understand. We can wait a little while, if there is some difficulty.
I'm afraid waiting won't do any good, ma'am. The situation is unlikely to change until the culprit is caught.
Eloysius fights her urge to roll her eyes. She puts the edict back, places her hand on her sword hilt, and straightens her back.
She looks up again, her expression completely changed.
The Grypherburg Police are under the jurisdiction of the Ursus Guard. You have people inside Tsarevgrad.
All you need to do is inform your commander that His Imperial Majesty's guests have arrived. The rest is no longer your concern.
But—
'Lieutenant Eloysius Vasilyevna Gorchekova, Imperial Guard Tsar's Battalion, accepts all responsibility for carrying out His Imperial Majesty's orders and consents to all inspections.'
Pass that message to your commander.
Can you remember the whole thing?
...Yes, ma'am.
Please wait here for a moment.
One more thing.
The couple hauling the goods over there, they are with us too.
The items are meant for the Tsar. You may include them in your report.
Done.
The road's not open?
It's open, but only for us.
Let's not waste the opportunity.
Enter.
Please wait here with the guests, Lieutenant Gorchekova.
Thank you.
You look around as the servant departs.
The room's furnishing is minimalistic compared to the luxury that you saw on your way here, but its owner's position of authority is obvious.
The curtains are closed even during the day, electric lights shine brightly, documents are stacked up on a cart, and the corners of the table have been repaired with gold.

opts: The office seems to be in frequent use.
You brought us in here directly?

lines.x: How can you tell?
There are multiple rooms with identical furnishings in the Amber Palace, as a safety measure. This is just one of them.
You should not make blind guesses.
What else did you think we need?
These may be unusual times, but nothing opens doors like one's rank in Tsarevgrad, even without all the medals on my chest.
The only people allowed to access this area are the Tsar, his most trusted ministers, and people who have been granted special permission.
You should therefore be respectful. Conversation is permitted, but I would refrain from commentary, if I were you.

opts: I meant no offense.

lines.x:
I understand.
Just keep your patience, as you did last time, until His Imperial Majesty is finished...
with the things that are troubling him right now.
—Chairman?
I thought Your High Excellency was still recovering at home—
I'm here on His Imperial Majesty's behalf. He has urgent matters to attend to.
Your work here is done, lieutenant. I would meet with our guests privately.
I've spoken to your father. He is concerned about how busy you have been lately, and hopes that you come home once in a while, if you could.
Your High Excellency's concern is appreciated, Chairman Witte.
I will take my leave.
The young woman claps her heels together in a military salute, then turns and departs.
The chairman watches her leave, only turning around once the door is fully closed.

opts: Greetings, Chairman Witte.
Your reputation precedes you, Chairman Witte.

lines.x: Greetings, guests from afar. Thank you for accepting our invitation.
I see we have learned of each other, in different ways.
Please, take a seat.
There is little time for pleasantries. Let us be frank and honest with each other.
Your Imperial Majesty, it is my honor to report the progress that the First Army has made on Project Zero.
Her High Excellency the Marshal understands that you are much troubled by matters of state and the traitors' movements. I hope the news I bring will do something to soothe these troubles.
...Where is Marshal Buterina?
She remains in her domain.
She's supervising Project Zero, and she should be the one reporting to me.
Why are you here in her stead?
I apologize, Your Imperial Majesty, I should have explained.

The Marshal's son, Anatoliy, was attacked a few days ago, and remains in serious condition. Her High Excellency has no choice but to remain behind, both to punish the perpetrators, and to prevent further instability.
After all, we are not like the Fourth Army; no hint of rebellion is permitted, whether internal or external.
Why have I not been informed?
It is the Marshal's private family matter, after all.
Now, if you have no other questions, I will continue my report.
How could you speak to the Tsar like this? You insolent—
I am simply stating the facts, yet you make a serious accusation. I am fully able to take responsibility for my words. Can you say the same?
Why you—!
That will do... continue, Kapitan.
Grypherburg has already committed tremendous resources to Project Zero. If there is no material progress...
There will be consequences.
Rest assured, you will not be disappointed.
Before we begin, allow me to satisfy my curiosity.
I understand Rhodes Island came a long way to the Far North, rescuing the Infected miners there.
May I ask why?
Rhodes Island is a medical concern, and our mission is to combat Oripathy. We are committed to providing treatment for any Oripathy sufferer who needs it.
Does the Empire of Ursus feel the need to question every act of kindness towards the Infected?
You tug the corner of Amiya's skirt.
...Infected, Cautus, leader of Rhodes Island.
You are known by the mononym Amiya, correct?
Understand that I am not seeking to interrogate Rhodes Island on your aims.
Lieutenant Gorchekova thinks highly of you. She is a good soldier, and I trust that her assessment is a result of objective observation.
Let me make it clear that I am very grateful to you for your actions in the Far North, which laid the foundation for this meeting.

opts: We mean no offense, Your Excellency.
Allow me to introduce myself.
I am Dr. Doctor.
I'm Rhodes Island's medical advisor.
I'm Rhodes Island's expert on Originium.

lines.x: Medical advisor?
I take it there is more to this title than meets the eye, if you're here as a representative of Rhodes Island.
An Originium expert. Your arrival may be serendipitous for us.
Go ahead, Doctor.

opts: We know Ursus is looking for Kal'tsit.

lines.x:
'Kal'tsit'...
Indeed, perhaps we should dispense with the formalities.
You notice that Witte tapped the floor with his walking stick gently, discreetly shifting his center of gravity.
He is considering what to say.
If not for the deep-rooted corruption within the Third Bureau, this name would have been known to our secret police sooner, not recently discovered in old piles of paper.
This is a good starting point, and you've brought it up of your own accord without trying to hide it. Perhaps we can come to an agreement.

opts: Are you looking for Kal'tsit in order to open the Sarcophagus?

lines.x: Obviously, as Elotta has told you.
He takes a meaningful pause and glances at you.
Due to various circumstances, we have had to... restructure our energy planning. It is the source of the empire's present dilemma.
Research into the Sarcophagus has resumed, but things are not going well.
We need Kal'tsit and her knowledge from Chernobog to help the people survive this winter.
By studying the Sarcophagus as she did in the Chernobog lab?
I see you understand that it is the fastest way.
Now, can you tell me where Kal'tsit is?

opts: Why do you ask?
You don't believe what the lieutenant told you.

lines.x: Please understand that I ask out of an abundance of caution.
After all, we both know that Kal'tsit was 'alive and kicking', so to speak, for all those years that the secret police thought she was dead.
I hope our conversation will not stand on unnecessary deception.
I ask not because I don't trust Elotta, but because I need to make sure that Rhodes Island is in a position to assist our research into the Sarcophagus.
We all keep certain secrets, of course, but some questions must be confronted, not evaded.
Dr. Kal'tsit is... indisposed.
And if I may be frank, we also have reservations about this cooperation.
We want to know if Ursus's ongoing research into the Sarcophagus will lead to a repeat of the Chernobog tragedy.
...That concludes the report. In summary, the First Army is currently holding position in the southwest.
Several shells powered by Project Zero energy were tested several days ago at a location in the wilderness of the Central Governorate.
The destruction has already left a deep impression on the Third Army.
It is no exaggeration when I say that this weapon will completely transform the current stalemate on the northern front.
They're acting without the Tsar's permission or the State Council's! They deployed this devastating weapon without even bothering to evacuate the nearby civilians—
Nothing grows on that barren soil but weeds. It is the perfect place to test the weapon. Why get worked up over a few vagrants?
It is His Imperial Majesty's land, and those were His Imperial Majesty's people!
Do you have the details?
Right here.
The seething servant takes the report and brings it to the Tsar sitting at the end of the hall.
Fyodor flips through the pages in silence, carefully reading through their contents.
The smell of bitter almond fills the empty hall.
Your Imperial Majesty...
(Raises a hand)
Tell the Marshal that the results are quite satisfactory. However, regarding the requests made in the report—the lost data from Chernobog and further energy supplies...
Grypherburg cannot provide these at this time.
The priority for Project Zero was to obtain a stable energy supply from the Sarcophagus. This was a hurdle that the Chernobog research never overcame, and our most pressing need.
But you have chosen to prioritize the weaponization of the Sarcophagus.
This was not the outcome I wanted when I made Project Zero a national priority.
Your Imperial Majesty, the Marshal is ready to fight and triumph over the enemies of Ursus.
If you do not support Her High Excellency, you will be allowing the traitors to bash open Grypherburg's gates and plunder the empire's treasures.
Insolence! How dare you speak to His Imperial Majesty in such a manner!
Yes, Mr. Chairman, Rhodes Island is currently in possession of Dr. Kal'tsit's research and her data on the Sarcophagus...
But we need to ensure Rhodes Island's safety before any agreement.

opts: Amiya—

lines.x: You stop mid-sentence as you see Amiya wink at you, realizing that she has an idea.
Yes... it should be a fair trade.
I have devoted many years to making Ursus a more civilized nation, and it is for this vision that I have stood at the Tsar's side all these years. We share the same dream.
I assure you that I will not give up my principles for the sake of convenience, especially not when there is another choice.
I apologize. I meant no offense.
I understand. Caution is a virtue rarely seen in the young.
But I think we have gone around in circles long enough. What are your terms?
We wish to borrow the Sarcophagus.
'Borrow'?
To what extent? How? And... why?
Here is the plan for your perusal.
In short, we wish to enter the facility to ascertain the Sarcophagus's unknown function, which Dr. Kal'tsit mentions in her records.
Its what?
We're not certain it truly exists. We are, however, certain that ascertaining it will not damage the Sarcophagus.
Dr. Kal'tsit's data indicates that it may be of help to Rhodes Island in our research into the new symptoms of Oripathy, and that the Sarcophagus may be more than just a source of energy.
Policy support from Ursus will, of course, be necessary for any follow-up research.
So Rhodes Island will share with us this function that may or may not exist.
It's part of Dr. Kal'tsit's research, after all.
So...
All you seek is a solution the existence of which you aren't even sure about.
It may not be important to anyone else, but it's of paramount importance to Rhodes Island.
What if the function doesn't exist?
Our agreement still stands.
Even if you get nothing from your investment?
We're prepared.
What preparations have you made?
What kind of plan do we need to convince the government of Ursus?
I have retained all of Kal'tsit's data on the Sarcophagus, which will help Ursus restart the Sarcophagus's energy core.
Doctor, you must decide whether we hand the power to restart the Sarcophagus to Ursus again.

opts: What do you think, Amiya?
What do you think, Mon3tr?
What do you think, Closure?

lines.x: If I were the one making the decision, I wouldn't want the Sarcophagus to be controlled by any regime.
But the Ursine Originium mines are drying up, and there are many people who urgently need the Sarcophagus's energy...
And we need the Sarcophagus's miracle...
Honestly, I'm not sure.
We witnessed the tragedy at the lab. No one can guarantee it won't happen again.
But Kal'tsit decided to seal the Sarcophagus away, rather than destroy it. I think she wanted to believe that there will come a time when the people of Terra will enjoy its benefits.
Oh, you're asking me?
Well... dealing with Ursus is kind of scary. But we have to take certain risks to bring Kal'tsit back.
Maybe I can add another layer of protection for the data. First we use it to reach an agreement with the Ursine government, then we unlock it once we're sure it's the right time.

opts: The situation is urgent.
For us, and for Ursus.
We must choose cooperation over conflict wherever we can.
We must all learn to put a little bit of trust in one another.

lines.x: The data that we are offering will be unlocked in segments in a terminal we provide, fully unlocking once we leave Zelgrad safely.
Any information Rhodes Island obtains from Zelgrad will be shared with you.

I see...
