You're not exaggerating when you said you're prepared.
And it seems you already know the current location of the Sarcophagus.
I expect the location of the Sarcophagus would have been part of any deal we reach.
We simply did some homework.
Yes, you know quite a few things... which saves me the effort of explaining.
But the information you possess also represents risk factors out of my control. I would not have considered cooperating with you, if our situation was not so dire.
I have one more question for you, my guests.
This mysterious scholar, known by the mononym Kal'tsit. She came to Ursus from afar, directed research into the Sarcophagus, and sealed it away herself.
She was neither a subject of Ursus, nor our enemy... and then there is Rhodes Island, who followed in her footsteps, until the two of you sit before me today.
What exactly are you after?
Would you believe a verbal explanation?
Yes, I want to hear it in your own words.

opts: Rhodes Island's answer is not a credible one from the perspective of interests.
We hope you will listen to us from an idealistic perspective.
We hope you'll be willing to believe.
That there are people on this land who are willing to fight for justice, unbound by national borders.
That there are people in this land who want to secure the future for everyone.

lines.x: Moving words, certainly...
A servant emerges from another door. He approaches the Chairman and bends down.
Should I serve wine to our guests?
Bring last year's Taman red wine. The sunlight there was good last year.
...I see.
The name Rhodes Island came to our attention long ago. We have been watching...
Rhodes Island's deeds have earned you an opportunity for cooperation.
I will write a letter of safe passage to Zelgrad on behalf of His Imperial Majesty. It's the only thing I can do for you right now.
Thank you for your understanding.
And there's no need to hack the government servers to understand the distance between Grypherburg and Zelgrad.
Zelgrad is Ursus's pride, her 'green city', the 'city of tomorrow'. It objectively welcomes any visitors.
I hope you find what you're looking for there.
Fyodor gazes at the report in his hands, forgetting that he is not supposed to show emotion.
The reporting officer remains utterly calm, unfazed by the Tsar's silence.
Would Your Imperial Majesty like some wine?
Mm... what's available?
Taman red wine. The grapes there were of good quality last year.
I will have some, then.
Your Majesty.
I do not say this to criticize Marshal Buterina. The pursuit of strength runs in the veins of every Ursine soldier... and the results have certainly left an impression on the rebels.
Remind Marshal Buterina, however, not to forget the mission the empire has tasked her with—strength is important, but strength alone will neither feed the people nor keep them warm.
...I will continue to supply Zelgrad.
I will also be sending several academicians from the Imperial Institute of Energy Science, in order to assist you with Project Zero's energy research.
I look forward to similar progress in that area.
And why the silence? Are you not pleased by the Tsar's magnanimity?
...The First Army will not disappoint you.
Certainly.
Your Imperial Majesty.
I'm tired, Saveliy. Where is Witte? Still meeting with the guests?
His message indicates that a conclusion has been reached. Perhaps the meeting has already ended.
It's urgent. I must see him, I must...
Ugh—
Fyodor tries to stand, but feels a bout of dizziness and almost falls back upon his chair.
He waves away the servant and presses his own forehead with his hand.
It must be that insolent brute!
Their marshal brushing off the mistake of forced conscription as merely an 'abundance of caution' was one thing, but how dare a mere captain of the First Army act with such impertinence!
How long must we continue to endure, Majesty?
No...
(Softly) It's not time yet.
What was that?
The scent is dissipating, Saveliy. I can no longer smell the bitter aroma.
Ah, I'll refill it—
Never mind.
Someone was waiting outside the door... the civil representatives from Odoyev Raion, I believe? Have them come in first. And tell them to be at ease.
Perhaps you can rest first. There is heat in the corridor; they will not freeze.
I summoned them. I should not make them wait.
If I am to know their true thoughts, I must make them trust me, not just fear or worship me.
Ah, there you are.
How did the meeting go? Not too badly, judging by your faces.
You take out the letter of safe passage.

opts: We reached an agreement with the Chairman.
We have an opportunity to approach the Sarcophagus.

lines.x: I said you'd be fine, but your friends just wouldn't believe me.

Hey, you don't get to see an Ursine imperial palace every day.
I guess flying a drone here would be an act of war...
(Looks around warily)
I suppose Chairman Witte set conditions in exchange for entry into Zelgrad?

opts: We must share some information with them.
They need someone to reveal the secrets of the Sarcophagus.
Chairman Witte bears us no ill will.
Amiya played the part of a consummate diplomat.

lines.x: Doctor, I was nervous!
We got permission, we should set out soon.
Personally, I would love to come with you, but unfortunately, there are other matters that require my attention.
Just one thing... will you have enough hands at the Grypherburg Oripathy treatment center when you're away?

opts: Is anyone threatening the safety of the Infected miners?

lines.x: You promised they would be safe in Grypherburg.
They are safe, at least officially... but as I said, things are not so peaceful in the capital right now.
I'll do what I can to protect them, but you should prepare some contingencies.
I'll be here.
It would be inconvenient for me to go to Zelgrad with the Doctor. My place is here, protecting Rhodes Island's patients.

Oh...
I forgot about you. This is much more reassuring.
One final reminder.
You may have the Council's permission, but don't expect things to go smoothly in Zelgrad.

opts: We're used to it.
What's the difference?

lines.x: I just heard about this, but there has been a change in the First Army garrison at Zelgrad.
It is now commanded by Anatoliy, Marshal Buterina's only son.

opts: Is he dangerous?
Is he difficult?

lines.x: Ask about Grypherburg in high society, and the most likely answer you'll get is... 'crazy'.
If half the rumors about him are true, he's not fit to be a soldier, much less a general...
However, his mother, Marshal Buterina of the First Army, is undoubtedly an intelligent woman.
She knows Zelgrad's strategic importance. I doubt nepotism is the only reason she made this assignment, at a time like this.

opts: We'll be careful.

lines.x: I hope you find what you're looking for... and help Ursus deal with this headache.

opts: Are you calling the Sarcophagus a 'headache'?
Isn't it supposed to be 'hope'?

lines.x: Headache and hope... why not both?
Well, I shouldn't talk too much about rumors and hearsay.
Stay safe, Doctor.
I don't appreciate being snuck up on from behind.
...Sorry.
Mama wants you to babysit me, doesn't she?
But look at you, a frail and feeble Infected. Ridiculous, isn't it? I might end up having to protect you, should anything happen.
Please don't worry about me, if anything happens.
Of course I won't!
Until then, however, I'll allow you to stay.
When do we leave?
Never mind that. I have questions. Answer them.
Why is it that I don't feel any more pain, even though the rocks are still there?
It doesn't hurt anymore... it's strange.
Because all I've done is soothe the pain, to relieve the constant fear of death. People are often confused at first, doubting that it's true...
How many people have you blessed this way?
Countless.
So, everyone who seeks your help.
Everyone who suffers.
Did they all see it? That golden, endless river... am I not special?

Why did you show up, claiming that you couldn't cure Oripathy, yet you somehow soothed my pain? What exactly was it that you showed me?
Tell me—
Tell me!
The young man turns around abruptly and grabs Hierda's thin shoulders, as though he thinks he can squeeze the answer out of them.
But Hierda does not understand the reason for his excitement.
Excuse me...?
The golden, still river! The endless river that I saw when you healed me!
You saw—
I only caught a glimpse, but it was when all my pain left me. There must be some meaning to it.
Is that the land of eternity that you talked about? Can everyone go there? But if so...
What's the difference between this land of eternity and the one beneath our feet?
I'm not sure what you saw, but if it calms and frees you from pain and hatred, perhaps that is your land of eternity.
I'm glad you saw it.
...Just seeing it isn't enough.
How can we go there? Tell me!
—Generalik—
Did you find him?
Blyat, we're supposed to leave ASAP, but neither of them are anywhere to be found—
Did I hear something over there? You, check it out.
Tell me...
I think someone's looking for us.
We should go, first. I'll tell you everything you want to know on the way.
—This is what the apartment's interior looks like. Most of your companions are housed here. It's on the edge of the satellite city, but the facilities are comparable to those in the city center.
Would you like to go inside?
Of course. Thank you for leading the way...
Who's there—
Hierda?
Zaya! Is everyone here?
Those soldiers herded us into this building. We were all confused, but it turns out it has everything we need, even though it's not much to look at...
Don't worry about us!
How could I not be worried?
I was wondering where you are, whether you're cold. But it seems that things are much better than I could have imagined.
Hierda turns to the soldier who brought her here.

Please communicate my gratitude to the Marshal.
For taking care of my companions, and giving them a roof over their heads, to protect them from the wind and snow—
You should thank me.
Of course. Thank you, sir.
You don't know why you should thank me, do you?
I could not have come to visit my companions, if you had not given permission.
Hmph. True enough.
Anatoliy takes a look around, then leans in to Hierda and lowers his voice.
So they're like me.
Yes. We're all the same. In the end, we'll arrive at the same place in peaceful bliss.
The 'land of eternity'?
Yes, the land of eternity, as I told you on our way here.
'We will all return to the same peace...'
Is this gentleman one of us, Hierda?
Hierda looks up into Anatoliy's eyes.
He—
...Hmph.
Of course... he's one of us.
When can we leave, Hierda?
What?
We can't stay here forever, can we? This place has everything we need, but there are more Infected out there who need your help.
Of course, we won't stay here forever. For now, however...
Hierda looks up at the gaunt silhouette of the young man in the corridor outside. It is as though the scent of blood in the command room still lingers at the tip of her nose.
She recalls the words that she accidentally overheard on the deck, and clenches her fist as she thinks.
We're in the custody of the army right now. That Generalik will not let us go easily, and I promised his mother to take care of him during this time.
Do you mean—
(Whisper) You and Zaya will need to take care of the others, until we're able to leave safely.
(Whisper) I must keep watch over him... his impulsive nature is a danger, not just to himself, but to others as well.
I think this is the place...
I wrapped Nina in this jacket when the power was out. There must be something wrong with it, that's what made strange things grow from her—
But I had only worn it when washing the clothes of those in white coats—
No, I should have burned it, like burning things contaminated with Originium dust...
But the green spots on it are nothing like Originium dust—
There you are!
There are still two more spots for laundry workers tomorrow. Are you going? I'll put your name in if you are—
Hey, what's up with the outfit? Are you going to work at the Originium factory? But I thought it was closed.
No... I'm not going...
I can't. Nina's still at the clinic.
Oh, I see, alright then. Family comes first.
Say, you haven't gotten sick too, have you? You used to work three jobs every day, wind or rain, but you're letting a well-paying job get away now?
I have to go. Make sure you wash your clothes thoroughly after the job, or—
Or just burn it...
What—
What do you mean? Why should I burn the clothes?
She's been acting weird lately, ever since the number of Infected in the city started rising...
Well, it's not like I have the luxury of worrying about other people.
Gospodin—
Gospodin Hellagur!
Hm?

*pant* *pant*
Phew.
You were walking so fast. I caught a glimpse of your sheath back at the last corner, but you were already on the next block by the time I reached it.
The Imperial Guard's physical training is far more rigorous.
...I'm out of practice.
Did you need something?
Well, I had been looking forward to a chance to talk to you.
My work is done after seeing your colleagues off. What about you? Where are you headed?
Going back to the Oripathy treatment center before nightfall.
You do not need to be so concerned. It's unlikely that anyone would make an attempt on them in broad daylight.
Just an old man with too much time on his hands offering what help he can.
There are many children there. It seems my colleagues believe that I am... good with children.
I understand that you have the time to walk with me, then.
What?
You wrote this, didn't you?
The young woman takes out a battered book before Hellagur can react.
A breeze blows open the book cover, or what is left of it.
Eloysius presses the book cover harder, as though trying to keep it together, or perhaps it is simply a sign of nerves.
The old man sees the title of the book—
The Endless March.
I didn't think there were any left in Ursus—
(Whisper) ...I thought every copy was destroyed in the purge.
You didn't answer me directly, although your reaction alone validates my hypothesis, to an extent—
I didn't write it.
But your name is in it, yes? You were once a glorious soldier, one whose name warranted mention in the military histories of Ursus. But now—
Whatever discovery you think you've made, your time and energy are better spent elsewhere.
As I told your father, I'm not expecting the government to restore my name or status. For my part, I no longer serve the empire.
Grypherburg abides my presence only because it has no interest in a powerless ghost.
Whoever you're looking for, he's not here.
The gauntlet leaves even more marks on the book cover, before she realizes and stops the act of destruction.
Eloysius puts away the book and ponders her next words.
Then...
What if I just wanted to walk with you?
If you're not in a hurry to get to your babysitting assignment, there is a little show I would like you to see.
It will not take up too much of your time.

lines.st: I see you, Scioppa. Come, over here—
Look at you, getting yourself all wet again. What did you find?
No rush showing off your loot, little hero. Give me your hand and I'll show you how to wash it. Make sure you get all the mud and dirt out of your fingernails...
This way, father won't find out where you went and what you did.
Are you really leaving, Scioppa?
I know you wouldn't stay here forever, but parting comes sooner than I thought. It seems like only yesterday you were hardly taller than that sword you're leaving with.
I don't intend to stop you, my little foal. I just want you to be careful...
Be wary of the future of the Volniki that those people paint, and their words about the glory of Ursus—those things don't necessarily belong to us.
Be safe... take care.

lines.x: This will do.
You're already taking a huge risk by coming this far with me.
Go back. Don't make your contact wait.

lines.st: What about you? Where will you go?

lines.x: I got two good arms and two good legs, I'll go wherever I want to go. I'm a true Volnitsa now...
...Hah.
Maybe I'll leave Ursus and become a competition knight in Kazimierz.
If they still take Infected knights.

lines.st: You should not be there!
You should be on the battlefield, with me, with us—

lines.x: Don't be silly, Scioppa.
I'm Infected. This truth is firmer than any armor.
But if you want to reminisce about the past, let's end it this way. Give me your back for the last time, then go back.
Go back to your ship, to your brothers and sisters who are still healthy.
We will not meet again, not until we hear the call of Baba—of death herself.
—Wake—
He's awake!
Bring him to me.

lines.st: Where am I...?
Aurora, warship—and the hands grabbing me. It's like how Oleg kneads his dough; he always uses too much force.

lines.x: What the hell does this kozyol grow up eating? He's heavier than a grown burdenbeast!
Get him up, the Marshal wants to see him—
Blyat!

lines.st: Where were my limbs when I fainted? I could hardly feel them now, much less stand. Damn...
At least now I know that the deck of the Fourth Army's flagship doesn't feel any different from the floor of a temporary barracks when you're lying on it.

lines.x: He seems barely conscious. Did you forget I told you to take it easy with the torture?
We didn't forget, sir. All we did was waterboard him, per your instructions, in order to get him to confess to his crimes.
Did he?
No, sir...
Then I suppose I'll have to do it myself.
Pick him up.
It is unbecoming of a major to lie on the floor like this.

lines.st: Gah... what a revolting voice...

lines.x: Wait, he's twitching—he's trying to get away! Pin him down!
Keep him pinned! Don't let go!
Argh, he's strong. Good thing we confiscated all his toys.
Good, don't move, stay right there... very good.
Look up, Scioppa Razin.
Ugh...
Your High Excellency... Marshal Evgeny...
When did I offend you, sir?
You did not offend me, Major Razin. I am simply deeply disappointed in your lies and disloyalty.
But your betrayal must be dealt with, in order to give an explanation to all the loyal soldiers of the Fourth Army, who are still fighting on the front lines.
Now tell me, is it true that you and 'Sechin' have been repeatedly assisting the Infected in escaping the camp?
I never helped the Infected—
No, you didn't. You were helping your comrades who had unfortunately contracted Oripathy, weren't you?
You have no evidence.
You were careful, but even the best-laid plans have flaws. You have never tried to help an Infected soldier escape during wartime, have you?
You were too hasty. You forgot that non-Ursus soldiers stand out in camp, and how many eyes are watching you.
I know. That's why it makes perfect sense to become a deserter at a time like this.
Which is why I see no reason for you to slander them as Infected.
If you wish to capture them and put them on trial—*cough* *cough*—I would certainly do all I can to assist. It was the result of my negligence, after all.
But if you want to frame me for crimes I didn't commit...
No amount of rumor and hearsay makes evidence that would be admissible to a court martial.
All you can do is torture me until you get the answer you want to hear straight from my mouth.
And that's not happening.
Is that so...?
Then perhaps this one will be more persuasive.
...What?
...Scioppa...?
*cough* *cough*!
Impossible.
Impossible! I sent her away, I saw with my own eyes—
I'm sorry, Scioppa. I...
That will do. Cut the line.
She tried to commit suicide as soon as she was captured. It took a great deal of effort to resuscitate her.
But you let her down, didn't you?
Let go of him. He has confessed.
Now, we can talk about the price of betrayal.
Give him a jacket.
It will not do to have someone freeze to death on my ship.
Well then, thank you for your kindness...
Your High Excellency.
Enough posturing. I know what you want to say.
My men wouldn't have caught your second-in-command, if she hadn't been so loyal that she remained near the base even after she was escorted away from the front lines.
You did a clean job. But it wasn't good enough.
Did she really try to kill herself—
Oh, you want to hear more? She put a dagger through her chest. Still struggles to string together a sentence.
Apparently, it wasn't the Army's standard-issue, but custom-made for your people.
He opens his palm, and a soldier places a silver dagger upon it.
Evgeny takes a brief look at it before letting go, allowing it to hit the floor.
Scioppa's gaze is fixed upon the silver dagger on the ground.
Even in the dim light, he can distinguish the red enchantment etchings on the sheath, and the name of the owner, a little faded from age.
You—
You recognize it?
...What do you want?
Do you remember the 'bomb' that fell near the front lines of the Third and Seventh Armies?
Sechin will retrieve this for me.
The bomb's gone boom. Everyone knows that. Do you want me to bring you the shrapnel?
People like you, living on the edge of death, often fail to see imminent danger, much less the full picture of the war.
I forgive you this.
Listen. The enemy of Ursus has always been the blind and stubborn State Council, not the Second Army that is simply following orders to fight me.
I have wasted too much time on rebellions, internal conflict, infiltration, and corruption. I must bring things back on track.
As the first step, the Volnov, Sechin's flagship, will sail to the First Army's satellite city where they are developing the weapon, and take it.
Are you out of your mind?!

The Second Army's Vanguard Battalion alone could easily destroy the Volnov, and that's before talking about the automated defenses that will be triggered should we somehow manage to cross into the Central Governorate.
Why do you think I'm not prepared to 'repay' their contempt? What the State Council did in December, I will pay back tenfold, a hundredfold.
You bought the Second Army off?
Watch your words. Besides, this is not your concern.
Fine. Let's say you're 'prepared', and the Second Army won't try to stop us. What happens once we reach the satellite city? We know nothing about that thing.
All you need to do is carry out my orders. You will receive further instructions when the time comes.
That's just empty words. I need a concrete plan. I have my men to think about.
My patience is limited, Major Razin.
I am not negotiating with you. I am stating my demands, which you will accept.
You and your formation will carry out my will, even if it's a suicide mission.
The alternative is for your second-in-command and the other Infected that you sent away to, let's say, 'seek the easy way out'.
I already know where most of them are.
What is Sechin to you—

Understand, Major Razin, that I have tried to deal with your unit more civilly.
Unfortunately, it has not worked.
Perhaps you have forgotten what you promised me when the Fourth Army accepted your ragtag band of outlanders.
You swore absolute loyalty to me and the Fourth Army, in exchange for the independent status of the Special Tactics Formation Sechin.
There was to be no more wavering between Armies, no more insolence and defiance. You were to be obedient as a burdenbeast, fierce as a tuskbeast.
Which part of the promise have you kept?
Oh, you want to dig up old scores like a divorce hearing? Two can play that game.
Shall we talk about all the help we provided behind the scenes? The mutiny in December that Sechin suppressed, not to mention all the other similar dirty work...
Including the decapitation operations that no one else wants to do.
Are you saying none of them count now, Your High Excellency?
Your sarcasm falls flat.
You have committed enough dereliction of duty during the campaign to be hanged ten times along with your entire unit.
In the most recent case, the operation in the Far North should have been perfect; there should have been no survivors, but for your cowardice.
But you were unresponsive and failed to clean up in time, allowing the pests to run free. And still I tolerated your negligence.
You briefly proved you were still useful in the mutiny. The members of your unit who gave their lives died for a worthy cause, I'm sure you accepted that gladly.
You're on your third chance now, Major Razin.
I suggest you take it.
Find your spot and line up. Do not try to get into the city through the forest!
If you're caught, you will lose your place and be sent to the eastern mines!
Next.
Me! It's me—my turn!
Finally...
Next, get in line.
Infected, miners... aren't we the kind of technical talent that Zelgrad really needs?
I'd rather keep my distance from them, even though I'm Infected now too... good thing we're not in the same queue.
Stay strong! We'll find our path once we're inside.
'Zelgrad, the Tulskaya of the new era, Ursus's largest industrial base in the future.' That's what the slogans on the barrenlands trucks all say!
Zelgrad will make every precision chip in the empire, as Tulskaya once made every shell!
If we're part of the project, that means we're needed, even as Infected—
It means Marshal Buterina understands the value of our minds.
Nearly everyone is Infected.
Why are you standing in our line? You... you almost look like a noble.
Only almost.
Huh?
Are you waiting to enter Zelgrad?
Yeah, did you see that miner who just went inside? He said he was from western mines. I guess the mines there have been shut down too, like the ones in the north.
But there's another checkpoint up ahead. Whether they can actually get in is probably a matter of luck.
Zelgrad never used to accept the Infected, despite the Tsar's orders.
I was wondering too, but I have a relative in the city who said the factories were hiring, and that maybe there'll be work for me.
My only skill was fixing Originium stoves, but I thought I would check things out anyway. Didn't expect to see all the Infected here.
Or maybe it was because of that thing.
The worker looks around warily before continuing.
(Whisper) I heard that all the Originium is gone from the mines.
As far as I know, the mines in the southeast still have reserves.
Well, I don't know about that... everywhere is a mess these days, but we can't have unemployed Infected running around the place. Someone has to take them in.
What about you? Why are you here? You're not Infected, are you?
...No, I am.
If it bothers you, I could leave and join another queue.
Oh. Well, I don't think you should be here in the first place—
Mercenary?
Veteran.
Unit number?
Special unit?
By His Imperial Majesty's decree, there's no such thing as 'special'.
...But you're Kuranta, not Ursus.
Forget it. Come with me.
Why did you bring me here?
There's a special passage for nobles.
But you don't know who I am.
Veteran, lieutenant, duke, count, heir, bastard, they're all the same to me.
You're an Infected who wants to enter Zelgrad, so you'll wait here.
Someone will come and meet you once your identity is verified.
Who's talking—
Goodness, Grisha, you can't treat a noble like this!
You can deal with her then, if you know so much about dealing with nobles.
Erm, excuse me...
Sirka.
Gospozha Sirka!
Yes.
Ah, well, as Grisha said, you'll have to wait here.
So Zelgrad is really opening its doors to the Infected.
You have never heeded the Tsar's orders before. Why do so now?
Well, I'm not sure... but I bet it has something to do with the Generalik.
The 'General' of the First Army with nary a feat to his name.
So you know—
He has quite a reputation.
Well, we shouldn't be talking about him like this.
Nobody's listening.
How do you know?
My Arts. You could yell 'I'm gonna kill that marshal's idiot son' at the top of your lungs right now—
Shh—!
...And nobody would hear you.
Sirka cooperates by remaining quiet for a moment. There is no sound coming from outside the tent, not even the soldiers who should be stationed nearby.
(Shakes head)
Maybe they just haven't reacted yet.
You don't have to talk if you don't want to. But you can think of it as turning on the kitchen radio when you go home, chatting to the potted plant on the windowsill over a cup of water.
...What do you want to hear about?
Anything you're willing to talk about.
Hmm.
You could start with this Generalik.
Alright, I'll tell you about my theory.
I think Zelgrad is opening its doors to the Infected because of the Generalik.
Reason?
(Whisper) Because the Generalik got infected.
Thank you for your candor.
Maybe I just wanted someone who's not intimidated by him to know.

My brother was one of the Generalik's bodyguards. After the assassination attempt that got the Generalik infected, he and his fellow teammates were executed. Their arms and legs were severed, and they were left to bleed to death.
The person who brought the compensation said he was killed in action by a Kazimierzian mine, that they never found his body.
I wish we didn't.
You found it.
Our mother is a medic. Cleaning up bodies is her job.
You can imagine the rest.
...My condolences.
Life goes on.
May I ask where the assassination attempt occurred?
On the main street of Zelgrad in broad daylight. The assassin was killed on the spot.
Yet he came back.
Yeah, that was a surprise...
A heavy topic to discuss.
I'm sorry.
You're not the one who should apologize. Let me tell you something a little more light-hearted in exchange.
Do you know that the queues outside are a mix of Infected and non-Infected?
I would have thought that the Infected would be segregated into their own queue.
Bozhe moy! I-I must check!
Please wait here for Grisha, Gospozha Sirka—
I'm sorry.
Your identity has been confirmed, but I'm afraid you're not getting away.
Your name is on file as a deserter. We must hand you over to the Fourth Army—
...Gospozha?

lines.st: 'We cannot provide an indefinite guarantee, but we can offer a reminder.'
'The relationship between Deity Grypherburg and the Armies is like that of a hand and several pairs of gloves.'
'The First Army was made from the finest burdenbeast fur. It fits poorly because of it, and no one expects otherwise.'
'One must understand the right trick to put it on, and put up with a little inevitable pain.'

lines.loc: Forest in Zelgrad Transfer Area Jan 20, 1102, 12:08

lines.x: The transfer area... Zelgrad proper should be just ahead.
According to the map, travelers bearing official documents should take the express channel. Our document is time-limited, and we should enter the city as soon as possible.
There are several queues, but I don't see any signs about an express channel.

opts: Besides, I thought there would be someone here to meet us.

lines.x: Let's wait a little bit. Maybe—
I'll ask someone.
Mon3tr!

opts: Let her go.
She knows what she's doing.

lines.x: But what if someone thought she was an Infected and attacked her—

The troop deployments here are typical of a secret administrative region. The First Army would not permit such chaos, especially not when they've already announced that they're accepting the Infected.
However, the electrical signals in the area do make one anxious...
Should I fly a drone to check?
Got an answer!
The express channel is suspended because someone tried to sneak through a few hours ago.
The regular channel is still in use, but they're letting people through slowly.
Looks like we came at a bad time.

opts: When do we have to be inside the city?

lines.x: By 6 PM. There's some distance between the transfer area and the entrance to the city. It'll take at least four hours, even by shuttle bus.
We can't stay here for long. At this rate, the letter of safe passage may expire before we get in if we stay in the queue.
Can't we show the letter to someone who looks reasonable and have them let us in?

Ursine soldiers wouldn't make exceptions for you, even if they look reasonable.
Different methods are required to deal with them.
Doctor.

opts: What do you need from me?

lines.x: Simple. Just act important and nod at the right time.
Her mechanical arms begin moving. The motions are not particularly large, just enough for those who approach to see that she is doing something.
Then, all the soldiers' communicators begin emitting a piercing wail.
A few moments later, an officer storms towards the Rhodes Island team.
Are you the ones jamming our communications? Who are you?
Finally, someone came. I was worried there wasn't a single serious soldier in Zelgrad anymore.
We are a medical research team from Grypherburg, here in Zelgrad to inspect the confidential project on behalf of the Council. Here is the Tsar's sealed letter of safe passage.
His Imperial Majesty personally commissioned our technical advisor, who is standing beside me. How dare you treat us with such negligence!

opts: (Nod solemnly)
(Nod haughtily)

lines.x: You don't look Ursine to me...
You're leveraging accusations now? After we've been made to wait for our contact in this place?
Is this how the First Army operates? I assure you, the Tsar will hear of this.
M-My apologies, we were not notified. One moment, please—
Stay away!
Stay away from Zelgrad!
There's a long line...
It keeps getting longer. Looks like a lot of people heard the news about Zelgrad accepting the Infected.
Don't worry.
That's not what I'm worried about—
Wait, there's movement.
Hey, that guy's clothes are really strange...
Is that even a person?
The strangely dressed figure goes straight towards a procession at the end of the queue, disrupting the adjacent lines.
Countless confused gazes fall upon the same place.
Listen to me! Stay away from Zelgrad!
Strange things, dust never seen before that infects people—
Dust...?
—Blyat! Shut your mouth!
It's not safe! Stay away! Stay away!!
Leave—
You again...
Sorry, Lieutenant Grisha, I guess she slipped onto a shuttle while we weren't looking—
We'll take her away at once!
Then get on with it.
There's no time. Remember what I said—
Stay away!
Quit gawking and get back to your queues in thirty seconds, or you're going to the back of the line!
What was that about?
A lunatic. Pay no heed.
Where is she being taken?
She'll be spending the next few days in jail, if nobody bails her out.
Sounds like it's not the first time.
Is that important?
It is.
Zelgrad's reputation as the 'city of tomorrow' is even more deserved by its tolerance of such people.
The soldier says nothing, staring at Raidian as though trying to put pressure on her.
But Raidian detects unusual tremors in his electrical signals.
She smiles.
But there is certainly cause for concern.
We must enter Zelgrad to confirm whether these concerns are justified, whether things are indeed normal here.
...I must first verify your identities and the authenticity of your document.
Of course, but please be quick.
After all, it is Zelgrad's fault that our entrance into the city has been delayed.
...Thank you for waiting. Your identities and document have been verified.
Just to confirm, what is your organization and the number of visitors?
Rhodes Island Pharmaceuticals. There are five of us.
For what purpose are you visiting?
The State Council has sent us to assist with Project Zero's research.
Confirmed.
Follow me.
I said, unload everything from the cart for inspection.
I'm not going to repeat myself again, unless you're trying to smuggle something too.
Too...?
Of course not, sir. I don't mean to cause any delays, but please, hear me out—
What's that?
The regular channel for the Infected.
There's a lot of people there. Are they gonna be waiting all day out there, in the middle of winter? There's no one here at the express channel.
That's the rules.
Even the express channel was supposed to be closed until further notice.
The First Army is already making an exception for you.
Thank you for the help, sir, but what I wanted to say is...
No... stop... shut up—
—take—
—into Zelgrad!
At another entrance a short distance away, armed soldiers are shoving a diminutive Infected, shouting loudly.
The Infected does not seem intimidated. Taking a few steps back, the figure remains straight-backed.
Around the Infected are civilians from the working class, some of whom seem to be miners, while others seem to be construction workers...
Their stance is clearly protective.
Amiya?
Your document will expire, if you delay any further.
Sorry, sir, but I must—
...We've been standing in queue for three days, following the rules. Your people have already inspected the cart. Why do you have to do it again?
For what? Are we not allowed to bring the last bit of possessions we have into Zelgrad?
I told you, Zelgrad will have all the necessities for you! No one gets to bring so much stuff inside!
You can't just take the very last things we own.
Gah, you stupid little—
Excuse me...
The back of the line's that way!
I came from the express channel.
The soldier takes a look at the express passage. A few people are standing there, all looking in his direction.
He looks away from the officer standing there and back at the girl, this time with a questioning gaze.
(Mutters) I thought the express channel was closed today. Who could have gotten it opened up...?
Can you tell me what you're arguing about?
They want to confiscate our supplies. Won't allow us to enter Zelgrad if we refuse.
It's the rules!
May I ask what's in the cart?
Just some wheat and flour that we painstakingly saved from working in the mines.
The youth pulls open the cloth on the cart and shows Amiya the contents.
(It's just some food, and I sense no hostility from them.)
(But the shape of these bags... are there other things in them?)
Amiya looks at the youth curiously, and meets the gaze straight-on.
I'll vouch for these people. Here's my pass.
I don't know what 'special rules' there are to enter Zelgrad, but all they have is wheat. It's harmless, hardly worth anything.
They've suffered a lot coming all this way from the mines. Surely letting them have a few more good meals won't do any harm?
...Ugh.
Fine. One last check, and you can go.
Of course, but please be careful not to rip the bags.
What a bother... fine, fine, take your stuff and go through. Stop holding the line up, and don't let me see you get into trouble!
Thank you, sir.
And thank you too, devushka. I didn't ask your name—
No need to thank me!
By the time the calm youth looks up, the Cautus has already turned around to her own companions. What's lingered is but a distant silhouette.
The line begins to move again.
'You will see the city of Zelgrad once we pass through the tunnel.'
'Tall buildings rise out of the green vegetation that surrounds the city, balancing nature and future perfectly.'
'Here, anyone who is willing to work can earn respect and a beautiful life with their own two hands.'
'The city of opportunity, the city of tomorrow.'

lines.st: '...Welcome home, new citizens of Zelgrad.'

lines.x: Uchitel! What's that behind those houses?
Some sort of hill-like terrain... or wall?
The whole batch is here?
Good. All of you, follow me.
Where are you taking us? The slogans said we were going to use our own two hands to—
Earn a beautiful life, yes, but first you need a roof over your head. You will then be assigned to nearby factories or industrial districts.
The city will provide appropriate accommodations for those who meet certain standards.
Really? I've never heard anything like it...
This policy is unique to Zelgrad. We provide standardized housing for lawful residents at low prices, maximizing the efficiency of workers' everyday lives, work, and entertainment.
This way, people who come here will never leave again, but take root and remain for generations to come.
Previously, such benefits were reserved for the most industrious or creative laborers, but now it's being expanded to anyone who passes the assessments, including the Infected.
No wonder there's been so little news coming from inside Zelgrad.
There are many rumors out there. You can see for yourself whether they're true or not.
And then you'll find out that those slogans were not exaggerated at all.
Another bunch of Infected.
They're accelerating the process.
At the very least, the descriptions about housing were not exaggerated.
An empty carton of cystymilk on the floor, pots and pans lying around the place, plants that are still green, the greying carpet on the wooden floor...
All signs that someone had lived here recently.
Wow...
(It's better than my lodgings when I was a tutor in Chernobog!)
(Whisper) There are at least eight to ten households in every apartment.
(Whisper) It's a serious fire hazard.
These are family apartments with two bedrooms and a larger kitchen. The family that lived here left a lot of things when they moved out to the new district on the east end.
They've already gotten new things, so you can continue using the ones that are here.
What about single people?
Most of the vacancies are family quarters. You can have several people share a single unit. Just register on the ground floor.
There should be enough room here for this entire batch.
Is everyone living in here Infected? Are the people who came here previously here too?
Yes, all Infected. Not sure about the second question. A lot of people come in, and we can't put everyone in the same place.
If there are no more questions, figure out how you want to split the rooms quickly, and I'll take you to the ground floor to get your paperwork done.
There's no need, we can do it ourselves—
Nika.
Huh?
Say no more.
(Whisper) Why did you stop me? Now we've got a tail we can't shake.
(Whisper) Look at the tables. They're speckless, like someone cleaned them carefully.
(Whisper) Yet the way stuff's laid out around the room gives the impression that the previous resident wasn't concerned about these details.
(Whisper) It doesn't make sense, even if the previous residents just moved out. What kind of marks would need special cleaning?
(Whisper) Something's not right here. We need to get her to lower her guard, so that we can try to make contact with Pavel's group.
It's so strange...
Is something the matter?
No, ma'am. We're just discussing who should get this unit.
There's just one bedroom here. I say we give it to Galina.
Her kid died on the way here. She's devastated and can hardly work. She'll need someone to look after her, which makes two people...

The diminutive leader of the group walks forward, thinking about how to get the soldier off their tails. Suddenly, the bedroom door is thrown open, almost hitting the youth, who only avoids it by instinctively leaping back.
A figure emerges from inside, swinging a chair at the intruder.
Oh...
I knew it was too good to be true!
Red, help me—
What are you doing?!
Wait, don't fight back...
You...
Who are you?
Tonya Alliluyeva.
Alliluyeva!
Oh—yes.
I'm here...
Who do you think you're putting on a show for? You're not being abused by anyone.
Inciting panic, dereliction of duty, obstruction of public officials, illegal gathering... any one of the charges is enough to lock you away for weeks, if not months.
Then why are you calling my name?
...You're lucky. Someone's bailing you out. Again.
But you have sixty hours of forest labor service that must be completed in five days, or you'll be locked up again without bail.
Do you understand? Nod if you do.
(Nods)
And stop claiming to be Reunion. It's not like you have anything to do with them, do you?
Alright, you can go.
(Searchlights... patrols are more frequent than during the day.)
(I can't stay above ground. I need to think of something...)
'To what lengths will I go to go back, back to that ship?'
The impassive woman silently eliminates possibilities from her mind. A lone deserter matters little to the Fourth Army; at best, she is a bargaining chip, or a tiny favor.
The question is, do they care about what the Fourth Army does? The First Army does not necessarily have to intervene in this war, as the history of Ursus has demonstrated time and again.
The new weapon is merely a symbol, a deterrence. Evgeny undoubtedly has designs on it. The Generalik... the Generalik is a massive weakness, but how to use it?
The fugitive evades the searchlights expertly as she ponders how to continue to remain undetected while causing just the right amount of chaos...
And how to go home.
...No, I'm really at my limit.
I'm going back...
The foundation structure separates the underground residential layer into several zones. Shouting can be heard coming from behind a half-closed metal door, warm light seeping from the cracks.
The duo tangling by the door are oblivious to the eyes gazing upon them.
That's what you said the last time. You said you had too much when your tongue hardly even touched the booze. Total nonsense!
Come on, have some more, you won't get a chance once you're reassigned to behind that wall—
Excuse me.
Oh, okay.
Hey, what's a noble doing here...?
I got to go. I've got a shift coming up.
Hey!

lines.loc: City of Zelgrad, Underground Pub Jan 20, 1102, 21:13

lines.x: The establishment is unsurprisingly filled to the brim.
Soldier and craftsman, farmer and teacher—whatever they were during the day, they are all just drunkards now.
They pack themselves in this noisy space, gulping down the same cheap liquor, and drag themselves back to their quarters before they pass out.
There are countless corners in Zelgrad like this one, as there were in the Fourth Army's base.
No one looks up at her. There are no waiters, only a sleepy owner, barrels piled up by the wall in the narrow passage, and drinking games that do not require any props.
Sirka slips through between the wooden tables to the far end of the pub, where she finds the disguised figure that has fully blended in with the crowd.
Yevsey Lukic.
Huh? You talking to me?
The woman lifts the edge of her jacket, revealing a nameplate with the Fourth Army's serial etched upon it.
She keeps her eyes firmly fixed upon him, making sure not to miss the slightest change in expression.
(Hushed) Lieutenant...?
Ugh...
(Looks around)
Come with me.
I wasn't expecting a Kuranta...
I'll be sure to report your displeasure along with your negligence, Sergeant. You have not sent back intelligence about the First Army's new weapon in a timely manner.
Otherwise, the Fourth Army would already have taken action, Sirka thinks as she follows the man's lead in stopping.
...N-No, there's no need.
I was expecting someone to come, so I didn't... just didn't expect it would be a Kuranta, not like the previous contacts. Which battalion are you with?
I'm not here for small talk.
What are you here for, then? My recent reports are all in the safehouse. But I'm busy right now.
He points to the pub behind him.
You're running an underground pub, a classic hub of information. But are you really leveraging it?
I've never had a slip-up in four years. I was even awarded the Vladimir Medal. How could you—
A second lieutenant still outranks you. I suggest you think before speaking.
What do you want to know?
All Code Red intel since your last report.
Verbally.
Here? Have you no concept of secrecy—

lines.st: Sirka

lines.x: In the blink of an eye, the man feels as though he has been separated from the space beneath his feet. The sounds of the rowdy drinkers grow distant, and the sound of water dripping from the pipes disappears.
A wall of air separates him and the Kuranta. He tries to speak but can not hear himself, nor can he tell what words his counterpart's mouth is making.
The sensation of suffocation fills his brain. He frantically grabs at his throat, unsure if what he is going through is real.

lines.st: Sirka

lines.x: *cough* *cough*!
I hope I don't have to repeat myself, Sergeant Lukic.
Let's begin.
...*cough*... hah.
I've heard of your Arts. Parlor tricks that war casters have long abandoned, good for nothing except to create a soundless environment.
So they sent a lieutenant from that famous Special Tactics Formation under that poor worm Razin... he taught you this trick, didn't he?
Fine, fine, I'll tell you. I guess we're on the same side, until the next time you people change sides.
I suggest you calm down. I was simply demonstrating the secrecy of this space.
Could have fooled me, suka, you people kill comrades like slaughtering burdenbeasts. You think I didn't hear about that mutiny in December?
You killed everyone, no prisoners taken, no questioning, no survivors! You drenched a whole battleship in blood. Not even the snow could cover up the smell.
Yes, that was where I contracted Oripathy.
...Huh?
I contracted Oripathy while suppressing the mutiny. This is my last chance to demonstrate my loyalty to the Marshal, infiltrating Zelgrad as an Infected...
You know what this means, and why it must be me, and only me.
Suppressing mutiny, Infected, lieutenant... hahaha!
I see, I see.
It all makes sense now. The Marshal has always seen you people as a tool, after all. Much better to lose an Infected who was scheduled for exile to begin with, than to lose an entire fleet—
What did you say?
Oh, nothing important.
Very well, I'll help you. I take it you'll be going back to the apartments since you entered the city as an Infected. What do you need to know the most?
The First Army's deployment in Zelgrad, the location of their marshal, and all the intel you have on the new weapon.
You want to go after Svetlana Ulyanova? Do yourself a favor and just end your own life. Less painful that way.
Then tell me about the troop deployments and the new weapon.
Listen, the most I can give you right now is the recent security arrangements in the city. You're not my contact, and thus not authorized to access Code Red intel.
Patrols are conducted in shifts, but the Generalik could show up amongst the patrols at any time. I've done my best to summarize the patterns of his appearance.
The spoiled brat always brings his retinue along. Driver, nanny, bodyguards, he's never alone.
I managed to get his house servants to reveal that, while he often operates on a whim, he usually shows up a couple of hours before the night shift change.
I had to dispose of those people, but the intel should be good. It'll be convenient if you could validate it—
That will do.
What?
Ngh—?!
The silver blade cuts his throat before he even sees it.
Then, the same knife impales his chest, and finally his axilla.
Swift and clean.
That was what I wanted to know. Thank you, Yevsey.
Or perhaps you prefer to be known as Prokhor? I wasn't all that optimistic about finding you after so much time has passed.
Ugh... uh—
But you remained true to your duty. Good.
The man twitches in his own blood, but nobody can hear him.
Sirka digs through his bloody pockets, removing everything she found, disguising it simply as a robbery-murder.
Proshchay, Gospodin Prokhor.
On behalf of Marshal Kuznetsov, I thank you for your service.
(Whisper) I promise you will share the credit for the assassination of the Generalik.
...'Regional autonomy' means the clear autonomy of governance that the constitution bestows upon administrative regions. Is that so hard to understand? Are you deaf or stupid?
Hmph, and who's going to be doing the governing? Who's going to give them the money to govern? And who's going to be responsible for the results of their governance?
You're just doing something pointless the most roundabout and overblown way possible!
This is taking power from the Armies! Do you know what checks and balances are? Did you even go to public school? I'm guessing not, judging by the rags you wear.
And what if I didn't? While you were learning how to lick noble boots, me and my family were making tents for soldiers fighting on the borders!
The Imperial Guard leads Hellagur through the arguing crowd, who fail to notice their presence.
Hellagur listens quietly, as his expression gradually grows more bemused.
I thought this was the council hall...
Indeed it is.
They don't look like the old councilors who used to sit here. Is this the reason the State Council was suspended for so long?
And they said you weren't a politician.
It was the Vice Chairman who said it. I suppose he still sees his old mentor through rose-tinted glasses—the perfect soldier who should be above such petty matters.
Why did you bring me here?
You already heard the opening. Why not sit down with me and continue listening?
It won't take too long. They're always arguing about the same things.
...I got no idea what you're babbling about. If His Imperial Majesty called us here to listen to you talk, we might as well keep listening to the council's debate!
At least those rubber-stampers are more pleasant to listen to than you and I—
His Imperial Majesty didn't call the citizen's forum so that louts like you could shamelessly demand money and land!
His Imperial Majesty called the citizen's forum to listen to our voices. The factories aren't running anymore, so you bet I want money and land!
We could farm and make little crafts so that we wouldn't be out of work, and Zheleznaya wouldn't become the next Katorga! Everyone's happy.
You say 'we', but it's all about yourself! Is that the kind of labor representative that Zheleznaya Raion has chosen?
I have nothing more to say to you.
I was elected by our folks, one vote at a time. Who do you think YOU are, svolotsch—
They're about to start fighting.
Nah, we're not on the streets.
Oh.
Let me see—
Folks.
We're still in the public opinion gathering stage. It's normal to have differences, which we should settle by sitting down and talking like civilized people.
We may not be nobles, but we should have dignity as representatives, even if it's only a temporary role.
We can't have the real councilors laughing at us, can we?
Hmph.
Gospodin Svetozar! I thought you would never speak up.
There's something I want to get a second opinion on before I submit my brief. I would very much love to have your feedback...
Hm.
What do you think?
Your father was right. I'm no politician.
But you saw through what's going on, at least part of it.
Your expression never changed while those two were arguing, even as they looked like they were about to start a fight.
But something changed when you saw that third 'councilor' approach. Why?
He seemed different from the others.
I'm guessing it's because he's a real noble.
You're guessing?
Guessing is all we can do, until we have evidence.
You said I saw through part of it.
Ah, yes.
The part you didn't catch is that the two people who were arguing were not the 'citizen representatives' that the Tsar wanted to see.
I say this not because there were too few expletives, or because they were using terms and concepts they should not be familiar with.
I say this because their appeals are too organized, too specific.
Someone is pulling the strings behind the scenes. And if this citizen's forum which His Imperial Majesty personally announced and is personally overseeing could be tampered with...
This will likely end up as yet another failed reform.
...Let me ask again.
Why did you bring me here?
I simply invited you to see a show. This is the opener. Miss the opener of a show, and it will affect your perception of everything thereafter.
I wish you would be cognizant of the thought I am showing.
But I won't force you to come back to us, even though there are many ways for me to do so.
You want to show that you're different from other Ursines.
Quite the contrary, I think I'm no different from the vast majority of Ursines.
We just want tomorrow to come, for ourselves and for our people, but even this is rapidly becoming a luxury.
This is why I need every bit of help I can get. Your abilities and your past will be of great help to my plan, but if you're unwilling, then I suppose I must seek other venues.
Your plan...
I'll tell you when the time is right.
Speaking of time, it seems we've kept the children waiting long enough. Let me escort you to Odoyev Raion.
This is your last warning, Tonya.
You'll be dealt with harshly, if you're caught spreading rumors and inciting panic again. You'd better stay on the straight and narrow!
Doing it by day doesn't work. I'll have to...
Are you alright, Tonya?
Mark? Were you waiting for me?
We all saw the way the soldier grabbed you downstairs. Did they throw you in jail again?
You shouldn't do this... think of your family.
All those things you keep talking about every day, there's no proof at all.
Yeah. More importantly, are you hurt? I just came back from the clinic. We'll have to go back if you're injured.
I'm fine. Were you at the clinic, Mark? What did Nadezhda say? Is my sister getting better?
Her condition's holding stable right now. No need to be too worried.
It was my fault for bringing back the work jacket to wash at home. How could I—
Let the government folks worry about any strange illnesses. We just take care of ourselves.
We'll have a barbecue and celebrate once your sister gets better!
Great! I just made sausages!
Finally! I haven't had them in ages. I started to miss them my second day here—
But I haven't found Kirill yet...
See? This is all good stuff. I just cut a couple, and my hands are already all greasy.
They'll taste so good cooked in soup. My mouth's already watering...
Guys! I haven't seen Kirill for days, and no one answers when I knock on his door. None of you have seen him either, have you?
This is no joke! This is no time to relax.
...Didn't we already tell you, Tonya?
You're pushing yourself too hard.
I—
Did you forget that Kirill just lost his wife and kid? I guess staying in this place brings back bad memories.
Maybe he left Zelgrad and went home.
It's unusual that he didn't say goodbye to us, but you can't just assume he's missing, or that it has anything to do with your sister's illness...
Surely the police will come if something's not right.
Are we just going to pretend that nothing's happening? You saw the strange spots and bruises on Nina—
And that's all there is, a little bit of rash. Happens all the time in this environment and weather. A little bit of rest is all it takes.
You said it's the clothes of those white coats, but I've been washing the same clothes, and there's nothing wrong with me.
With a smile, he puts a hand on Tonya's shoulder. Faint green spots are visible underneath the tiny hairs.
Tonya jumps, causing the others to look at each other in confusion as she struggles to explain her actions.
...Tonya?
Well, she's under a lot of stress.
Look, Tonya, I know you have our best interests in your hearts, but it's best if you don't talk about those strange things anymore.
We're so happy here. Living in Zelgrad is like springtime compared to life elsewhere in Ursus. We should cherish it.
We'll go and see Nina tomorrow, then pick up the other kids from school. Have a good meal, drink to your heart's content, and forget all those things, alright?
That's right, Tonya.
Things will get better.
Night falls, and a stiff silence comes upon the city.
A dark shadow vaults over the wall, arriving at an abandoned warehouse, avoiding the things scattered on the ground on tiptoes.
...Good, the stuff's all here.
I can't wait. Tomorrow has to be the day—
The day for what?
—Who's there?!
...Who are you... ugh—
Quiet, unless you want your arm broken.
W-Who are you? What do you know?
Y-You're interfering with the Reunion! My comrades will have your head!
Enough bluffing. I've been following you, and I can tell that you and your 'comrades' have nothing to do with the Reunion.
Five bottles of flammable liquid, a bundle of Originium explosives... the Reunion isn't dumb enough to attack a gate guarded by the First Army with just this.
...I didn't think it would defeat them. But what they're doing behind those walls must have something to do with the strange events that have been happening lately.
So you want to blow a hole in the wall, set a fire, get people's attention.
You think the things the Army's hiding in the labs will come to light if you make enough of a commotion.
But these cans and bottles are all the preparation you've made...
You haven't even investigated what that wall's made of.
A wall is a wall! Stone or steel, what else could it be? If it could be made, it could be destroyed.
You think you can set the explosives under the patrols' noses, when I managed to pin you to the ground by myself?
I practiced! I'm prepared!
Did you practice on location? You think you can deploy and detonate it at a range that they won't find out?
You don't understand! You never saw—you don't know that all of Zelgrad is now in danger from some unknown source. I need to get people's attention, even if—
You still don't understand?
You're facing the First Army. Fighting them by yourself is futile.
Your 'comrades' are just ordinary people whose eyes aren't open yet. No one is truly on your side.
Besides, how can you be sure that the incidents have something to do with the experiments behind the wall? You know the experiments exist, but you have no inkling about the details...
How do you intend to explain to the people once you've gotten their attention?
...At least, I have to make them look up...
You want them to look. How about we look at the present? Forget your neighbors. Do your closest family fully believe what you're saying?
Will you come and pick me up today, Tonya?
I don't want to stay at Uncle Mark's house anymore. It's not our home, and I don't want to bother them...
...I'll take you out to picnic once spring comes and Nina has gotten better, alright?
Has Nina gotten better? You've been so busy, we hardly see you other than bedtime.
It's like you're not around even when you're at home. We have to call your name several times to get you to answer. You're not at the table or in bed—
You don't hug us any more. Why?
What are you doing, Tonya...
But what else can I do? I...
I tried everything I could think of. Nina's still in the clinic. That strange bruising might have spread already. I don't even dare go and see her—
What can I do...
Calmed down a little?
You... you sound like you know Reunion well.
That's not important.
You want to know what you can do? There's always one thing, and only one thing—
Find more evidence.
More evidence...
You need more evidence to prove that your sister's condition is not an isolated incident, and that it could affect everyone.
Convince them that this is a matter of life and death to them. Only then would they listen to you.
Let go, Valiya.
(Whisper) There's a soldier with them.
Thank you...
What—
Oh, I forgot, somebody has moved into the second floor.
Follow me.
Did you also arrive in Zelgrad today?
We—
That's enough chit-chat.
You'll be working in the same district, there's plenty of time for you to talk then. Let's go.
Who's coming with me to registration?
Excuse me, I have a question... if there are other people on the second floor, while the first floor is the security room and public spaces, where do the rest of us stay?
There are three of us who are not yet housed.
Can't you squeeze in? Or I could take them to another building.
But maybe there'll be room here in a few days...
(In a few days...?)
What's your plan?
The youth exchanges a glance with the miner and shakes head at the soldier.
We'll find a way to squeeze in.
'Has it lathered up yet?'
'The blade's still hot.'
Excuse me... excuse me.
Sorry, those guys were a pain! Team A should be all present now.
Captain Pavel!
The man gives the miner at the front a crooked salute.
(Nods)
Good work, lads.

We had been operating according to the original plan, but we realized we had lost contact with your group after we found a good gathering spot. If you didn't find a way to reestablish communication...
Good thing we had the contingency. What's the current situation here?

This location is temporary. The residential layer is connected to the apartments and some districts. Land is at a premium in the satellite city, and this place isn't likely to remain abandoned for long based on the frequency of patrols.
We can't stay too long. I have an idea what you're trying to do and I support you, but you should explain it to the others. We'll get this done quickly.
Alright.
Everybody, listen up.
Our primary objective is to ascertain what's going on here, then try to find the Infected who came before us but seem to have gone off the grid.
Something's clearly off about this place. There is surveillance everywhere. Things are even harder than the last time we entered a nomadic city.
We still need a few more days to plot the patrol routes, but we already understand that the Infected in the satellite city are separately housed.
That's the question that I want to discuss—we've passed through many towns and villages, but never before have we seen soldiers patrolling the streets and residences with such frequency.
There were more guards around our apartments than there were on the streets along the way. That alone is suspicious enough.
Right, that's why I decided to test them while there was still daylight.
This is your last warning! Not one step further!

Sorry, sir, I didn't mean to—
we just did a head count, and some people were missing. We were concerned that they might get into trouble wandering around the city.
You can't go through here! Give me their names and descriptions, and the Army will find them.
Wait... I think that's—
Karl! Is that you, Karl?
The soldier instinctively looks in the direction in which the youth is calling. The seemingly frail figure quickly slips underneath his arm and gets through.
Blyat! I need backup! Get that one!
More shouting and the rattling of boots, and the youth is quickly surrounded by a circle of black military uniforms.
Several hands reach out to grab those thin arms, but none of the soldiers pull their weapons, despite their fierce expressions.
That's dangerous! You should tell us before taking such risks.
Thank you, but the reason I dared to try was that I noticed that the soldiers weren't equipped with lethal weapons.
And I was right. They seem unwilling to harm me for some reason.
You mean they want to keep an eye on us, but not hurt us?
Sounds like a glorified prison.
Worse. We have soldiers instead of prison guards, and we know nothing about what the Army's intentions are.
Perhaps this intention is the reason why they've suddenly opened their doors to the Infected.
Uh—
...I've been talking to the local Infected all afternoon.
They said most of the Infected are under the care of the Army and housed in designated apartments.
Prior to that, however, they were sent to a local clinic, where the doctors don't care whether you're Infected, and accept the factory scrips that only circulate in the industrial districts.
You mean those paper-thin metal plates that are only seen in this place?
Yes, some of us who came in earlier got it yesterday. Strangely enough, wages here are issued daily...
Anyway, after Zelgrad's recent Infected policies were introduced, everyone assumes that clinic is working with the Army.
Maybe collecting data for them for Oripathy research? If the Army's really holding us like prisoners, then this so-called clinic...
...I see. Good work.
The clinic sounds suspicious. We should investigate.
Go back and prepare, wait for my word. Be discreet when moving weapons.
Alright!

opts: Have you finished your checks?
We'll talk once the room is secure.

lines.x: No problems. The room's clean, no surveillance or recording equipment.
I put jammers by the wall, just in case. It's one-time, but it'll be useful until they find out.
The soldiers said the Marshal of the First Army is treating Rhodes Island like VIPs, arranging the best accommodations and heavy security...
In other words, we're being watched.
So the soldiers outside the hotel...

opts: Probably here to keep an eye on us.
They must be hiding something.

lines.x: Yeah, everything feels so eerie here.
Like that woman who stopped us at the transfer area earlier today!

opts: She was talking about 'dust never seen before that infects people'.
But there are already a lot of Infected living here.

lines.x: Unless... she wasn't talking about Originium dust or Oripathy.
If there's another illness that we're not aware of...
Could it be a new symptom of Oripathy? I remember that Raidian raised a hypothesis in her report about why news of Infected mutation first spread from the Far North.
Even though we know now that it was likely a ruse by the Grand Duchess, wouldn't those involved have come to the conclusion of Oripathy mutations too?
As was the case the last time, we can't jump to a conclusion until we learn more.
I tried asking questions during the day, but the locals don't want to talk.
Or rather, they're quite happy to talk, but as soon as you ask whether there has been anything unusual going on, they either ignore the question, or fall silent altogether.
The officer who led the way was the same. He reminded me not to have too much contact with the locals.
Was it for our own safety, or something else?

opts: Remember the buildings hidden behind the wall?
What the Army is trying to hide is probably in the buildings behind the wall.

lines.x: The locals don't know what's behind the wall either. It's like an entirely different city to them.
It's strange. It seems like the First Army's research doesn't rely on the Infected here for labor—why do they do this, then?
The open areas of Zelgrad are no different from the average nomadic city. The First Army's research institute must lie behind the wall.
Based on the officer's reaction, the letter of safe passage from Chairman Witte isn't enough to get us through that wall.
And we've heard nothing from the Marshal who was supposed to welcome us.

opts: Grypherburg has no reason to deceive us.
Grypherburg doesn't control the First Army.
Did you notice?
Zelgrad is particularly warm.
It's like spring.

lines.x: Is that so? I didn't quite feel it.
I noticed too... this sort of weather is not normal.
Doctor, do you remember about the mysterious new bomb that Hellagur mentioned?
It might have something to do with the Sarcophagus... we need more information, and quickly.
We've got just the right woman for the job—you up for it, Raidian?
Yes, I should be able to intercept some of the communications.
The code the USSG obtained which Dur-nar sent us is used by large military installations. These facilities often send electrical signals at a specific frequency.
What do you think, Doctor?

opts: Try it, Raidian.
Be careful.

lines.x: Here we go—
The crack of static electricity echoes through the empty room.
Everyone present has seen Raidian's Arts many times, but they cannot help but hold their breath, watching her furrowed brows and twitching lips.
(Whisper) Raidian, are you really gonna be okay?
(Whisper) Trust her, she's master—
Ugh—argh!
Raidian barely took a step before stumbling and falling.
Raidian—
Overload! I brought emergency meds. Hang in there, Raidian!
Ugh...
Electric-magnetic radiation... here...
Raidian!
The night is deathly silent, except for the echoing of orderly footsteps in the distance, magnified by the emptiness.
There was food and clean water in the break room by the sentry post prior to the shift change in the patrols in this district, a perk that other units do not enjoy.

Ever since the Generalik returned to Zelgrad, they occasionally got off an hour or two early, and extra supplies began appearing in the break room, which they were even allowed to bring home to their families.
No one knew why. No one asked, because why would they mess with a good thing while it lasts?
Nor did anyone suspect that the foodstuff had been tampered with. Tonight, someone has made sure that they would not leave the break room for a while after their usual little feast.
(Their replacements should appear in four minutes, based on the patrol routes.)
(Even if Anatoliy doesn't show up personally, his bodyguards should be here to 'act in his capacity'.)
Mmph—mmph!
Have you thought it over? You can talk if you have, or you can join your comrades on the floor.
(Nods frantically)

lines.st: Sirka

lines.x: Hff... ha—
Was it the Generalik's unit who replaced you today?
I-I've never seen them, I don't know—
(Raises hand)
We don't know who takes over the shifts! We get notified to stop at the sentry post, and that someone will take over the next shift, but no one tells us who's taking over.
Although, it will certainly make sense if it was the Generalik...
What if it isn't?
Then there should be another unit on patrol, but everyone's schedule is packed, and no one can be in two places at the same time.
Unless there's a unit that's not on the shift schedule—the Generalik's bodyguards.
What do you mean?
It could only be his bodyguards. If he doesn't show up personally, his bodyguards would be patrolling on his behalf.
(Quietly) He's here.
...How's the fuel?
As you commanded.
Is there enough?
There have not been any reports about shortages.
Keep an eye on them. Our people need to be involved in every step. There must be no mistake...
You should understand.
The source of the young voice appears in Sirka's field of vision.
She has never seen the Generalik before, but she is certain that she has found him.
The tyrant of Zelgrad, the only son of the First Army's marshal...
(Softly) Anatoliy Svetlanov Buterin.
Gazing upon the malicious visage illuminated by the flickering searchlight, so reminiscent of the Marshal's younger days, Sirka clutches her dagger and hides herself in the darkness.

The guards around her mark do not matter. The unfamiliar girl next to him does not matter. All that matters is the spot that her blade needs to find, the neck, the heart, or one of the arteries, where a single well-placed stab will kill—
She is ready, as she has been so many times before. But she did not expect the prey to detect her.
—Who's there?!
Huh?

lines.st: Sirka

lines.x: Anatoliy—
But Originium Arts have set up the perfect environment for the assassin, and the prey's awareness cannot stop the killer's blade.
A sudden breeze rustles clothes and masks the approaching footsteps, the leap, and the sound of dagger ripping through air—
Sorry, Generalik.
I need to 'borrow' your life.
The bodyguards have detected the intruder, even without hearing her sound.
But the weapon has already pierced the target's neck, and withdrawn as slickly as it went in.
Sirka is not in a hurry to escape. Without a pause, she proceeds to make her next stab, only to realize that there is no blood flowing from the first wound.
What—
It seems she has simply cut a gap in some kind of hard, golden substance.
It does not even look human.
Ugh...
What... is this?
How could this be? I had—
There's the assassin! Get her!
After her... hurry—
After her!!
After her! Don't let her get away!
You two, stay here and protect the Generalik and Hierda! The rest of you, with me!
Generalik, your injury—
...Let me.
Let me see his wound...
The girl lays her hands on the young man's neck.
There was a piece of Originium crystal hidden underneath the collar, which should have been ripped open along with the flesh around it to reveal the bone beneath.
Underneath her palms, however, the injury is less serious than first imagined.
...It seems the Originium has already begun to repair the wound. There's no need to worry.
What did you say?
I said, it seems the Originium is repairing your wound. Are you in pain?

I don't feel anything. But that suka pierced my neck—
I felt it!
I couldn't speak, couldn't make a sound... I felt like I had died.
Maybe she only cut the Originium crystal on the surface of your body. I'm sorry I wasn't able to stop the assassin...
Hah, what can you do? A sword would go right through you without even slowing down.
Maybe she did kill me. Maybe I would be a corpse, if not for you—your miracle.
I can tell the difference between having my skin cut and having the artery in my neck cut.
It's not a miracle... *sigh*.
What I want to know is, what does this mean? Does it mean I can't die? Not even after a thousand assassination attempts?
And it's all because of you, even though you claim you can't save me, that you only remove my pain...
You're the real deal, my friend. You've saved me twice now...
Argh...
The young man's voice grows weaker after his initial excitement. The repairing of his wound has drained him.
You need to rest.
Tell me, how can I repay...?
He soon falls unconscious.
...I don't need repayment, Anatoliy.
I never have...
Hierda looks up in the direction where the assassin escaped, soldiers in hot pursuit.
She recalls those eyes that she saw in the darkness, bright and calm.
Desperate and dangerous.
She was Infected too...
How did it come to this? Is there anything I can do?
How is the Generalik?
He's sleeping.
Is he out of danger?
Yes.
In that case, you should get some rest too. I will keep watch.
Thank you for all that you've done for the general.
No... I simply try to give comfort to everyone who needs it.
I'm not tired. I think there might be other people here who need my help.
I would like to go out and find them.
We cannot deny your requests... but the Generalik's orders were for you to remain by his side.
He will not be happy if he wakes up and finds that you are missing.
I promise, I won't be away for long. Please, give me a chance... a chance to do more, in order to enrich my soul.
Very well, but please be careful.
The city is currently taking in additional Infected. We cannot guarantee that these ruffians will not cause trouble.
I'll be careful.
Please, my friend is in bad shape! I need to get medicine!
As I said, there is a strict curfew in place here.
Either you submit a request and wait for a decision, or hand the patient to us, and we'll transport her to receive treatment.
But you don't allow anyone to go with! There's no time, I have to—
Not before sunrise. It's the rules.
Purr...
Huh?
Now go back.
What that—in the bushes behind you?
That sort of trick won't work—
*roar*—!
Target has been spotted in Naberezhnaya, near the Third District.
Ponjal. Reinforcements are on their way.
Wait, is that really—
Backup! I need backup!
The soldier quickly turns around and calls to his comrades near the building.
Amiya takes one last look at the shadow darting through the bushes, and takes off in the opposite direction.
(Phew...)
(This was the busy street we saw during the day.)
(Hm—)
—I'm sorry, I'm sorry!
I got held up checking the boilers, I'll go home immediately—
You will be detained and fined for violation of curfew.
Do not attempt to resist.
Please, I have to go to work tomorrow—
(I have to avoid the searchlights. But why is there such a strict curfew here?)
(I hope I can find more medicine for Arts overload reactions...)
(Raidian...)
The city of Zelgrad feels dark, even with lamps on both sides of the streets, as though neither the twin moons nor the stars shine upon it.
Amiya dashes along the side of the street, dodging the ever-present searchlights, looking up at the signs on the buildings.
*Whimper*
It's you... Are the people looking for you nearby? Why are they chasing you?
(Rubs against Amiya)
(Tugs at Amiya's skirt)
Oh... where are you taking me?
I'm sorry, I don't have time—
Purr!
The 'cloudbeast' in the shadows keeps tugging at Amiya's skirt, trying to pull her towards a nearby alley.
Looking in that direction, Amiya sees that there is an area of shadow that the searchlights do not touch.
Hm—
I should check it out.
What is this...
A figure sits by the wall in the shadows beyond the searchlights' reach, hardly human anymore.
What little skin is visible through the bandages that almost completely cover his body shows a shade of eerie, translucent green.
Skin and muscle tissue on his arm are forming small clumps like moss and peeling off.
All he can do is wrap his arm in more bandages, as though hoping it will slow the departure of his skin and flesh.
(Hoarse wailing)
Wh-What happened to you?
Mur...
Mur... where are you?
Purr...
Mur? Is this its name?
The light from the searchlights finally allows Amiya to see the 'cloudbeast' clearly.
*sniffles*—
The strange creature growls softly, as though confirming that Amiya has found the man, then disappears into the night.
I can't see... I can't see! Where are you, Mur?
The twisted figure stumbles towards her, his soggy flesh making a sickening sound underneath his bandages.
He does not realize that he would reveal himself to the searchlights if he took one step further. Amiya dashes forward and stops him.
Look out—!
Who?
Who's there...
