What... what's this sickness?
I-Is there any way I can help?
My goodness, your arm...
Amiya catches the man as he collapses. He emanates the scent of a rotten bog as his limbs twitch.
It is the scent of death.
Mur... Mulka!
All of you...
...left me...
Will never, see again.
Will never...
'Will never see again.'
In the man's confusion and pain, Amiya once again touches the emotion that causes her pain.
A black crown appears above her head.
As she touches his consciousness, she sees a small cabin, a woman and child who never returned after leaving home, a cloudbeast leaps from the window sill—
And a man who brought back a monster.
'The collapse in the new industrial district caused nineteen deaths and thirty-four injuries at a nearby school.'
'...We express our deepest regrets for the accident. Compensation has been issued to those affected...'
I won't open the window again, Mur. I won't give you another chance.
Purr?
I won't open the door again...
I won't open it for anyone.
You and I will be the only ones here.
Forever...
'...An experimental animal escaped from the industrial district. Anyone with information should call the Department of Livestock at 10103. A reward is being offered...'
Purr...
We'll never leave each other. They won't take anything else from me.
Yes, that's it...
Kirill!
Kirill! Are you home?
I haven't seen you at the factory in a week. Are you alright?
If you are, go talk to the supervisor and get formal approval for leave, okay? They won't let me do it on your behalf—
Kirill...
If you can hear me, remember that you can rely on us.
We're a community, remember?
Your condition, 'Mur', and that voice outside the door—
What's all this about...?
Oh—
(Oh no, they found me!)
(I must buy time, try to get this patient out from here.)
(He's unconscious. I have to hurry—)
Target acquired.
Do not attempt to resist.
Third District patrols, in position.
(I can't get caught right now. I have to figure out what's going on with this man. This could be what Zelgrad is trying to hide—)
(I remember now. That woman at the transfer area was saying something about dust and infection. Now I see a patient with strange symptoms... yes...)
I'm sorry, I must—
Do not attempt to resist.
Do not—
You there! Follow me!
This way!

lines.loc: City of Zelgrad, Underground Residential Layer Jan 21, 1102, 02:16

lines.x: The streets are empty... but the underground is much busier.
Is this where the Infected was pointing me to?
Go get help, we need extra hands—
Oh. What are you doing here, kid?
Is something wrong?
The pub owner Prokhor is dead! Looks like a robbery-murder. His body was found in the sewers. Who would have thought something like this could happen in Zelgrad?
The sewer cleaners found him. We need more people to haul the body up, and then we'll report it in the morning...
Oh, why am I even telling you this, just make way, I need to get help.
I'm no help when it comes to something like this... sorry.
It's alright.
(Is this where they found the body?)
(There's someone here...)
Excuse me—
You found someone?
A kid? What are you doing here? Where are your parents? This is no place for you.
I would like to ask for directions. Can you point me to people who need help?
People suffering from Oripathy, or other kinds of illness and pain...
Weird kid... I guess you're looking for a hospital? Someone in your family got sick or hurt?

Hospital...
That works too.
Well, you'll only get arrested if you go outside now. But there's a place I can point you to if you need a doctor urgently...
She'll treat anyone, as long as you have money.
'Go out the steel door with a red circle on it, and take the path without street lamps or searchlights.'
'Keep going until you reach a wall. Crouch down and shove at the wall until you find a spot that's loose.'
'That's the door that leads to an abandoned factory, where you'll find the clinic and doctor you're looking for.'
Doctor... doctor...
Painkillers, please, give me painkillers! I'll give you all the factory scrips I have! I can't take it anymore, I can hear the rocks grow beneath my skin—
The doctor said not to rely on medicine until the pain reaches a certain threshold. It'll keep you from developing resistance too quickly, and make the meds last longer.
Just hang in there... we've got to get back to the factories after we get our meds for the day. You need to rest while you can.
I can't stand...
You're just imagining it! You're hurting so much that you can't feel anything. Let's see what degree of pain it corresponds to—
Hey, I think you're allowed meds now.
Quick, ask—ask for me!
Please, allow me to help.
Who are you?
I don't care who you are, just help me—please!
What are you talking about? We don't even know who she is—
Hierda walks forward and takes the hands of the Infected on the stretcher in her own.
Tiny Originium grow from his ice-cold hands and legs. They can cause such lingering pain that death easily becomes preferable.
What are you doing? I'm calling for the doctor. Doctor! Doctor Nadezhda Pavlovna!
*pant*... *pant*...
Wait... your Originium is changing color?
I can't do much, but I can at least stop the pain.
...Is he dead?
No, I think—
What are you calling... dead...
Blyat! I thought—I thought you had gone to heaven already, you lucky bastard!
It doesn't hurt anymore... thank you.
I don't know who you are or how you did it, but could you help that guy over there too?
I apologize on his behalf. He might be a rude mudak, but he was only worried about me.
Hey!
Of course.
This is what I came for...
She speaks softly as she takes the other Infected's hand.
A warm, dazzling light surrounds the Infected. He feels himself rejuvenated and even stands up from the ground.
This is amazing... I got better all of a sudden! It's better than any medicine! How could this be?
What are you—
Oh, Doctor Nadezhda! I-I'm not saying your medicine's bad! Not at all!
Uh...
Doctor Nadezhda...
(Is that the doctor the man in the underground layer was talking about?)
Hierda turns around to see that a door has opened at the end of the corridor.
The fluorescent white light of an operating room shines through the door, where a masked middle-aged woman wearing a white coat and gloves is standing.
Doctor...
The doctor shakes her head, wipes her hands with a towel and puts on her gloves again, before waving Hierda over.
So you're that one they say removes people's pain with Arts.
You know of me?
I thought you might come. I've already lost a bunch of patients thanks to you.
You may have cured their ailment, but you've also cost me a large chunk of my income.
I thought you were a doctor...
Does a doctor not need to eat? Besides, legally speaking, I'm not a doctor anymore. My license was revoked. I'm working unlicensed now.
I'm trying to make enough money to get my license back. What do you think I should do with someone who's ruined my livelihood?
I regret it, but I can't just stand by and watch when there are patients who need my help.
Seeing the girl's nervous expression, the face beneath the mask seems to relax.
Just a bad attempt at a joke. Don't mind it. The atmosphere here is depressing enough as it is.
But I am curious how you manage to do it. You have such incredible Arts, yet all you do is travel and preach like the Yurodstvo, without charging a single coin?
I can't explain my powers... but please understand that I mean no harm.
Well, you certainly look cute, but I'm not in the habit of trusting someone who gives without asking for anything in return.
What are you here for, little bunny?
Doctor Nadezhda! I have an emergency here!
Never seen this one before, but he's in bad shape—
Huh? You're here too, Hierda?
Oh... it's been a few days, hasn't it? You seem to be in better spirits now.
Enough chit-chat, let me see the patient.
Put on protective clothing immediately, Borislav, and prepare the surgery room.
Gotcha!
...Belay that, take a dose of metabolism inhibitor right now, and try to get in touch with Tonya.
I'll deal with the surgery myself.
Hierda hears the patient's weak, pained cries as the bed is pushed past her.
She instinctively reaches out, hoping to give her usual help, but fails to give the patient any comfort.
Hierda follows the patient as he is pushed into the operating room, but she could do no more than let go of the hand in front of the operating room door.
Thank goodness...
Did you find this patient?
I should... thank you...
Just doing what I can... are you a doctor here?
The patient's condition is very unusual. It's not like any Oripathy I've seen before... I'm not even sure if it's Oripathy at all.
Do you know—
No, I'm not a doctor... I wish I was.
But I can't heal them. What I can do is so limited...
I'm sorry, I got ahead of myself. I take it you are a cleric?
It's alright, I didn't notice either... that you're so sick too.
You mean my condition...? How can you tell?
No, you're not like the others... you're very ill, but you're not seeking salvation, and I shouldn't do anything for you...
But how do you endure it, when you carry so much pain with you?
I'm sorry, I don't understand—
The diminutive Cautus casts her gaze towards the operating room.
I feel pain... a lot of pain.
I thought I didn't feel pain anymore, but I still feel such heavy pain when I see these people suffer...
Why... why does God make people suffer?
Why does she put such trials upon them... is suffering God's law?
Amiya is perplexed.
The Cautus before her seems even younger than her, but there is a sort of altruism with her that seems incongruent with her age.
Even without the black crown appearing, the Sarkaz King's power links Amiya's consciousness with her counterpart.
She does not sense any strong emotion, only a disjointed cloud, or a roiling ocean. The endless sorrow in the girl's consciousness threatens to swallow her.
Amiya is not willing to delve any further.
But my understanding is that this is not in line with Lateran law—sorry, I don't mean to offend your religion.
I don't think any suffering has to be inevitable. The pain imposed upon us is something that we should fight with all our strength.
To help those who are suffering and defeat the ones inflicting the suffering... that's what we should do.
But there are always people who can't be saved.
There's always suffering, with no end in sight... does what we do really have meaning?
Do you not despair?
Perhaps.
I would have been crushed by despair, if I were on my own.
But I'm never by myself, never have been...
Someone once told me of her dream, of her vision for this land... when people will overcome their differences, and Terra becomes a home for everyone.
Her dream has inspired and united many people. I have borne witness to the legacy of that dream, and I'm certain that people will continue to carry it on.
I don't know how to completely eliminate suffering, of course. I suppose that's something only 'God' can do.
There may be no end to suffering, but hope continues to live on.
A home for everyone...
How is he, doctor?
Where did you find him?
First District, in an alley by the factories.
It's quite far from Kirill's home.
He must have known that he didn't have long to live, and he didn't want to be found by people who knew him... poor Tonya is still looking for him.
Do you mean...?
I've done all I can, but his basic biological functions have completely failed... all I can do is mitigate his pain in some measure.
Is there anything we can do?
Even the most miraculous Arts cannot reverse total failure of biological function.
But feel free to try to ease his pain with your Arts, if he wakes up.
Did you find medicine, Amiya?
Closure—
I just found a doctor. Give me a moment.
Doctor Nadezhda, do you have medicine for Arts overload reactions here?
Arts overload reaction? What are the symptoms? Weakness in the limbs, or brain fatigue?
She lost consciousness... we don't have enough emergency medicine. Can we get some from you?
Lost consciousness? That sounds serious...
I can't just give you that sort of medicine without ascertaining the patient's condition. I'll come with you.
Alright...
Doctor—
Metabolism inhibitor for you. I wasn't joking. Stay behind and help him, if you're willing.
There's no obligation. If you don't want to help, you're free to leave on your own.
Borislav will be bringing Tonya over. She's been looking for the patient. There'll be someone taking care of him.

Oh, and... Amiya's the name, right? Take a dose of metabolism inhibitor, since you've been in contact with that patient. Not that it's much more than a placebo, given how little we know about this sickness.
Alright, let's go.
...Wait!
Amiya... that's your name, right?
Yes.
My name is... Hierda.
Maybe we'll meet again—
Where is the patient? Lead the way.
O-Okay—Sorry, Hierda...
...Will we meet again?
Hierda walks into the operating room after the others have left.
The disintegrating patient has been moved to a bed, surrounded by transparent tarp sheets as a temporary quarantine measure, making it hard to see clearly.
Hierda walks closer, and sees that the patient's chest continues to rise and fall underneath the new bandages.
Ugh...
You're awake? How are you feeling?
...It hurts...
Help me... help me.
I-I can't end your pain. I tried, but I couldn't liberate you from your pain like I do with the others—
Ugh...
Is there anything I can do to make you feel better?
Argh—ugh...
...Kill...
What did you say?
Kill...
Me.
Kill you...?
I can't see... Mulka.
My Mulka—
You can't get up—
*cough* *cough*!!
You need to stay still and conserve your strength. Using up your energy now will only make it hurt more later.
Do you need something? I'll help you.
*cough*...
I went to where we first met.
I saw you sitting there with a cloudbeast in your arms.
How strange, when you're already gone...
Argh—
Sir!
What do I want...? I want to die...
Kill me. Don't give me any more hope.
Don't let her see me as I am now...
No, maybe... maybe I can—
She cannot describe her sudden impulse. Does she want to fulfill his wish, or help him live on less painfully?
There is no act of resolve. Hierda simply reaches out again and places her hand upon his heaving chest.
(I ask you to grant another wish.)
(May your blessings be upon all of us equally.)
(Even if Oripathy is not the reason for his pain, even if he could not know your name...)
I hope, from the bottom of my heart, that you will be far from pain.
The skin, a sickly green covered in red blood, peels off like moss. The soft flesh beneath has hardened.
Orange rocks begin to replace what is left of the man. Hierda's eyes go wide; she has never seen a transformation like this before.
Finally, a small smile appears upon the patient's face.
...If you see 'Mur'...
Help me...
Thank him for his companionship.
What did you do?
I... I didn't—
I don't think I was seeing things.
Please explain—what did you just do to this patient?
The young man deftly brushes the dead body to one side with his sword, takes a silk handkerchief from a servant, and begins to wipe away the blood from the blade.
So, tell me...
What do you mean when you say you don't know where she is?
...We sent someone to follow Gospozha Hierda, but we lost track of her after she entered the underground residential layer.
We began searching for her immediately, and we have narrowed down the search to an illegal Infected squatter zone that we have been trying to eliminate.
We believe that Gospozha Hierda went there to... perform her miracles.
Perform her miracles... Hmph. Who told her she could hand out blessings like that? Does she think everyone deserves this salvation?
Generalik! We found an illicit gathering in the Third District while pursuing the assassin!
These Infected are in violation of curfew, and attempting to resist arrest. They may be a diversion for the assassin—
Your orders, sir?
Both the Third District and the main urban area where Gospozha Hierda might be are not far from here.
'Might be'?
...In fact, we are certain she's there.
Then we'll go to the Third District.
It's too late... he's dead.
We saw it! This girl used Arts on him, and then he died!
The youth gives Pavel a wave off.
We do not wish to harm someone who is unarmed. We would appreciate it if you could provide us with information that demonstrates you are not hostile.
I didn't harm him... I just didn't want him to continue to be in pain.
The doctor could not treat his condition, and I couldn't save his life.
He was sick? What sort of illness?
I want to know too... I've never seen it before.
The youth steps forward to the side of the bed, carefully examining the dead patient's terrifying cadaver...
The expression does not change in the slightest.
This validates our hypothesis. Whatever secret the Army is hiding in Zelgrad, it's killing the people here.
Zelgrad is not paradise for the Infected. We must tell people the truth, and get them out of here.
You're right, but how are we going to get the word out when we have a hard time getting the group together?
You... want to take the people here away?
I have friends here who will believe me... I can contact them, if you're willing to take them with you.
We would love to be able to trust you, young lady, but how do you prove that you can be trusted?
...I can tell you about the Generalik's troop deployments here—
What's happening?!
We didn't alarm any soldiers on our way here!
Maybe somebody else caught their attention.
No time for analysis. We pull out according to plan.
As for you, young lady—
...I'll come with you.

lines.st: '...Pavel, when there is danger, let the students leave first; they're easiest to identify, and likely to be considered less of a threat.'
'Their Tulskaya Technical School background makes them a higher priority for retention amongst the Infected. More numbers will be preserved if they get away.'
'All life is equal, of course, but sacrifice is inevitable in our work. We must all maximize the value of our lives for the cause.'
'Is it sad? Perhaps, but I do not have the luxury to wallow in sorrow. I must save my strength for anger and resistance.'
'That though the winter night be long and cold, have faith that the sun will shine again upon us equally.'

lines.x: We're under the Second District. I remember the pillars marked with different colors in this passage. The exit is just ahead.
Are we just going to leave like this? What about your comrades who're staying behind?
If the Teacher and Pavel wanted us to leave, there must be a reason for it. Maybe they'll join us after fighting off the soldiers.
Shh—hide, someone's coming!
I saw someone. They must have went this way.
Don't get distracted. The other Infected don't matter, but the Generalik wants that Cautus found at any cost!
They're looking for... me?
Put down your weapons and you'll be spared!
Put down your weapons—
Turn that thing off.
Y-Yes, sir!
Turn off the speakers!
There's fewer of them than I thought. Report.
Yes, sir.
At around 0300 hours, patrols found a group near the entrance to the Third District underground, apparently attempting to gain access to the residential district through the underground layer.
We were outnumbered and the Marshal gave express orders not to harm Infected resources, causing us to lose track of some of them during the chase—
The killer presses his forehead, trying to soothe the splitting headache. He did not even look before swinging his sword.
...Someone who can talk better.
S-Sir!
There were more of them, but the patrol was short-handed, which allowed some of them to escape to the underground layer before we could confirm their identity.
The complexity of the underground layer makes tracking difficult. However, such a mistake should not have happened to begin with! It was our error!
You talk well and you know how to reflect. But that can't wipe clean the mistake, can it?
I-I—
The soldier reflexively glances at the still-warm body of his comrade lying on the ground.
He remembers the rumors: Generalik Anatoliy hates people who are talkative, people who overestimate themselves, and—
He hates liars.
I will accept any punishment! / Perhaps I should explain.
You—what?
Perhaps I should explain. I was directly involved, after all.
A volunteering hero. What do you say to the charges of illegal gathering and resisting arrest that you and your friends are facing?
Uchitel—
(Shakes head)
We did not resist arrest, because we were not gathering illegally. We have stayed to await justice.
Disappointing. I thought you'd have something new to say...
You bore me.
The Generalik turns around to face his soldiers before the calm youth has a chance to add anything.
The Infected here refused to cooperate with you, didn't they?
That's resisting arrest.
Sir!
So it looks like you have no idea what to do if there are more than a couple of people resisting arrest.
Foolish and inflexible.
I accept any punishment—
But I am magnanimous, and therefore I will show you what to do in these circumstances.
He moves.
The sword reaches the calm youth first. She would not have been able to avoid it, if someone had not pulled her out of the way.
Argh—
—Pavel!
Even after the youth saw the sword take the life of a trained soldier, it is hard to accept that it has now taken one of their comrades just as easily.
The older miner did not have time to even utter a word. His eyes wide, his life frozen at the instant when he grabbed the youth's hands.
Only when there are screams and sobbing coming from behind does the youth realize what has transpired.
You make an example, like this. If killing one isn't enough, kill another, until they cooperate.
Mother's orders are important, of course, but under extraordinary circumstances such as these... does it matter whether the Infected is alive or dead?
I have made this decision. I, Anatoliy Svetlanov Buterin, take full responsibility for everything that happens here.
Now, before I cut off another head, who's going to tell me where your unruly friends have gone?
You're mad! We won't—
The bodies on the ground lie as evidence of the two lives that have departed.
They dye the soles of the youth's boots red, but she does not look down. She looks up, straight into the Generalik's eyes.
Why the anger? You failed. That's the truth that no amount of killing will change.
You claim you have the power to do anything, but you clearly can't get your way. You can't pry open our mouths with your sword, nor will you learn what you want to know.
We have bought precious time for our comrades, while you thrash about, locked in the cage of your own anger.
How dare you—
Fury twists the young man's visage. He wants to raise the butcher's knife again, but he cannot find a sliver of the fear he seeks in the youth's face.
And the whole lot of companions behind as well. Miners, farmers, nothing more, yet not a single one panics or flinches. He is unaccustomed to this reaction, or lack thereof.
Suddenly, Anatoliy realizes that he would simply be creating willing martyrs.
...Enough.
I've seen too many hackneyed tropes tonight.
Kill them all and clean up the mess. Then find—
Stop!
Hierda?
Hierda!
I'm sorry, Anatoliy, I heard you were here—
You came back! You didn't flee!
But why did you leave on your own?
You should be by my side always. This was your promise. Don't you know what a promise is?
I... I'm sorry for the misunderstanding.
But... what's happening here?
Anatoliy tries to block Hierda's line of sight, but he can do nothing to mask the smell.
The scent of blood fills the air, even in the cold night.
...Anatoliy.
You promised not to kill more innocent people.
Hierda tries her best not to sound accusing. She does not want to anger Anatoliy, or further escalate the situation.
If only there was a manual on how to deal with a fickle, temperamental child with too much power over life and death...
Yes, I promised.
Anatoliy...
But you didn't keep your end of the bargain. You left me.
I was only doing what I could while you slept. I said this to you, and you agreed.
If I agreed to anything, it was only under the condition that you stayed with me.
...I don't know how we can carry on, if you keep changing the conditions—

'Don't know how we can carry on'?
You don't know how you can continue to stay by my side?
No, listen to me—
Who planted such terrible thoughts in your mind? Who instilled such ideas in you—
You never questioned me before!
The sword is tossed aside, like a piece of scrap metal.
Anatoliy grabs the Cautus's slim shoulders. Then, amidst the surprised cries, his right knee hits the floor—
He kneels down in front of Hierda.
Oh—
I see you've suffered a malign influence. Tell me, what should I do? How can I change your mind?
Only I can realize your vision and bring glory to your great blessing—as long as you don't leave my side again.
I forgive you! I forgive all your mistakes, for leaving without a word.
But please, don't leave me again... never again say these terrible words.
...I promise.
As long as you promise never to kill another innocent...
As she picks her words, Hierda looks at the corpses lying in the middle of the road, and the Infected behind them.
Most of them have the same expressions on their faces, pained and wary.
Promise not to harm these Infected anymore... not to take any innocent lives.
And I will promise in turn.
I'll stay by your side, and never leave again.
Lieutenant.
...Yes, Generalik?
Herd these scum back to the residential district and put them in an empty apartment.
Station an artillery regiment to keep a close eye on them.
Anatoliy?
Enough. Waste no more time on these dregs.
Let us go.
A lone figure sits in the warehouse. She has sat there through the night, until dawn begins to crack upon the horizon.
'Convince them that this is a matter of life and death'...
How should I tell them...?
Zelgrad is not home...
Are you alright, Tonya?
Doctor Nadezhda Pavlovna...
Sorry to keep you waiting. I've been getting a lot of emergency patients lately.
You don't look well. Do you want something to calm your nerves?
No, I'm fine. I appreciate everything you've done for me and my sister.
Her condition—
Slow down, Tonya. You only brought her yesterday. I need to keep her condition under control first, and I still have questions for you.
First, have similar symptoms appeared on other members of your family?
No, not yet.
Just to be safe, I've entrusted my other siblings in the care of my neighbors, and checked for the source of infection according to your instructions.
Did you find it?
There's only one possibility... my work jacket.
It was issued to us at work, very thick and warm, so I put it around Nina those few days when the power went out... I shouldn't have done it!
She's at home all day. The only thing from the outside she could have come into contact with was that jacket.
And I found a strange... powder on it when I checked it.
Powder?
Yes... I've never seen anything like it. It clung to the surface of the jacket like some kind of dust. Probably got on it while I was washing the clothes.
Whose clothes?
The First Army... or rather, the First Army's researchers.
You mean this has something to do with them?
...We can't be sure yet.
I know what you're thinking, Tonya, but right now there's no way to prove that the powder caused the illness.
We'll have to get past that wall to find out.
...What will happen to my sister? What will the illness do to her?
I'm sorry, Tonya, but I haven't found anything similar to this in the books.
I don't even know if it's just a singular incident or not, until more patients present themselves.
I need more information about this strange new illness.
*sigh*...
Not a good feeling, is it, to be the only one awake?
Yes... I don't how I can make the others believe me.
Do not blame your friends.
Perhaps the land has never promised a future for them, not since the day they were born. They lost the courage to face the truth when happiness is dangled before them.
They will not thank the one who wakes them; they will blame you for ruining their dream.
When the future is full of despair, short-sightedness becomes a survival mechanism.
I won't blame anyone... I know it doesn't seem like an immediate danger to them.
Wait, who are you?
I entered the city with the workers.
It wasn't my intention to disrupt your lives. I only came to see... an old friend.
Will she be here? I don't know... but she is rarely absent from spectacular occasions.
I don't understand what you're saying. If there's nothing else—
How unfortunate. I do understand what you're saying... and what you're looking for.
I help the sleeping wake up, and make the weak strong.
Perhaps we can help each other... if you're willing.
Ah, I see I forgot to introduce myself—
Nice to meet you, Tonya. I'm a teacher. You may call me... Koshelna.
(I think I lost them for real this time...)
(They were strictly aiming for my legs. Were they trying to immobilize me? Why didn't they shoot to kill?)
This is strange...
...Ugh—
You're bleeding. The smell will draw pursuers.
Who—
Let's keep it brief.
I know what you did, and I took care of some of your pursuers. At the current rate, your blood loss will send you into shock in three minutes.
I'll staunch your bleeding, then take you to a place that's... relatively safe.
Who are you?
That's not important, and it's not like you have any other choice. Maybe you could try to stab me with your final breath... but would that be worth it?
Yes, that's more like it.
Keep quiet and conserve your energy.
I went and got a look, Red. Guess what?
The people that we ran into during the day and the folks that came in with them are all gone. Third floor through fifth floor are empty, and we hardly heard any footsteps.
I pried open a few locks just to make sure—
Next time don't pry the locks, just knock.
If they're anything like us, they wouldn't have been sleeping well the first night here.
Do you think they were taken away quietly like the previous group, or did they leave on their own?
They're all miners. I gather they came from the north based on their outfits, but it's not clear whether they're from the Far North.
Let's find that industrial district mentioned in the intel.
I've never had the chance to ask, but do you really trust her that much? Maybe she wasn't really looking for the people who were taken away, and the intel's no good—
She had many chances to get us killed and run away in the last two years. Why hasn't she done so?
How am I supposed to know what she's thinking?
Then shut your crap and don't let me hear that again, or you can go back to Nine and get your brain straightened out before coming out again.
...I'm just being vigilant!
You can, but only if you keep it to yourself at this stage.
We're a very, very long way from having the luxury to settle old scores.
There's no one here...
Doesn't look like anyone's been working here for a while, either. It's been abandoned for a long time.
There are holes in the roof, and no equipment in sight. Looks like it's all been moved.
Industrial transfer.
What?
When we first came, the soldier who acted as our guide told us that the previous tenants in our apartment were 'coincidentally' moved to other districts because of industrial transfer.
No matter how 'coincidental', however, industrial transfer rarely takes place between different districts of a nomadic city.
It's only megacities like Londinium and Grypherburg that have the demand and the capacity.
And the corporations that performed industrial transfer in Londinium ultimately ended up moving their factories to smaller nomadic cities nearby, rather than other plates within the city.
How do you know this stuff?
I read.
Fine...
But Zelgrad is just a medium-sized nomadic city... built upon a small-sized nomadic city, even, with unmapped expansion plates all over the place.
There are a lot of questions, but we'll have to take them one at a time. There's no one here, nor in the dorms either. For now we can eliminate—
Wait.
What?
There's something up ahead—
Hey!
No.
What?
You were right, next time, we should ask her what she's doing.
She left someone here for us.
It's typical Arts overload symptoms alright, with concurrent acute neurasthenia that makes single emergency medication less effective.
There isn't much I can do other than prescribe sedatives and rest. She should refrain from using Arts until neurasthenia symptoms disappear.
(Mutters) Thank goodness it wasn't that...
What do you mean?
It's nothing... say, your description of the symptoms was quite accurate, and you performed appropriate early treatment. I take it you have a bit of medical knowledge?
'Have a bit of medical knowledge'? I'm—

opts: We're from a pharmaceutical company.
We conduct research into Oripathy.
For certain reasons, however...
We don't have a doctor with us right now.

lines.x: I see... interesting, isn't it, to have so many 'doctors' arrive in Zelgrad lately.
Well, I guess I'm done here. I'll go back now—
One moment, doctor!
Do you know anything else about the patient that I brought to your clinic?
Just another poor soul too far gone to be helped... what else are you expecting me to tell you?
You were not surprised to see his symptoms.
You have seen others like him before, haven't you? How many other people have gotten the same illness here?
Oripathy isn't the only thing that kills people in this land.
Besides, if something is being deliberately suppressed in Zelgrad, there's a reason for it, and I'm not going to look for trouble.
I don't care what kind of doctor you are and why you came to Zelgrad. All I can tell you is that you shouldn't get involved in this stuff, and get out as soon as possible.
But you haven't left.
You haven't given up on helping the people here. Don't we share the same goal?
Don't flatter me. I'm just scraping a living by doing what I know how to do.

opts: We need a 'doctor' to help more people.
We trust any 'doctor' who's true to his or her duty.

lines.x: Hah... listening to that stuff is what cost me my license. Talk is cheap.
But fine... I still don't recommend that you get involved, but if you insist on investigating...
One of the workers told me she took a piece of contaminated clothing from behind that wall...

opts: The problem is with whatever lies behind that wall.
Does that strange powder have something to do with the Sarcophagus?

lines.x: Doctor, I'm worried about what Amiya and that doctor described...
Kal'tsit should have sealed the Sarcophagus five years ago.
But Ursus is evidently hacking into the Sarcophagus very aggressively. I can't tell how far their research has progressed until I see the Sarcophagus myself.
We can't afford to wait!
I agree...
Raidian! The doctor said you have to rest!
Maybe I'm not the one who should talk, but shouldn't an elite operator exercise better judgment? Stay in bed.
I encountered powerful countermeasures while trying to probe what's happening inside the wall... it's well-defended...
Besides the army's electromagnetic jamming... the whole city's magnetic field feels strange...
I'm sorry, Doctor... I can't help for now...

opts: You took on a great risk for us.
No one could have done better.
Get some rest, Raidian.

lines.x: See? Listen to the Doctor, won't you? At least keep the blanket around you if you want to sit up. You were shivering just now.

opts: But we do have to act quickly.

lines.x: Based on what I saw, there are more strange things going on in Zelgrad than we thought.
That gravely ill patient, the strange creature... the First Army must be hiding something terrible.
The First Army seems to be uncooperative towards the State Council. It's unlikely that they'll help us.

opts: We can't sit around and wait.
We need to get through that wall.

lines.x: We have plenty of experience with situations like this! Leave the fighting to me!
There's no such thing as an impregnable wall. Even the Armies of Ursus make mistakes.
If you ever need someone to hack through a firewall, I'm right here!

opts: It's very late. The garrison is probably on alert right now from all the commotion.
Let's look for a way to get through the wall during the day.

lines.x: Stop walking around like that, mudak! You're making my eyes hurt.
It's been two days since they took the boss. When are you gonna go and get him out?
We have contingencies for situations like this. If he isn't back after one week, and there's no movement outside, Oleg will take over and we'll get ready to scram...
Are you out of your mind, svolotsch? Boss was telling us to be flexible, not run away at the slightest sign of trouble!
There isn't much difference.
Of course there is. Don't you remember what we sing when we drink? 'Volniki have two paths to freedom, one they carve out with their swords, the other when they bleed and fall'—
We haven't done anything except bite like an obedient tuskbeast ever since we came here!
Kuznetsov's people are everywhere. We'll be detected immediately if we leave the base during the ceasefire. Right now, we need to keep the ship safe, and say nothing if anyone asks.
Oleg is already planning the retreat.
At least we need to make those mudak pay the price for looking down on us.
Is that more important than your life?
But we're not that lunatic Kuznetsov's pet tuskbeasts!
Even a tuskbeast will bite through its fence if cornered. Sirka would agree with me, if she was here.
But she's not.
You're right, though. We would be making a night visit to the flagship right now if Sirka was here.
I'm starting to miss her. Should've learned those tricks of hers. Damn it all...
Enough slacking! Scioppa's back, and in one piece!
You have three minutes to hide your liquor and smokes and illegal Arts units—
We weren't drinking!
Or smoking. And we already hid our Arts units in case Kuznetsov sends another inspector. They took a bunch with them the last time, even ones that were still being repaired.
Where's the boss, Oleg?
On deck! No one knows when he came back. He was standing there when I saw him.
He just smiled when I asked, saying that everything's good. You know how people have been on edge since that incident in December.
What's our next step? Are we still leaving?
The alarm's cancelled for now. Go back to your posts. I'll make another round; I'll let you know if anything happens—
There you are, Oleg.
Boss!
I want everyone who's awake out on deck.
I have a important announcement to make.

lines.loc: Assault Ship Volnov, Upper Deck Jan 21, 1102, 02:45

lines.x: Is everyone here?
Everyone on the night shift.
Inform the others after the shift change.
What's going on? The last time you called all hands was...
Remember the bomb that went off in Central recently?
Who could forget? We could feel it all the way here. They say it left nothing except some strange-colored dust. The sight of the Viy eating someone could hardly be more terrible.
Hah, the Viy eating someone... you're right.
That's the First Army's new weapon, which the people above really want to get their hands on. That's when the Special Tactics Formation comes in handy.
The man shrugs and turns around to face the others, which fall silent as he opens his mouth. His smile never leaves his face as he raises his voice.
In other words, we just got a big job.
What do you mean?
Are you saying—
Yes, we're going to steal the First Army's new weapon.
Wait a second. Going to the First Army's position means passing through the front lines, right? Which means we'll have to deal with the Second Army. Is that even possible?
Or are we going to go around—
Or is it just a part of some kind of operation?
Maybe we just need to carry out our orders, like when we put down that mutiny.
You're right. His High Excellency Marshal Evgeny Andrianov Kuznetsov has made arrangements for us to pass the Second Army's lines safely.
All we need to do is...
Advance.
Can we talk specifics, now that it's just the two of us? You might have fooled the others, but you can't fool me.
So that was enough to fool the others.
What did Kuznetsov do to you? Did he put any holes in you? Let me see—
Ever since that purification operation in December, everybody had tons of questions for me whenever they ran into me on the training grounds, but no one said anything today.
Is it because optimism is our nature? Does nothing else matter?
Because they believe in you, of course! The Ataman who lights the way, the war caster of legend, the great leader of the Volniki, who reap enemies like mossoat...
Who would they believe in, if not you?
Wow, keep going, any other titles I haven't heard of?
—But if you ask me, I would say that foolishness is our nature.
Foolish enough to not remember old grudges, foolish enough to survive, foolish enough that people in power won't suspect that we might get back at them.
I'm glad Sirka isn't here to hear it.
I'm your second-in-command now. Stop talking about our noble lady every opportunity you get.
Well, you don't like it when I bring up Pavel.
He's been gone three years, he's probably hit it big again somewhere else. He doesn't need us to reminisce about him.
In Baba's name, man was born to be a quartermaster. He can fill his pockets wherever he goes. If it wasn't for Oripathy...
He never wrote back.
Were you robbing Messengers again?
Come on, you knew where I was these past two days, Gospodin Oleg, how would I find the time?
Finally getting back on topic? Now talk. What happened?
What I said, basically.
What about the part that's not 'basic'?
Not basic, eh... you were there when I killed Basmanov, weren't you?
You remember what he said to me?
...Surrender to Kuznetsov. That's all he wants.
Stop resisting, Basmanov. It was sheer madness to commit mutiny on the front lines, not to mention your second-in-command was leaking all your plans—
I don't blame him.
...What?
I don't blame him. I don't blame anyone...
I just blame myself for not seeing the truth sooner.
What truth? The obvious truth that you can't win?
The truth that the flames have already burned away houses and clothes, and will soon reach the skin and the flesh beneath... we should have awakened sooner.
What are you talking about—
I don't blame you, truly. I knew it was you who came, when even Private Vyacheslav made it to the bridge alive to deliver the news.
The Special Tactics Formation... the isolated, expendable, fickle executioners, the free Volniki who are never truly free—
All I know is that the arrival of Sechin means you won't even get a court martial.
Yet you're giving me a chance to escape, just like how you let the miners go.
On the surface, you're just doing everything Kuznetsov told you to do. Yet even now, you're trying to give me a way out, against his wishes.
The stalemate continues. Kuznetsov needs every soldier he can get. He will forgive, if you surrender.
Do you know the name Yakov Petrov, Major?
No.
What I shame.
It's only now that I realize that there was someone who saw that the house was burning, except no one was listening to him, and called him a madman.
That is what they will call me. Oczip Basmanov the traitor, disciple of Yakov Petrov.
That's all I have to say, Major. I'm not surrendering. You do what you must.
I only hope that your blade will always remember who you are.

lines.loc: Assault Ship Volnov, Command Center Jan 21, 1102, 09:21

lines.x: Thirty-two klicks until the front, sir. We're seven hundred and fifty-one klicks from Zelgrad.
ETA is five hours for the former and seven days for the latter.
Good work.
Oleg will relieve you in half an hour.
I can go on—
No you can't. Go to bed.
This kid was on duty all day in the control room while you were away. He only took a two-hour break before coming back. Won't listen to me at all.
I was just worried!
Stop worrying. If thinking about things ever did any good, I would have prayed to Baba for a bolt of thunder to smite Kuznetsov.
Now get out of here, I'll be checking the quarters in two hours.
Good, looks like life will go on, if anything happens to me.
Do you need your eyes checked? Did you see any of them listen to what I say?
They will when I'm gone. You're more of a leader than I am. It was a wise move to move you out of logistics—
It was because I made good pies and didn't let you take extra ones, wasn't it?
Well, that's part of it.
I knew you were out for vengeance.
Come on, don't say that—
You're still thinking about what Basmanov said.
—Huh?
Maybe his ramblings made sense in his own mind, but that last thing he said was clearly a taunt.
You trust your blade more than you trust anyone else, don't you?
Now that's unfair, of course I trust you guys more.
Idi v'banyu. We all know that they call us Volniki the free folk because we have the freedom to come together or part ways as we please—
So, the only things we can and must trust is ourselves and our swords.
Is that a sword, anyway? Or an Arts unit? What IS it?
Never mind. Anyway, it will always know you, and it will never kill you. That's all that matters.
Oleg.
Huh?
You like to talk about Baba. Do you know who she is, or what she looks like?
No idea. She might be Kuranta, or Liberi, or Elafia, but she couldn't be Ursus.
All old stories that we tell to pass the time. We need stories and song to bring us together. Isn't that what your precious Sirka always said?
...'Our Baba put a glass house upon the legs of a fowlbeast'...

lines.st: Our Baba put a glass house upon the legs of a fowlbeast.
Not to move from place to place like us, but so that she could turn around and shut people out at any time.
She never asks what you want, but asks:
'What else can you lose?'
She takes your burdenbeast, your sword and bow, the wealth that you traded blood for;
Even the victory that made your mother proudest.
Our ancestors called her an evil witch, but they learned when they grew old—
She was simply collecting on death's behalf.
If one has nothing left to pay:
Their sword thrice-broken, their siblings all buried upon different battlefields, and with no strength left to even hate—
Baba would be silent.
She no longer blocks the way, but turns her hut around, and reveals the path without echoes.

lines.x: 'The last thing she said to us was...'
'I can protect you no longer.'
Yes.
You can't carry a tune, but you remember the words well.
Sirka sang it for me a lot.
Alright, you can stop—
I often wonder, if there comes a day when even the all-powerful Baba can no longer protect us...
How far will we go to survive?
Message from central command.
Put it through.
I see you've left the base.
An astute observation, sir.
You should be reporting your position and status every two hours, Major Razin.
A report every two hours is impractical. Should I explain the reason in detail?
Do not waste time on long-range communications. Report on your progress.
Well, as you know, the Volnov has left the base and is currently approaching the front lines. Assuming we do not need to linger near the front lines and observe the situation—
There's no need. Proceed directly.
Even if it might cause the Second Army to attack?
I said, it is not your concern. What you should be concerned with is getting your men near the satellite city before you run out of power.
There's no time for you to stop, according to my estimations. The Volnov must arrive at the designated location in three days and complete the mission in conjunction with another unit.
I don't know anything about any other unit.
Now you do.
Now, what is the current progress of the Volnov?
Scioppa takes his time glancing at the control panel before answering.
Accelerating steadily. I can't give you an accurate figure, but it will eventually reach a figure that will allow us to arrive by the ETA.
Is that so...?
Then I hope that central command will not have to initiate the next communication.
Why did you lie to him? How long can we keep this up?
In order to survive, we must first solve our most pressing problem.
Give the Second Army enough time to react, then pray that Kuznetsov's 'guarantee' pays off before we're blown to smithereens.
Hiding by yourself again, my brother Fedya?
Why aren't you with Mother?

lines.st: I... like your apple tree. Besides—I don't want to stay there anymore...
That smell is everywhere in the room... I don't want to go back!

lines.x: What smell? The smell of disinfectants, of bitter almond?
The smell is from things that help Mother. I put bitter almond fragrance in my room to stop myself from coughing, and to relieve the pain...
You know that.

lines.st: ...But you're not there either.

lines.x: Because those people in black won't let me go in anymore.
They don't even want me to come near you.

lines.st: Sister...

lines.x: She picks a low-hanging fruit and puts it in the boy's hand.
The fruit is red like agate, like the culmination of the sun of countless summers at the palace, summers that he had forgotten.
He no longer sees the red corridor in the glass palace, only the rays of the sun shining through the leaves and branches like broken glass, and the cool apple upon his palm.
He hears only the sweet, glass-like voice in his ear.
But I'll pay them no heed.
You're my only brother. Nothing can break our bonds of blood.
I'll find you.
Fedya... Fedya!
*cough* *cough* Thank goodness, you're still here.
Listen, I know you don't want to go, but you must. Go with them to Mother's funeral. Do you understand?
I can't be there, but you can...
Come, let me sort your tie out. Your pants are dirty. Did you trip again? You're always so clumsy—
Now, go.
I'll wait for you... under the apple tree.
Yes, my brave Fedya. Do not be afraid, though some may try to confuse and control you, for you are stronger than them all.
You will hear the most sincere voice, the voice of me calling to you.
And I will be here, waiting for you.

lines.st: Fedya.

lines.x: ...The summer palace? Why am I dreaming about something from so long ago...?
The one in the dream... a sister?
But I have no siblings...
Argh—
(The headaches are getting more frequent.)
(Ever since I came back from Katorga...)
Your Imperial Majesty, I bring the latest progress report on the citizen's forum.
Good timing. Saves me from thinking too much.
You look tired.
Strange, isn't it... I had a dream about the summer palace, which I have not seen in many years.
There's a beautiful apple orchard nearby. It'll be a good place to recuperate, if you feel the need.
...Apple orchard?

Yes...
Never mind, it's not important—what's the progress?
Most nobles who were already on our side are inclined to continue, following the Katorga Incident.
They have quickly accepted the decision to trial the citizen's forum, and a few of them are even willing to divert tax funds to establish similar pilot programs in their territories.
I believe it's a good start.
What's the catch?
I'm sure Your Imperial Majesty understands...
The Winter Emergency Resource Allocation Act will not convince the conservatives of the State Council just because it passed the citizen's forum.
It's not just the conservatives. No aristocrat will willingly give up their own profits, much less allow the council to dictate what little remains of the nation's Originium resources.
Even if it's the only way to save Ursus.
Not the only way, apparently, in the eyes of many.
The generals of the empire wallow in the dream that my father weaved for them.

Wasn't enough blood shed on Bloodpeak already? Did they think it was a glorious defeat? Ursine territory would be twice as large now, if they were half the geniuses they think they are!
Absurd... Ridiculous!
...*cough* *cough*!
Please, stay your anger, Majesty, as the doctor instructs.
I expect they understand these things full well. I believe they simply want to get as big a slice of Ursus's flesh, before chaos truly descends.
For some of them, the unity of the nation and the plight of her people pale in comparison to ensuring their own prosperity and that of their descendants.
What are you implying?
I have news.
Out with it.
Only a few people with access to the Amber Palace know that Project Zero's energy utilization research is not progressing as hoped, all of whom are under strict surveillance.
However, our intelligence indicates that the Fourth Army began moving almost at the same time that we received the news.
They are quietly amassing forces for another push along the front lines, while simultaneously moving in the direction of First Army territory.
They're ready on two fronts.
What this means is that the Fourth Army has thoroughly infiltrated not only Grypherburg, but Tsarevgrad itself.
This is a serious matter.
You wouldn't come to me with unfounded conjecture. Who do you suspect?
(Hushed) Vasily Gorchikov.
The Vice Chairman? But isn't he the representative of the new aristocracy in the Duma—
But his family business has longstanding ties with military nobility, and the family of his late wife, House Gorchikov, is a noble house with a long and storied history.
It was by marrying into his wife's family that he was recommended to the Imperial Guard.
Objectively speaking, Vasily's position was always uncertain.
I seem to recall that there was a servant in the Amber Palace from a branch of his family. Saveliy.
I see you catch my meaning.
If someone in legislative leadership goes over to the pro-war faction—
Wait. Volkina, the honorary Vice Chairman who never attends meetings. She's a military noble too!
But she never expresses her opinion.
It's her actions, not her words, that are important. The same goes for Vasily...
Keep a close eye on them. Do not let anyone get away. We must put a stop to any sign of a schism, whether superficial or material.
Understood...
...Are you tired, Witte?
Of course not... Majesty.
I'm beginning to feel powerless, Witte... can we really change anything? Is there anything we can do?
There is still much we can do.
You have cast aside the shadow of your father. You must demonstrate to them that your kindness is not weakness, that it requires even greater strength.
We must not surrender to the things that you rejected.
Enough... I do not want to hear such flattery, least of all from you.
The citizen's forum is a necessary reform. We need more people to stand with us. Time is short.
The empire cannot afford any more internal strife. We cannot use violence against these dissenters.
More patience... continue to work to persuade them, try to awaken their love for this nation, or at the very least, a little bit of conscience...
You're right, Witte... we can't surrender yet.

lines.loc: Rhodes Island Temporary Treatment Center, Odoyev Raion, Deity Grypherburg

lines.x: ...I should have come in the last time I passed by. It's totally different inside!
Why didn't you?
Well, I thought I would do that when there's no longer a line of patients outside the door waiting for treatment.
Now it looks like they all fit inside, even if it does get a little crowded.
I heard you helped a lot.
Not nearly enough.

Do you know, there's a girl here, one of the surviving miners from the Far North who told me the entry hall was the first area to be completed. She likes it because it's always warm and bright, even at night.
But I know that Rhodes Island had to invest in appearances first, just to satisfy the nobles and facilitate further operation.
Otherwise, they would hardly have paid attention to an Oripathy treatment center in downtown all of a sudden.
It is warm and bright, though.
...Sometimes I wonder whether you're just acting dumb, or—

...think, it's important.
But, should we wait...
For Dur-nar to, come back?
Oh, that's the girl I was talking about.

Get everyone, indoors... warmer than, outside.
As for where, to put...
Oh. I can help, to carry some—
Vetochki.
—Oh!
Sorry, did I scare you?
No, no! I just didn't, hear you...
You came again! Thank you!
Just happened to pass by. I see the streets outside are empty, and the stoves have been taken away. Have the rooms been cleared? Enough furniture and equipment for everyone?
No, not yet. Some mattresses and, sheets have arrived, but not enough, and it's so, cold outside...

Better to have, everyone, in the hall.
Oh! At night, we'll try to, get everyone, a bed!
There won't be, anyone in the, hall, when there are, inspections...
...Tsk.
Listen, Vetochki, we both know that the requirements for the treatment center to be perfectly clean and tidy aren't realistic.
Forget about those for now. Just let me know if you need anything. I'll do what I can—
But you sent, the mattresses, and sheets, didn't you?
...What? But I haven't gotten the new supplies yet—
Who came?
A man, wearing clothes, like yours... he brought, the things, and a few, people.
Just now...
That's him!
...Platon?
...Tsk.
What are you doing here?
I thought you took leave to see your sick mother?
Yes, this is one of the charities that my mother sponsors. But I'm surprised you found the time to come to Odoyev and look after these commoners, busy as you are.
I thought His Imperial Majesty and your bright future were the only things on your mind.
No—
Get back.
Behind me, Vetochki.
Is that so? What a coincidence.
Since when did House Lunin become a sponsor of Rhodes Island? When my family is taking full responsibility for this matter?
...Perhaps you should make sure a contract is exclusive before you sign it.
I could say the same to you.
What ARE you doing here, Platon? You have never had the slightest interest in commoners or charity.
Yet you've started doing these things all of a sudden, with a whole retinue of bodyguards... either you've suddenly discovered the goodness in your heart, or you're putting on a performance.
But where are your cameras and lights, if you just want to take a few touching photos for the newspapers and intercity net?
None of your business. Do you want my sponsorship or not?
Of course. Every little bit counts. Next time, however, I suggest you go through official channels.

After all, it's not just Oripathy patients here, but also a group of witnesses under His Imperial Majesty's protection... you don't want to be in the position of having to explain if anything happens to them, do you?
...Hmph!
Where are the supplies he brought, Vetochki?
The blankets, have been, handed out... the mattresses are, still in the, warehouse.
We're planning to, clear out, more rooms, then t-take the, mattresses out.
Eloysius scans the faces of the patients in the hall. They are draped in new blankets, some huddled together, others curled up on the floor.
No one wants to interrupt a moment like this.
Let me see the rest of the stuff.
This is where the supplies he sent are stored.
Care to give a hand, Gospodin Hellagur? I would like to perform another check.
You suspect him.
I didn't think you would be interested.
Not so much a suspicion as a hunch... but maybe it's just all the assassinations and talk of spies that's gotten me on edge.
When you think about it, procuring this stuff represents no difficulty for his family whatsoever. It just never occurred to them to do so.
I'm supposed to be his superior, sort of, but I never managed to have a good influence on him—
My impression is that rank works differently in the Imperial Guard from the Armies.
Unlike the Armies, which have a strict promotion hierarchy, Imperial Guards mostly graduate directly from the military academy. As members of the aristocracy, all of you start as lieutenants.
You are equal in rank, even if you hold different positions, and this will not change in the near future.
Are you saying it's normal that he resents me?
I've seen it many times. Besides, the Imperial Guard doesn't have automatic promotion by tenure.
Not to mention these are peaceful times, and not even the Great Rebellion could breach the walls of Grypherburg. There are few opportunities for merit and promotion.
You're complaining.
Of course I'm not! Besides, things are changing. What I wouldn't give to not have the opportunity to earn merit now...
Platon's family has been trying to get him into the Central Army and onto the front lines. I rejected the reassignment. I suppose it's another reason why he doesn't like me.
If things have gotten to the point when the Central Army is mobilized, no one in Grypherburg is immune.
The Capital Ursus Guard, part of the Central Army, must stand with the Imperial Guard as the final line of defense.
It's disunity that you're concerned about.
You're much easier to talk to when you don't play dumb, you know? If the vice-chairman was here, he would tell me to stop wearing myself out and put myself and family first.
The Far North Incident has brought the schism amongst the factions of Grypherburg to the surface, while the insurrection in Katorga has raised the alarm for the fence-sitters.
I have no doubt that Grypherburg would have fallen apart in the literal sense of the word, if any of the recent assassination attempts had succeeded—
Wait, these supplies...
Is something wrong?
They're all military supplies. They're usually only seen in the military and the factories that supply it.
The council may occasionally divert military supplies in the event of an emergency, but Platon? How did he get his hands on these things?
What was he doing here?
Hmph... hah.
...Who's there?!
Colluding with traitors under the pretense of an Infected treatment center. Just as I thought.
Tell me, lieutenant.
Where is the traitor?
...Traitor? What are you talking about?
An intelligence contact point disguised as an Infected treatment center, payment made in supplies instead of cash...
All the threads lead to this place, sticking out like a sore thumb.
What are you hiding here? Who are you harboring?
There's one right here. A ghost from the past. Suspicious.
Is it you? Have you returned with the incomplete duty of the past, only to abandon it again?
But you are not even carrying a true sword.
Leave him alone! Shouldn't the Royal Guard's top priority be to find the assassin—
Oh.
Trying to change the topic is not an appropriate tactic, Lieutenant.
Hand over the spy.
So you have reasons to believe the spy who let the assassin into the palace is hiding here.
Fine. But I don't know who this spy you're looking for is. Give me time, and I'll get to the bottom of it—
My time is limited, Lieutenant.
If you are unable to give me the answer I want, I shall carry out my mission in the most expedient manner.
It will not take too much effort to clear this place.
Clear? Like how the Fourth Army cleared those miners?
You are confounding justice and injustice.
I'm not questioning your intent. But how can you guarantee that your actions are appropriate, that the source of your information wasn't subject to any misdirection?
It's not just the vulnerable, the outsiders and Infected whom you scorn and suspect. There are also survivors and witnesses to the Grand Duchess's crimes!
You're acting on your own in such an important matter. How can you be sure you're not being deceived into making the wrong decision?
Because we do not.
We are only weapons, extensions of the tsar's hands.
Weapons do not measure or judge. In the hands of the Royal Guard, cause does not lead to effect, only wordless bloodshed.
Eloysius realizes that she has made a fatal mistake, treating the demonic creation before her as a being of reason and emotion—
As for you...
Tell me, Lieutenant.
What exactly are you doubting?
The stench of Dominion rapidly fills the space.
It brings fear and spreads despair, as is its natural order—
Only when she sees a figure suddenly appear in the way that she realizes her sheathe is empty.
The one who took her sword was so fast that her eyes could hardly follow. A flash of steel, and the spreading darkness is beaten back
Wha—
She hardly felt the flow of Originium Arts. The drawing of the sword alone was enough to repel the Royal Guard briefly.
Even a ceremonial sword with hardly any practical purpose.
It seems recent circumstances have driven even your kind to desperation.
Otherwise, your kind would never have taken direct action in Grypherburg, wasting time on chasing uncertain leads.
At the very least, it has not happened for decades, not since the Great Rebellion.
...You cut open the Dominion. You—
The Armies have never truly stood together with the Royal Guard. It seems that their counters against the demonic and eldritch remain effective.
Futile struggle.
Are you any different? It has been a long time since the last Royal Guard was punished for acting without authorization.
His exile to the Far North was upheld, even though it was demonstrated that the individual in question had merely misjudged the situation out of concert for the tsar's safety.
As far as I know, he never returned to Grypherburg. Perhaps he still roams the blizzards of Sami, pursued by his erstwhile comrades as a calamity—
Failure is unacceptable. We are the ones who exiled him, not His Imperial Majesty!
Suspicion has already formed. Many would be glad to see you further alienated from the tsar. Yet you yourselves are in no position to respond openly.

Though you find yourself out of favor with the tsar, you could not point your swords towards him, and so you have engaged in one atrocity after another... Simonch, Chernobog... and others that have remained unknown.
What do you think you know—
Tell me, Blade...
Do your kind know that you are taking a gamble again?
...The last clown who toyed with words has already been put to the torch.
Do you want to follow in his example?
I'm afraid threats don't work on me.
You said I'm a ghost from the past. But I may not always remain that way, if it becomes necessary—though I would prefer that things did not come to that.
And I will draw my sword for everyone in this building under the protection of Rhodes Island.
A thousand times and more, if I have to.
Until those like you are repelled, or until I can no longer stand.

You abandoned Ursus, yet you claim to protect her people.
Hypocrisy, foolishness...
Conceit!
You can deny what I say all you want... but I don't think you'll gamble.
Even if it's betting that you can cleanse this place before I kill you.
You don't want Ursus to lose another Blade.
We'll see how long your resolve lasts.
Lieutenant.
As terror grows distant, the young Imperial Guard finally rediscovers her voice.
...Go on.
I will give you time. However...
Whether to stand with the empire, or continue to associate yourself with her traitors and enemies...
I want to see the answer the next time we meet.
Your Imperial Highness, the Messenger has returned, three days earlier than expected.
Shall I show her in?
Please do.
Elisaveta stands up and pushes the unread report to one side out of habit.
The tea has already cooled, bitter brown sediment gathering at the bottom. She knocks the cup lightly with her finger, but it makes no sound, as though she is knocking on a solid object.
Outside the door, the servant seems to be talking to someone, but the conversation is muffled and indistinct, unlike the clearly intelligible words a moment ago.
She begins walking towards the door.
Applewood continues to burn in the black stone fireplace, but the fire is no longer cracking. Even the fire itself begins to grow dull, blending into the surrounding black.
The darkness flows towards Elisaveta, shrouding the surrounding walls in black.
Ilyusha.
Yes, Your Imperial Highness.
If the Messenger has any concerns, she can come back tomorrow.
Bring me another cup of tea. Linden honey and lemon slices... just like old times.
As you wish.
The crack on the map that leads to Grypherburg, and the wriggling border lines...
What are you here to remind me for?
Evgeny Andrianov Kuznetsov will be judged. His defeat is imminent.
Oh? Perhaps he was too young, if he staked everything upon a game of unknowable odds, and wasted all his chips and margin on waiting.
But what does this have to do with me?
You concealed the death of a Royal Guard in your demesne, and assisted the Fourth Army in its attempt to hold Grypherburg hostage under the pretense of eliminating rebellious Infected.
You participated in the entire process.
Your Messenger has told me all I need to know. I even know how much funding and materiel you provided to Kuznetsov.
I've heard that such threats are simply a tactic you employ to reinforce your public image, in order to become the stuff of children's nightmares, a sword hanging above the people's heads.
Stalling will do you no good, Elisaveta Konstantinovna.
You do not call me by my patronymic now, the that shares a house with His Imperial Majesty.
Just because you're one of the tsar's last remaining blood kin does not protect you from being put on trial.
You may have picked the right side in the Great Rebellion, but that won't protect you forever.
I never thought so. I protected the young tsar at the time because it was the right thing to do. I did not seek any repayment or benefits.
I was and still am the Grand Duchess of the Far North, no more, no less. I have never sought anything else for myself.
The soldiers of the Far North have fought on the same side as you countless times in the war against the demons, but today I see you with my own eyes for the first time.
The Emperor's Blade... the Royal Guard.
Tell me, how could your kind have died at the hands of those feeble, frail Infected?
Your tea, Highness.
Three minutes, lemon and linden honey, as you requested.
Thank you, Ilyusha.
Your service is always impeccable. It reminds me of your sister...
Elisaveta.
Oh, I'm sorry, where were we? Ah, yes, your colleague who died in my jurisdiction—
Excuse me. If you were discussing this matter and its aftermath...
...Ilyusha?
I believe the full responsibility for this matter falls upon me.
Her Imperial Highness entrusted me with unfettered access to this place. I chose to go over her head and issue the blackout order to local governments ahead of time.
Ilyusha.
The tacit approval of the Fourth Army's actions was given during my conversation with their herald.
And the unanswered letters from Grypherburg were destroyed by these hands.
Her Imperial Highness knew nothing.
I said, you don't have to—
Did you think the tsar would believe your story?
I never thought you would stoop so low as to pass off your crimes on a servant, Elisaveta.
But you are still given the luxury of choice. You can choose to end your own life here and now, or face judgment in Grypherburg.
There is little time—
The slender servant suddenly pulls a short sword.
He points it at the impassive entity before him, then—
The Grand Duchess knew nothing.
Foolhardy.
Before the darkness consumes him, the servant suddenly turns the sword around and stabs himself in the chest.
I will... prove...
Ilyusha...
Fool. This proves nothing.
The Grand Duchess's expression does not change in the slightest, only a single trail of tear revealing her emotions.
She walks up to the dead servant and closes his eyes.
You're right. He was a foolish boy.
He was impatient. I told him there was another way, but he would not wait, even for a moment.
Elisaveta.
Shh...
You haven't answered my question.
But it doesn't matter anymore. I'll answer it for you. What could have killed a Royal Guard so easily, wiping him away like a speck of dust...?
You knew about the Yurodstvo—
'It is time, shaman.'
(Ancient Sami) 'Sovereign of the beyond—'
(Ancient Sami) 'The will torn from the void!'
(Ancient Sami) 'I implore, unbound—'
Elisaveta! You have colluded with the Sami in order to control the Yurodstvo—
From the summoning, from the blood, from the cold void, a strange shadow emerges from white into crimson, dominating reality.
A million faces, a million pairs of eyes.
Yurodstvo Gabrielus.
Indeed...
A piercing, low-frequency howl echoes in the air, which seems to be some kind of language, one which reality lacks the means to comprehend.
You are truly—
(Whispers) Finally... success.
There is no wind, and the only entrance is shut, but two pitch-black figures suddenly appear by the sides of the white monstrosity.
Seize it.
As they lunge at the target, the floor beneath its feet collapses, or rather, melts—
The Yurodstvo remains standing, seemingly oblivious to the threat.
Yurodstvo Gabrielus.
Ursus does not need you.
We do not need you!
No—!
The entity known as the 'Yurodstvo' begins to blur, splitting into countless overlapping silhouettes.
It murmurs, reaching out towards the only living thing here that is not a demonic creation—
The Grand Duchess.
Seeing the failure of the first attempt, the Royal Guards immediately switch position.
Black swords impale the Yurodstvo's flickering, warping torso. White and red peel off to reveal a deep, transparent circle.
The howling does not cease.
No, no...
...The Yurodstvo is suspected to have anchored its identity as a family member of one of the miners.
...Miner's child... family of four. The father and mother were executed in 1096, and the grandmother committed suicide soon after. She is the only one left in the household.
She was amongst the miners who escaped. It must be her.
It seems that a traumatic reaction, or desperate pursuit of some kind of emotion, is sufficient to anchor the Yurodstvo in our reality.
Auntie Elisabeth—Auntie Elisabeth!
Where are my apple trees? Why were they replaced with other trees?
Fedya hasn't come. He spends all day staring blankly at mother's bedroom, or crying by himself. If he finds out that the apple trees are gone—
Oh, my dear Nastya.
The apple trees have gotten a terrible illness. They had to be replaced with other trees that could survive there...
The 'rust sickness'? Like mother?
...No, it's not the same. Your mother will get better.
People don't get 'rust sickness'. It's just a common cold. She'll get better.
'Just a common cold'?
...What?
If it's just a common cold...
Why did she grow so thin and frail? Why did she never wake up?
Who are you—
What are you saying?
Perish.
No.
No, no, no! I will not permit it!
It was Nastya—the poor girl no one cared about!
You used her, only to abandon her. This time, I will not allow it—
Come back, Anastasia! Come back to me, and never leave again!
Anastasia—
(Ancient Sami) 'Fire and blood, my wishes upon ye—'
—Elisaveta! What... what have you done?!
This is wrong... we have failed! Retreat! Retreat!
Are you... Anastasia? Or...
'You look exactly like your mother, down to the scent of bitter almonds.' That is what she wanted to say, but she could not say it.
The taste of blood fills her throat. Elisaveta gazes at the miracle before her, forgetting to even breathe.
Time passes second by second. No one dares be the first to act.
Ursus...
...does not need an unruly Yurodstvo, nor a princess who never existed.
Elisaveta, you have declared war upon all of Ursus.
...Anastasia.
Shall we help them?
Help these poor madmen and grant them the blessing of pain, those people who wanted to hurt you, control you, make you disappear!
Grant them this blessing, until they no longer struggle. Then, they will realize—
Auntie...
I'm here, I'm here, my dear Nastya!
...Auntie.
As you wish.
She looks up fervently at everything. Yet the smile is concocted, as if there is nothing reflected in her eyes that could make herself happy.
The monster now known as Anastasia raises her hand slowly, pointing behind Elisaveta.
I grant you life.
And grant you death.
Gabrielus, your duty—
Accept it.
The Royal Guards show no fear. They do not attempt to dodge or flee, allowing themselves to be consumed by the asymmetric shadow, tearing apart their humanoid forms—
The dripping blackness constantly crushed and reconstructed...
Until it is filled and replaced by something else entirely.
Recompute, Zeroth Order Oil Tank.
Set lifeform entropy to minimum... yeah, forget about the complicated stuff for now. Just simulate ideal conditions.
Data fitting failure.
That doesn't work either...
Zeroth Order Oil Tank, log data...
Attempt 2068...
...Still unsuccessful.
What do we do, Kal'tsit...?
You said Rhodes Island would do just fine without you...
...You damn liar.
Kal'tsit! Kal'tsit—wait!
What's up with all those confidential files that you hid? I couldn't understand a word of it.
So you saw them.
Don't pay too much heed to them. They can be unsealed when the time comes. You have plenty of time to study them.
Don't gloss over it. What's up with you handing me full authority over Rhodes Island?
I want to make this an official request.
When trouble comes to Rhodes Island, you will be the one whom the Doctor and Amiya count on, not just in your capacity as chief engineer.
Not as engineer? What else can I do?
You see how much Amiya has grown, and you know how smart the Doctor is. How am I supposed to help—
I have no doubt about Amiya's leadership, the Doctor's decisions, or the skills of the elite operators.
But these are not enough, if Rhodes Island is to become a safe harbor, a home for many people.
With everyone carrying a heavy responsibility, Rhodes Island needs someone who can give strength to others.
Vision is a rare gift, but so is being unperturbed by challenges.
That is your gift, Closure. Nobody does it better than you.

Hm...
Hey, wait a second, you're just calling me short-sighted, aren't you?
You're trying to dump all the work on me because you think I'm a pushover!
I can't promise I won't develop a temper like yours, if I take on that much work.
Well, if you're not willing to take on the responsibility, I'll have to go with my backup plan—
Wait a second!
Look, I promise I'll do my best to help the Doctor and Amiya...
But tell the truth, please—you haven't been yourself ever since you came back from Londinium. We can all tell.
If you're really tired, go and take a long vacation, but stop talking like you won't be around anymore.
Tell me the truth: What sort of future are you planning for?
I'm not making preparations out of pessimism for the future. I'm just hoping Rhodes Island will be in a position to deal with anything that happens.
Rhodes Island will not stop because of the loss of any one person.
You're always cold as a robot, but now I wish you really were one. It wouldn't be so hard to bring you back, if you were.
How am I supposed to put you together from this bunch of data?
I don't know how long I can keep going, if you don't come back, Kal'tsit...
Arrrrgggghhh! My head hurts!
I'm hungry. I should get something to eat...

Is everyone sleeping? No one sneaking in extra shifts, right?
Raidian's door is locked...
Mon3tr forgot to close hers?
...She sure sleeps in an interesting way.
Amiya... Doctor?

opts: Can't sleep?

lines.x: (Nods)

opts: You saw something terrible tonight.
Are you afraid you'll have nightmares?

lines.x:
Stop treating me like a child, Doctor...
Mm, I know you're just joking.
Well... I still have dreams about Dr. Kal'tsit and Theresa... they're not nightmares.
You're not going to bed yet?

opts: I'm worried about you.
I'm worried about what's to come.

lines.x: Oh... I guess it's my turn to comfort you.
It's alright. We can chat if you can't sleep... seems like it's been a long time since we've had time to talk in quiet like this.

opts: We've been very busy.
You've had a lot on your plate.

lines.x: I'm not as worried about myself as I'm worried about the other operators.
We haven't fully recovered from what happened to the ship, and a lot has happened in the meantime... now, we have another dilemma in front of us.
I'm worried that people might not pull through. I want to do more for them, but I don't know how...

opts: You've done so much already.
They see you as a leader they can trust.
You've given a lot of people strength.

lines.x: Really? I hope you're not saying this just to make me happy...
But... I want to believe that I'll at least be someone you can rely on.
Doctor... do you think we can trust Chairman Witte?

opts: I trust him.
I'm not sure.
I don't trust him.

lines.x: I recall that Chairman Witte was a proponent of peace five years ago.
But he could not stop the tragedy that happened in the Far North mines... a tragedy that may yet repeat itself.
He's obviously keeping a lot from us.
I understand his position, but the hidden mysteries of Zelgrad remain unsettling.
But you're still confident that we can work with him to mutual benefit.

opts: The situation in Ursus is complex.
The Zelgrad Sarcophagus is the key.
