The research here will have implications beyond Ursus's borders.

lines.x: I understand that we're dealing with a critical issue.
I keep thinking... how many things like this has Dr. Kal'tsit dealt with before?
What does she think about, when she faces these decisions?

opts: It must be very hard.
She must be very strong.

lines.x: Mm...
I'm trying to shoulder the responsibility, but sometimes I can't help thinking, if only Dr. Kal'tsit were here...
Doctor... actually, I'm beginning to have doubts.
At Chernobog and Londinium, we had a clear goal, an enemy to overcome... but who is our enemy this time?
We can't stop the fallout of Originium exhaustion, or the deaths brought about by internal strife. People hate each other for reasons beyond Oripathy and race.
I can't help but feel... it's the land itself that we're fighting.

opts: Maybe that's what Rhodes Island has always been about.
Idealism means fighting this great land itself.

lines.x: I brought this up because I ran into... an unusual girl. She's Cautus too, maybe even younger than me.
She asked whether there was any meaning to what we do, if we know we can't save everyone.
I said yes, but I can't deny... sometimes, it makes me anxious to see that our dream is so far away.
And it's been getting more frequent...

opts: We can't allow the meaning of our actions to be defined by a distant outcome.
It's the right thing to believe in our dreams. That's why we do what we do.
Fear of failure is inevitable—
But it's not an excuse for inaction.
In any case...
I choose to believe in hope.
I believe that Terra has a future.

lines.x: That's the kind of answer I expect to hear from you.
Just like the stories you used to tell me when I was little. Every story has a different fantasy, but in the end, all of them—
Oh... but you don't remember them, do you...?

opts: Then it's your turn to tell them to me.

lines.x: Mm-hm...!
The night is cold. Amiya cuddles up to you.
I understand. I understand it all.
You love life and believe in hope. It is your nature, the bond that ties us together.
But how could you forget...?

lines.st: Hope that can never be realized is nothing more than a lie.

lines.x: ...I'm afraid I have to stop you.
The Marshal has ordered strict secrecy over New Lab Six's research. Even an inspection of research progress—
You are Alita Valueva? Director of this lab?
...Yes, sir.
Then you know that the Marshal has given her son, Anatoliy Svetlanov, full authority over the Kushkina Project.
And you must know that the Generalik has reached the end of his patience with your lack of progress.
I have already explained to the Marshal that energy supplies have been highly inconsistent since the beginning of the Originium vein crisis.
As the research progresses, its demand for energy grows... just as one cannot make butter from water, experiments cannot continue without the right conditions.
On the unauthorized transfer of energy—
That is exactly what I'm trying to say—
I've submitted a report on the matter to the Marshal, and personally overseen the shutdown of potential channels. It will not happen again.
Please explain it to the Generalik. I would be happy to submit a copy of the report for the Marshal to him.
Ah... I'm sure he would be very interested.
The Generalik's temperament is unlike the Marshal's. He wants to see New Lab Six's effectiveness and loyalty.
See those in your husband's lab, for example... the smallest of leaks has already ensured that they will never have the trust of the First Army again.
Do not repeat their mistakes.
Give her the letter.
Yes, sir.
Sir, this is...
Data provided by a friend of the Marshal's. The Generalik has instructed me to give it to you, so that the lab can improve upon Kushkina according to the concepts contained within.

Also, the test animal on the loose is causing panic amongst some of the civilians. The Generalik would like you to resolve this matter immediately, or at the very least find out the cause... do you understand?
Alita takes a deep breath. Her fingers touch the letter sealed with Grypherburg's standard Hippogryph seal, and nods without hesitation, suppressing her doubts.
I understand... please tell the Generalik that I will do my duty and complete the goals as quickly as possible.
Phew—
They're gone. You can come out now.
Thank you, professor. They would have been suspicious if they saw me.
I'm the one who should thank you, Marat.
You're taking a huge risk, helping me look for data while acting as the Army's science consultant. I don't know how to thank you.
I'm not just doing it for you. I'm curious why they're suddenly recruiting so many Infected all of a sudden, myself.
Did you find anything?
Yes.
They're using those Infected to provide 'energy' for the project.
Are you saying—
In the literal sense of the word.
Passphrase.
'Snow made from iron does not burn.'
You're three minutes late. Be careful next time. The ones inside are not as well-tempered as we are.
Not much we can do about it. There are fewer and fewer usables, and harder to acquire the goods. The higher-ups would rather those who are in less serious condition keep working.
They'll come down on us if quota's not met.
We should worry about ourselves. We'll end up like those in the truck if we get infected ourselves.
What's that sound—
Huh? I didn't hear anything.
Well, it's about time this old bucket got an overhaul.
Keep moving, don't waste time.

lines.loc: The Walls, City of Zelgrad Jan 21, 1102, 09:03

lines.x: Phew... that was close!
I can't get any closer with all that jamming... not after I almost lost No.128.

opts: Did the drone get anything?

lines.x: Let me see... no, there's too much noise.
The drones start acting up within about 1km of this area. They can still fly, but real-time video is inoperable, and other preloaded functions are also disabled.
There's something really weird about this wall!
Before the Rhodes Island team lies a tall, grey wall that stretches as far as the eye could see. The marks that rain has left upon it glow metallic blue under the grey skies.
Closure looks up at the wall that blocks out half the sky. Its size and weight is oppressive, even at a distance.
Good thing the patrols don't come around here, and we haven't seen any other locals approach. Do they all pretend the wall doesn't exist?
It stretches out from downtown. Who could fail to see it?
Military-grade ECM equipment is deployed throughout the wall. It far exceeds what a normal military facility requires to prevent accidental trespassing.
It's strange.

opts: If the First Army is determined to stop cooperating with the legislature...
Then it's no wonder.

lines.x: We'll be spending our entire stay dealing with this equipment, if we don't think of something.

opts: Raidian?
What's the matter?

lines.x: I have some discoveries, or should I say, hypotheses.
I tried to use my Arts this morning, focusing on specific human signal bands to reduce workload.
I thought about giving up after several attempts came up empty before I discovered a band that periodically disappears before reappearing.
It occurs at regular intervals, with two iterations up to this point.
Did you see anything go through the wall?

opts: A truck went through.
But we didn't see what the payload was.

lines.x: I remember it. The searchlight followed it without setting off any alarms. I thought I was lucky, but it seems strange now that I think of it.
If the curfew was imposed in order to covertly transport something behind the wall—

opts: It's very possible.
It may be the only way for us to sneak in.

lines.x: If we want to use it to sneak in, we could lay in wait along its path.
Come back, Doctor. We need to plan our next steps.
This time, I need to be present.
Doctor!
You said you found an abnormal patient? Is he—
The doctor shakes her head before Tonya could finish.
You came sooner than I thought, Tonya, but...
See for yourself.
The doctor lifts the quarantine tarp and reveals a body covered by white cloth.
Lifeless like a marble statue.
Then, she lifts the cloth and folds it up...
Tonya's nails dig into her palm. She has seen death plenty of times, but never one as terrible as this...
She sees the familiar face, the soul long gone from it, but not the slightest sign of pain or struggle upon it.
The brow is relaxed, the eyelids closed, the slightly curved lips highlighting the lines of age, freezing everything into what appears to be a benevolent smile.
Then, the neck, the shoulders, the torso... Tonya's eyes go wide.
Bright crystals extrude from the pale skin, reflecting a yellowish glow in the ceiling lamp's light.
No, no, doctor...
It's not the same as what happened to my sister...
A quiet sigh answers her in the empty operating room.
The symptoms are indicative of an acute Oripathy onset.
But he had demonstrated similar symptoms as your sister when he first came. If your sister was in the initial stages, he was in the final stages.
Could the illness be... with Oripathy...
But people with Oripathy don't die so peacefully!
You're right. Oripathy patients often experience unimaginable pain when they die, as their bodies disintegrate.
I performed a comprehensive check before you came...
His vocal cords were not swollen, nor were there any scratch marks on his body. His muscles were relaxed, with no sign of painful spasms prior to death, nor any sign of disintegration...
But all these questions do not change the fact that he died from Oripathy.
This points to the possibility that his condition, and whatever is affecting your sister, is simply a variant of Oripathy.
Tonya was no longer listening. Her ears are ringing, and her eyes refuse to avert their gaze from the smile on the dead's face.
It is neither release from suffering, nor hope for the end, only a numb comfort.
His consciousness, his soul, all his emotions towards the land, even fear itself, have been soothed over by a gentle yet irresistible force.
And the only clue, the last hope to discover the truth about the strange illness, is gone with the patient's passing.
...What's that sound, doctor?
What sound? I don't hear anything.
I think I hear my sister crying... is she calling to me?
Look at me, Tonya. Your sister is in isolation. I keep my eye on her every day and hum lullabies to put her to bed. She'll be fine.
She's still sleeping. Children her age need sleep to recover. Whatever you're hearing, it's not her... take a deep breath.
No, doctor, it's not that...
It was raining heavily that night. I ran through three streets to bring her to you. She was so light, like an empty basket...
But her head, pressed against my forehead, was burning, so hot it made my tremble...
I still don't know what she's sick with. It wouldn't even leave me with a speck of hope!
Why did it do this to her, to us...
What did we do wrong?
Tonya!
Go—
Doctor, we have to go! The soldiers have found this place! They're already downstairs. We'll need to take the emergency passage.
What about Nina?
In the incubator. Should we grab her?
...What's going on with Tonya?
Give me a hand and get her up. Nina cannot leave the incubator at this time. We can only pray they'll show mercy to a child.
Leave the rest. We can come back for it.
So light...
What about this one?
We have to leave him.
He might even buy us some time.
Let's go.
I left a sign for the others in the operating room.
Gah... they got away again.
Doesn't matter. Our primary mission is not to arrest people. They always get wind of things, like those 'musbeasts' in the underground layers.
Found anything other than the kid?
No.
Did you search every room thoroughly?
I—
—Found it!
There's a body in the operating room, but...
Take it anyway.
Be careful not to knock off any pieces.
I'm taking these meds too.
There's no date on them, who knows if they work at all. But suit yourself.
Better than nothing.
Doing this stuff every day... I don't want to wait for that factory scrip khuinya to get my sleeping pills.
That one again?
Yeah.
Something happened during fresh-air time? Refused to kneel, or—
Offered to take punishment for the others when boss was punishing the Infected.
Again... carry the suka up.
Hey, still breathing?
Zhopa, they're gonna kill someone if they go on like this.
The Generalik wants the Infected alive...
Tell the tupoi Luzhin to explain to the Generalik. I'm sure he could spin a bunch of flowery words, considering it was the Generalik who stuck him in our squad to begin with.
Watch your words. Luzhin is our superior officer, for now at least. The First Army's—
Honor? Discipline? As if there's any of that left in the First Army. Blyat, screw that svolotsch Generalik...
Bleh, keep an eye on 'em, and call a medic at any signs of trouble—those pizdets animal doctors do nothing well except clean up dead bodies...
But I bet this suka will last the night.
Shouldn't have defied us, eh?
I can take it... leave the others alone.
Hey, you asked for it. Don't say we didn't warn you.
I saw bandages on your arm while you were carrying me, and that wound on your head...
Did you defy your own superior, Ratkov?
Don't push your luck. I'm only here because I was ordered to keep an eye on you. Don't presume to question the Generalik just because we've talked a couple of times.
Sorry...
I just happened to see similar marks on you, which made me think... perhaps we're not so different after all.
The youth fights the pain to take out a packet with blood-stained fingertips, dangling it in front of the soldier with a trembling hand.
What are you doing?
For you. Medicine powder made from a plant that grows only on the Northern Tundra. Works wonders on wounds...
How did we not find it when we searched you?
Survival wisdom that Ursus taught us... take it. I have enough for myself.
I know this medicine.
What?
I grew up in Zavorsk. One time I got a gaping gash on my leg that almost reached the bone. My grandfather poured this medicine over the wound, and it only took one night for the wound to close.
My family gave me a bunch when I enlisted. It came in handy in the two years that I spent on the border fighting bandits, before I was transferred to the First Army.
I didn't expect to see it here.
Zavorsk... it's near the Far North...
Yes. I haven't heard from my family ever since the Fourth Army's insurrection.
Most of my companions came from the Northern Tundra.
If I can meet up with them, I could ask them about your family—
There's no need.
I'm already breaking rules by talking to you like this.
I have to go. I can put in a request if there's anything you need.
You said your grandfather used that medicine on you.
The one who gave me the medicine said that only lumberjacks and hunters who live in the Northern Tundra forests know how to make it.
Your grandfather—
He was a lumberjack. So was my father.
While you joined the First Army. Good...
I know many children of lumberjacks. At least you aren't learning how to bury other children of lumberjacks.
The soldier's shoulders twitch, as though he had been whipped.
You know how many soldiers have claimed those forests for themselves, backed by the rich and powerful.
They beat up and expelled those who lived in the forests, forcing them to leave the land which their ancestor had always lived, becoming homeless refugees, or willing slaves.
No doubt your father and grandfather will be proud of you, seeing you grow up strong and healthy, escaping such cruel fate with your family...
What are you trying to say?
My question for you is—whose son are you?
Your grandfather, the lumberjack from Zavorsk...
Did he heal your leg so that you can bend it to the oppressors, or stand with dignity like a true son of Ursus?
I have no requests for you to pass on. I only ask that you remember that you are a child of Ursus, like me, like all of us.
We will never bow to those who wield the whip. We fight for everyone who should not be whipped.
If the day comes when you want to find out about your father and grandfather, I... *cough* *cough*—
Save your strength...
I'll pretend I didn't hear any of that. Whatever you wanted to say, save it.
Wake up, boss.
Mm... what's going on...
Bozhe moi, your wounds... those monsters—!
Doesn't matter... how did you get out? I thought we were all locked up.
All the doors got unlocked for some reason.
We came to find you as soon as we got out. No soldiers along the way. Maybe something's gone wrong. Anyway, it's our chance!
But can you move? Your injuries—
Don't worry about me...
We don't have a lot of time, no matter whatever's happened with the Army. We need to move immediately.
Here, hold onto me.
Our people are all here... what's going on?
It's you—
I talked to my mates. The guys on duty will leave a gap. You have ten minutes to get out.
Thank you so much...
Ratkov, If I hear anything about your family—
Forget it. We all know it's a long shot.
What will you do? The general will undoubtedly punish you after we leave.
We will not submit so easily. Anatoliy no longer deserves our loyalty.
There is considerable discontent towards his behavior in the Army. He will pay for his outrages.
We've talked enough. Go, and don't waste this chance.
...Take care, Ratkov.
I will remember you, son of a Zavorsk lumberjack.
Hm...
You're awake?
Where are we? Nina—
The soldiers came to the clinic. We only had time to get you out.
We couldn't take your sister because she couldn't leave the incubator in her current state. I'm sorry.
Ugh—
Headache? It's normal after blacking out like that.
Is Nina still there? Did they take her? I have to—
I went back to the clinic when you were out cold.
...Doctor?
Nina wasn't there. They took her. The good news is that they took the incubator too. The bad news is... we don't know where they took her.
I understand you want to find her, and I'll do what I can to help, but—
Promise me this, Tonya. You have to stay strong, even if you don't find her... the rest of your family need you. They look up to you.
You want to know what you can do? There's always one thing, and only one thing—
Find more evidence.
Doctor, you're sure that Kirill had the same symptoms as Nina when he first came into your care, only more serious?
If you believe me. There was a Cautus who could use healing Arts, who might have eased his pain at my request. No one else came into contact.
The Oripathy progressed rapidly. And what happened to him doesn't look like the result of pain relief.
Then I must find more evidence... and Nina.
I must find Nina...
What are you going to do?
What I had to do.

lines.loc: The Walls, City of Zelgrad Jan 22, 1102, 00:25

lines.x: Target lost.
Target has left the surveillance area. Drone acquisition lost.
That means it's now within one klick of the wall, near your position.
The patrols have left. There should be a gap of about ten minutes along the road.
I'm coming over, Amiya.
Got it!
Watch out for the searchlights.
Do you see a grey vehicle?
Not yet!
Wait, I think—

opts: It's coming.
Approaching from behind on the right side.

lines.x: I'm not there yet! Wait for me—
We haven't made a move yet. Stay safe, Closure.
I see it. Looks like a modified Infected tractor for use in the wilderness.
I've heard of military tractors ending up with the Infected after retirement. Not sure I've ever seen it go the other way.
We'll have to get closer to find out.
You'll fall out of comms if you get any closer.
Let's go in and figure it out from there.
Very well. I'll reestablish communications once you're inside.
Raidian out.
Guh...
The radio always goes out around these parts. Nothing to do when waiting for the door to open.
Didn't they say they were building a new base station? How's the signal still so lousy—
...From this vantage point, we can't even see how the door opens, or what sort of security measures are present.
We may have to get on the tractor before it gets swarmed by patrols and go inside with it.

opts: I'm not sure I could make the jump...
It's a little high.

lines.x: No worries, I got you!
I think I'll need help too.
I can take Closure too.
Counting on you, Mon3tr.
(Hushed) Quiet now and stay focused. Wait for my signal.
Why's it taking so long for the door to open today, bratan?
Who are you calling bratan? I'm your baba.
You'll wait if you want to go in. They're still checking your creds.
Wasn't you here last night, baba.
Yeah, they reassigned everybody to the suburban factories. We're on three shifts a day now, don't even get to sleep.
Alright, you can go in—
*cough*—*cough*!
What's that—
...Woah, we got a lunatic trying to attack the wall!
Attack on the wall! Need backup at Zone A! Repeat, need backup at Zone A!
There was an explosion, someone's trying to force their way through—
There's someone else here? Did we luck into unexpected help?
No time to think about it now!
Raidian has rendezvoused with us. Let's use the chaos to get on the tractor—
—Close the door! No one gets in!
Attention—
Crossbows ready!
W-Wait! Don't point those weapons at me! I'm just delivering stuff!
Ugh, I'm gonna miss my next stop—
Hold it!
I'm sorry, I-I really can't afford to be late!
Looks like a twenty-four-man squad with potential reinforcements coming up. We need to get moving.
(Whispers) Come, Doctor!
Doctor! Give me your hand!

opts: I'm trying—

lines.x: —That one's trying to get inside! Fire!

opts: Give me a hand!

lines.x: For an instant, your cries seem to be drowned in the noise.
Before your hands grasp anything in the darkness, you see a somewhat familiar figure in protective gear run towards you.
Stand firm.
The figure charges at you and lifts you up, until you manage to find Mon3tr's hand and get on the edge of the tractor.
Then it disappears before you have time to react.

opts: Who...?
Thank you—

lines.x: You turn around to see the figure in protective gear clumsily trying to climb the tractor, only to fall back onto the ground—
Easy prey for the soldiers rushing in from a distance, crossbows raised.
Look out—
Closure—
Look out!
Closure's drones manage to fend off the first wave of attacks, even with their capabilities restricted to flight.
But their limitations quickly show as she attempts to shield the stranger from the same attacks.
The plasma shield doesn't work either! Damn this thing!
Look oooooouuuuutttt!
Over here. Take your drone.
Stay behind me.
Is that a blast shield? But the material—
Why did you stay behind? You already got on the tractor!
You helped the Doctor, didn't you? Besides, some people have a knack for acting before thinking... just think of me as being their rear guard.
The door's shut, but at least they got in—
Push forward! Surround them and take them in!
Ugh—!
I got you. Looks like we'll have to run in the opposite direction.
Hey, you—are you Infected?
It's complicated, but vampires don't normally get Oripathy—
...I have no idea. You're the first Sarkaz I've seen...
Right now, though, it's a good thing.
Good? Why?
Hopefully, it means we'll only end up in a police station—
More reinforcements? Okay, NOW I'm done!
Wait, I don't think it's—
What did you say?
Do your drones still work? Can you use it to draw them to the other side?
I want to check—
—Bravo, turn around and attack the intruders!
Good, they're not on the same side. I don't know who they are, but we gotta run towards them!
Beats getting caught by the First Army.
They're distracted. Run!
You're—
You think there's time for self-introductions?
Come with me if you want to live.
They're still hot on our tails. We're outside the jamming area now, I can draw their attention with a drone.
Try.
Well, try is the only thing I can do—
No. 6 ready, max speed, high visibility mode—
*huff*... *pant*...
That should distract some of them...
Hey, are you okay? I'm taking off your mask—
What's your name? Are you hurt?
Me? I'm Tonya...
Nice name. The drones are off. Let me see if you're hurt. I know a thing or two about first-aid.
I'm just... cold...
You're losing blood. Did a bolt hit you?
I don't know...
I think... I've seen the mark on his back before...
Reunion...
Forget about that for now! There's a wound on your leg.
Take this.
What is it?
Medicine. Apply it and grab on—
I'm taking another route.
What's different about this one?
Narrower and more remote.
But not narrow enough that their vehicles can't get in.
Correct, but it'll buy us some time.
How many did the drone draw away?
A quarter, at most. They're probably just going after No.6 to make sure there are no loose ends.
We're dead if we can't shake at least half of them before they set up roadblocks ahead.
I-I'll think of something!
You'd better. We need to stop and find the entrance to the underground layer.
It's safer underground.
Wait, stop—we can't go around!
There's someone ahead!
A miner?
But not one of us. You're—
We met in the apartments.
This is no place to chat. Come with me if you trust me.
We found a place underground—
Let's go. We have people on our tail.
You all know each other?
Take her from the vehicle. I'll drive it off to somewhere hidden.
There's no need! We'll go together. I'll have a drone hide it for you.
It'll last until morning, at least. Let's go.
The scouts have returned!
No movement from the Army after we shook them. Rumor has it they're still trying to figure out what happened. Maybe it'll give us a breather.
We can't let our guard down. Plant some sentries amongst the local workers during the day to keep an eye on the Army.
What about the injured worker?
She's fine... the one who came with her is taking care of her.
(Whisper) You take care of the sentries. I need to talk to this gentleman.
I'm afraid the place is a little cramped. We don't have much space here.
It's alright. Our people have settled in. We appreciate what you've done very much... but I don't know your name yet.
...Ivan Tulin. We came from the Northern Tundra mines, seeking refuge.
It's clearly not the first time you've done something like this. I would have thought you were trained soldiers, if you weren't wearing miner clothes.
You're a fine leader.
They're fine people. Death has stalked us from the Northern Tundra all the way to Zelgrad. We had to learn how to survive, fast.
Now, if I might know your name as well...
I'm Red. We call ourselves... Reunion.
Reunion? Do you mean—
People have been talking about your exploits in Londinium. I'd heard you'd returned to southern Ursus.
I often told them about it while taking them southward...
Most of my group are Infected miners. I see hope in their eyes when I tell them stories about you.
I didn't expect to run into you here.
Did you come to Zelgrad because you heard they've started taking in Infected?
We had hope. But I needed to find out why Zelgrad was doing it.
No point in hiding it. We sensed something was off the moment we set foot in the city.
The military-assigned housing was suspicious, then we heard a civilian clinic was working with the Army. We suspected that they were conducting experiments on the Infected.
We wanted to find out the truth. Many of us have already given their lives to do so...
...I'm sorry for your loss.
Based on our understanding of Ursus, changes to Infected policy do not happen simply out of the kindness of some aristocrat's heart.
We need to learn more about what's behind it.
Perhaps we all have questions for the two ladies over there.
In a corner, Closure carefully puts an old jacket over Tonya, who is still unconscious, her lips drying up.
I should get some water... hang in there, Tonya.
Closure feels someone touch her shoulder and turns around.
Tulin's hand is holding a brown water bottle with gentle eyes, Red standing beside.
Oh, Tulin—sorry, I heard the others call you that...
It's alright. I'm glad to help.
You and Red have already helped a lot. Thank you so much.
Since the situation's kind of desperate right now, I'm afraid I'll only be able to repay you once we're out of the woods...
That's not what I mean. But I would like to know why you were there, if possible.
Well...
I'm afraid I can't talk about it.
It's not that I have any suspicions about you, but the operation I'm participating in is top-secret.
Is it because of me?
No point denying it. I saw the surprise and wariness on your face when you saw me. You recognized me, or should I say, you recognized Reunion.
How did you know I was with Reunion?
Besides the symbol on your back, it was the Arts you used to get through, and your blade.
I've... read the files.
Files? Who are you?
There's no need to ask any more, Red.
Our friend here is from Rhodes Island. She goes by the name Closure.
Y-You're...
The Sarkaz straightens her back at the familiar face, breathing rapidly as she instinctively shields herself with her arm.
Talulah... I should have expected that you might be here when I saw Reunion members.
...I apologize, Closure.
I know Rhodes Island and I did not part on the best of terms.
What are you doing here? Were the Infected...
I heard about what happened in the Far North, and about Zelgrad...
I don't believe what Ursus is saying about these things, so I needed to know what they're doing to the Infected.
I expect that words alone will not change your mind, but Reunion is helping the workers here.
...I can't say I believe that's the only thing you're after...
But we agree that the walls of Zelgrad hide some kind of secret, not just about the Infected, but also something that I'm not at liberty to disclose.
If this is what Reunion is here for, I would say there is room for negotiation... I'll think about how to tell you, once this girl here gets better.
Thank you, Closure.
Thank you. For tonight, at least.
I guess I should give you some time to catch up. I'll go check on the sentry arrangements to make sure there's no mistake.
One moment, please.
Ivan Tulin... that's how you introduced yourself to Red.
May I talk to you in private?
I didn't expect to run into you here.
You know the name?
The words you wrote in the Northern Tundra mines have spread far and wide. I've had the fortune to read it... I was very touched.
I wanted to find your group... but circumstances did not permit it.
And then you went quiet, and people thought you were... I'm glad to see you here.
You're younger than I thought, though.
...I'm honored.
I want to ask... do you know a woman called Yelena?
Yelena told me she met a remarkable man when she was a guerilla in the Northern Tundra.
He told her stories about good people being oppressed... he wanted to teach them the meaning of resistance.
Then he bid farewell to the guerillas, because he had to cross the snowfields and journey across Ursus, in order to learn the ending of those stories.
I may need some help. What was Yelena like?
A white-haired Cautus... one of the most resolute warriors I've ever met.
I knew I would never forget her, the first time I saw her.
I know there are many honorable warriors in the Northern Tundra, but not all of them tell me their names... I'm sorry.
If your friend and I ever crossed paths, I hope it was good memories that I left behind.
Yes... the memories must have been precious.
Talulah... you are called, yes?
Yes.
I haven't heard much of the story associated with the name itself, but I have heard plenty about Reunion.
I suppose... it's not an entirely satisfying story.
I can't and I won't judge your group's resolve on rumors and hearsay. Now that we've met, however, I'm sure I'll have plenty of opportunities to know you.
Regardless, you have raised a banner that many can see. It's a great accomplishment.
Besides... I like the name 'Reunion'. We do need to unite our strength.
I believe we can walk together.
It's a pleasure to meet you, Talulah.
The youth removes gloves and extends a hand to Talulah, a rough hand covered in chilblains.
Talulah takes the hand.
It's a pleasure to meet you.
Where is Father?
He went out early in the morning, ma'am.
What about the butler?
He went out with Master Vasily.
It's been a long time since you were back, ma'am. At least take off your coat and cloak so I can wash them for you—
No need. I'm not staying, just coming back to grab something.
Neither Hellagur nor Vetochki have access to the treatment center's administrative files. Looks like I'll have to wait for Dur-nar to come back.
Father's seal should give access to the treatment center's roster and guest list. The study...
The lock was changed?
Marsha!
No, the servants don't have the key either... who is Father trying to keep out? Why didn't he tell me?
He never stopped me from entering the study, nor does he have a reason to suddenly—
—There's a guest, ma'am. Should I have her come in?
What?
From House Volkina, it seems.
The Duchess Volkina? The 'shadow vice-chairman'? I thought she never communicated with other nobles in private—
Oh, well...
Take her to the reception room.
I'll greet the guest on Father's behalf.
Would you like something to drink? I'm afraid options are more limited than you might find at other places. Father went out and you missed our afternoon tea time, so the stove was turned off.
The cup of tea on the table is untouched, if you would like.
No, thank you. I'm not visiting any other place, nor am I here for tea.
In that case, what word do you bring from Duchess Volkina?
I have a letter for Duke Gorchikov.
For Father? I will accept it on his behalf.
To tell the truth, I did not expect to see you here, Lieutenant Gorchekova.
My impression was that you do not come home often.
You know me so well? I'm starting to like you.
Let me tell you the truth as well. I'm opening this letter if I get my hand on it. You can choose to give it to me now, or give it to my father directly when he comes back.
I don't know why they have private dealings with each other, but such an honor is not necessarily a good thing for House Gorchikov.
Now that I know, I must prepare.
Hm.
Huh?
Her Highness said I was to give the letter to you if I saw you here, that it made no difference whether it was delivered to you or your father.
I was wondering. In rumors and gossip, you have always been Eloysius of the Imperial Guard, not Eloysius of House Gorchikov.
...I am both. I have never tried to distance myself from either.
It seems Her Highness was correct.
Rumors are but rumors. Family is family.
Of course, I—
Here you go. The Duchess Volkina awaits a response, from you or your father.
Eloysius clutches the letter. The wax seal on the envelope is hard and irregular, a distorted imprint that is simultaneously forceful yet careless.
Duchess Volkina has always paid little heed to these details that often become a topic of conversation in Grypherburg, living a unique lifestyle that is almost ascetic.
Perhaps this is why she oversees the Ursus Guard, ever the great city's steadfast defenders, aloof and unconcerned with relationships or conflicts.
As though she is living in a vacuum.
But who truly lives in a vacuum?
She slices the tattered wax seal and takes the letter from the envelope.
Marsha.
...Marsha!
Yes, ma'am?
Why was the lock to the study changed?
Master Vasily ordered it two weeks ago, to prevent break-ins, given the situation in the city.
Two weeks... was there a break-in?
No, but one cannot be too careful.
Were the window locks changed?
No, they weren't.
Good.
Ma'am?
Eloysius stuffs the letter into her pocket.
Wait for me outside the study. I need you to run an errand for me, for which I'll give you a token.
Go to Lunin Manor and send Lieutenant Platon Lunin an invitation in my father's name. He is a colleague of mine in the Imperial Guard, and I have something to discuss with him.
Take a car bearing House Gorchikov's coat of arms. Come back directly if he's not home. Do you understand?
It's important, and urgent.
Ma'am, the guest is here.
Bring him in.
You were looking for me, General—
He stops mid-sentence and turns to leave.
There are plenty of things that even my father can't do.
He can't give you what you want, Platon.
What do you think you know?
You're the sole heir to one of the most powerful houses in Deity Grypherburg. What do you know of rejection?
You've always gotten everything you wanted. All I'm asking for is an opportunity... yet you will not suffer even that.
Why shouldn't I seek my own path? Just because the Lunin name is a rung below yours?
Tell me...
...It's not what you think.
Take a look at this.
Eloysius hands over Duchess Volkina's letter.

lines.st: I'm afraid I must respectfully decline your request.
Reassigning officers at a sensitive time like this is likely to lead to speculation, and compromise the longstanding trust and partnership between the Imperial Guard and the Capital Ursus Guard.
On an individual level, a soldier should not be selective about their position, or the risks that come with it. Kindly communicate my opinion to Lieutenant Lunin.
The defense of the capital demands unity between the two forces, not separate agendas. I hope you will not allow a moment of weakness to fracture the defenses of Deity Grypherburg.
Signed, Duchess Valentina Ruslanovna Volkina

lines.x: I take it you didn't expect Marshal Volkina—Duchess Volkina to reject the request, even when it went through my father.
She is the commander of the Ursus Guard, but also one of the vice chairmen of the State Council. Don't you know that she and my father are not in the same faction?
Transferring from the Imperial Guard to the Ursus Guard used to be completely normal. She clearly refused because she suspected—
Suspected what? That you were a spy for my father, or for the Imperial Guard?
...I simply asked General Gorchikov for help. Am I not even allowed to do that, after you denied my application?
You know my father's military title is merely ceremonial, don't you?
And while you may think like a noble, believing that things that have been should always be, I don't think you're actually that stupid.
You think you're qualified to judge me just because you've been my superior officer for a year?
No, I'm assessing Platon Lunin, top student at the military academy.
I knew him, and I thought he would be like me, blyat...
Top student, as in always second behind someone who never shows up to the training grounds?
I already explained that I was not at school that year because I was accompanying Chairman Witte on his survey of Central Governorate.
I see. You're using your father's name to summon me so that you can insult me with this piece of paper and the past.
Insult you? No, no, you think too highly of yourself.
What's your point?!
Let me ask you again, Platon.
Why did you go to the Oripathy treatment center in Odoyev?
Where did you get those military supplies, and how have you taken advantage of the facility's acceptance and transfer of the Infected?
...So that is what you're after.
Fine. I was spying for the Grand Duchess. I went to the treatment center to find a chance to kill all the miners.
There. Happy?
No, I'm not happy.
Der'mo—
I really feel the military academy should work with intelligence agencies to teach a practical counterintelligence course based on real scenarios, rather than just do written exams.
It's second-rate, responding emotionally to questioning and trying to distract the interrogator with the most obvious undercover identity. I'm not happy with your answer.
I'll give you one last chance, Platon. For old times' sake.
Tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth, and I will ask Chairman Witte for leniency. I share responsibility for your mistake, after all. At least your family will be unscathed.
How noble, except for one problem...
Who's asking you to 'share responsibility'?
You're just speculating. You know those military supplies were clean, and the letter only proves that I asked General Vasily for help, nothing more.
You don't have any other evidence, and you won't find any. Whatever conjectures you have about my dealings with your father, about the treatment center, what's done is done—
Why are you still so obsessed?
I need to know the truth! I need to know—I need to know if you were the one who let the assassins in and helped them escape when they made the attempt on the Chairman's life!
I need to know what my father made you do—
Hah, I see you don't trust your father... guess what, your father doesn't trust you either.
He doesn't believe you will achieve anything with your sword. You were already beyond his control, long before the Far North Incident.
No, you couldn't have known his thoughts.
Couldn't I? He talked a lot, about you. Oh, old Vasily loved you alright, but his contempt of you was such that he would turn to the pro-war faction to protect you—
What did you say?!
You didn't know, did you? He prepared a way out for you through that treatment center, because he knew you were weak.
If you ask me, you should run away before everything goes to hell in the city, just like he arranged.

You see? There's nothing you can do, even if you know I was a spy. I'm not about to prostrate myself before the tsar to beg forgiveness, and you don't have the guts to take my head and claim the reward.
All we can do is exchange words like some third-rate talk show...
Ringing began to fill Eloysius's ears as soon as she heard the words 'turn to the pro-war faction'.
She tries to follow Platon's words by reading his lips, but finds it increasingly difficult to focus.
Turn to the pro-war faction... treatment center... a way out?
An intelligence contact point disguised as an Infected treatment center, payment made in supplies instead of cash...
All the threads lead to this place, sticking out like a sore thumb.
What are you hiding here? Who are you harboring?
What...
What did Father offer to the pro-war faction?
Hah, look at you now! So pathetic you're not even worth hating anymore.
Eloysius grabs Platon's collar—prim and proper, the uniform of a soldier, of the proud Imperial Guard.
The symbol of honor and duty.
Hvatit etogo breda, Platon! Tell me—
Tell me!
Why do you ask if you already guessed? I'm just following orders, as a soldier should.
You knew security measures were relaxed for the treatment center's patient transfers. You took advantage and let the assassins in—
...You've gone mad! All of you have gone mad!
Hah... you finally got it right, for once.
No...
You and I...
Hey, Eloysius.
You will come with me to see the Chairman and admit your crimes.
To hell I will. Unless your father sells me out, why would I betray him when you have no evidence?
Your father is much better at winning people over than you are, Elotta.
Don't make me do this, Platon—
You have another choice, but you won't take it.
On the hunting grounds, you always killed your prey in one blow, even when it was prepared in advance.
You don't have the stomach to torture me.
You... the Chairman is still alive, but...
Did you know that the Emperor's Blade showed up at the treatment center right after you left?
What?
You left plenty of loose ends, but the Royal Guard doesn't care. All they want is results. If—If there didn't happen to be someone there who can stop them...
There would have been no one left alive that day.
And what of it?
You would be dead, along with those Infected who should have been! The perfect outcome!
Platon...

lines.st: 'I will give you time. However...'
'Whether to stand with the empire, or continue to associate yourself with her traitors and enemies...'
'I want to see the answer the next time we meet.'

lines.x: ...You're right.
I see you've stopped thinking.
No. I've found the answer. I must make a choice.
What the—
You were slow. You had a chance to fight back.
Argh—
Platon...
I won't let you compound your mistakes.
I can't allow you to drag more people into this.

lines.st: 'And I will draw my sword for everyone in this building under the protection of Rhodes Island.'
'A thousand times and more, if I have to.'
'Until those like you are repelled, or until I can no longer stand.'

lines.x: ...Perhaps I'm doing this wrong.
But if the price to pay is that there will be no place for Father or me in Ursus, then so be it.
This is what I must do.
Proshchay, Platon.
I'll try to protect your family.
The only Imperial Guard left standing in the reception room picks up the bloody letter from the floor.
She tries to wipe the blood, but only succeeds in making it worse.
She gives up.
Eloysius walks over the twitching corpse on the ground, past a terrified maid—
She is going to seek amnesty.

lines.loc: Assault Ship Volnov, Command Center Jan 21, 1102, 14:42

lines.x: Approaching Second Army territory.
Boss, should we keep our pace and press on?
Keep going.
...Hey, what if—
Don't worry. We're through the front lines, so it's smooth sailing from here. You've heard him many times, haven't you? Always stops whenever we might hit back.
Kuznetsov's got a strange mind, but he's smart. Might treat us like trash, but he'd still use us until we're all used up before throwing us away.
Also, he cares for his reputation. Refusing to change his station to 'protect the north', marching outside Grypherburg without orders to 'suppress the rebellion'...
Letting his own warships be destroyed on the front lines during an armistice because of 'recklessness'? Doesn't sound reasonable at all.
Your astute and logical analysis would make one think you're close to him, even though we've only been serving Kuznetsov for barely two years.
How can I feed you lot if I can't even manage to ask around about our superior?
Back on topic. Since we're safe now, we no longer have to worry about the Second Army coming after us.
But their vanguard battalion is right there.
Oh, right. Send our identification code to their command center at once.
Did you only just remember to do that?!
I tried earlier, but we were out of range.
—Bzzzzt—
Put it through to the speakers.
Re...
The signal can't possibly be this bad, when we're already this close?
It is silent. Nothing comes through for several seconds—terrifying for those in the midst of war.
Everyone subconsciously straightens their backs as their breaths echo throughout the cabin.
If this is not a signal problem on the receiving end...
...Send it again.
We already did.
Should we switch to the contingency plan?
We're too close for that. It's too late to fight them now, we couldn't do much.
Safety first. Go—
Received.
Identity verified.
Received.
We will be gone in two hours.
Phew.
Chief.
Huh... wuh? That's new. You've never called me that ever—
Come with me for a bit.
'Don't worry'? 'Smooth sailing'? Yebat ty, What's got you acting like a frightened little boy, then?

It's different when I might drag everyone down with me.
Besides, that's was the past... I have no clue what deal he's done with the Second Army.
Perfect, because I rather not care about that now. What's important is whether you're going to tell the others or not.
...I didn't expect us to make it past the front lines, actually. I thought everyone would split and run off on their own, at which point it wouldn't matter.
Expectations and reality, completely different things. You'll have to tell them what you told me, unless you want them to die.
I don't want to send anyone to their deaths.
Yourself included?
Do I look like I have a death wish?
Who knows? I wasn't the one who personally escorted Lieutenant Sirka ten miles away, claiming I only went for a walk.

Alright, I won't die either. We good?
Let me think...
Chief, I'm serious. None of us are cowards. I think they deserve the truth.
If this is your own mission, or even if it's just to save one of our comrades... I think the risk of death will be the least of their concerns.
In any case, you should let them know.
They'll be able to intercept a broadcast from the ship, so let's get everyone on the mid-deck first.
I'll think about how I should break the news.
This must be the first time we've done so many meetings in a single day, and everyone's here too, even those on the night shift—
Shh. Just hear what the Boss has to say.
It's definitely something important.
The crowd instantly goes quiet.
Scioppa stands on a makeshift platform, composed of empty vodka crates stacked on top of each other. He manifests his Arts, quickly creating a soundproof space covering the entire deck.
He turns around, the light of his enchantment subtly flickering under the sun as it transmits his voice clearly to the crowd.
Listen up.
First, I must apologize to you all.
What?
(Whisper) You hear that...? What for?
I'm sorry for not telling you the true reason for this expedition.
I won't explain how I came to that decision, but as your commander, I am responsible for my decisions, and since my reason for hiding the truth no longer exists—
Boss, just tell us already. What is it?
The truth is... this time, Sechin has not voluntarily accepted the order to seize the First Army's new weapon.
This is also, essentially, a suicide mission.
He finishes with a deliberate pregnant pause to give the crowd time to process his words, expecting a wave of questions, but there is only silence.
Countless eyes look at him with the same expression. On the plains, on the battlefield, here and now, they have not changed.
Their trusting gazes seem to weigh down on him, and he suddenly realizes how tongue-tied he is now.
Making a speech, telling the truth—it now seems so arduous.
...So, that is why...
I swear to you...
As he struggles to find the right words to say, he notices Oleg has moved.
Oleg is now next to the platform, and he pats the young man on the back with his large hands that used to knead dough daily, almost knocking his leader off the platform.
Hey—
Go on. Everyone's listening.
Say what you have to say, whatever it is.
I took on this mission because the Fourth Army has information on the whereabouts of some of our old comrades who left us upon becoming Infected.
Just before we shipped out, Lieutenant Sirka was seized by Kuznetsov's men.
—Lieutenant Sirka?
I think she was a quiet one... that Sirka?
We have to save her.
Yeah, boss. Why don't we go rescue her right now?
That's the trouble. I don't even know where she is, I've only heard her voice over comms with Kuznetsov.
So, our usual method of sneaking in, killing, rescuing, and getting out won't work here.
So that only leaves me one path to take...
I'm not afraid to die. I'll ambush Evgeny and force Sirka's whereabouts from his dying breath! Maybe I can't do it alone, but I'm sure there are others willing to join me—
I know we can come up with a plan.
Count me in!
Me too!
The responses echo in the soundproof bubble. From the highest point on the deck, the man looks on as the cacophony of voices nearly take physical form, and shakes his head.
It's impossible. I know you're all more than willing to kill for this, but no.
Why?!
If I hadn't agreed to his demands, we'd never be able to save Sirka, and I couldn't protect the rest of you either.
We can protect ourselves!
Could you protect yourselves from a whole unit of war casters?
What?
Before I decided to bring you all into the Fourth Army, I probed around and found out about a team, practically doing the same thing we do.
Kuznetsov's personal guard. A special task force composed of elite war casters.
You mean... a whole unit as strong as you?
I'm nothing to them.
Leithanians use Infected as Arts units, but Ursus has researched the limits of using uninfected as casters, forcing them to use the tiny amounts of Originium within them as a catalyst.
To reach their limit and to use the terrifying Arts units inside them, they endure the pain with drugs and body modifications, and this makes them adaptable to all sorts of combat scenarios.
But this way, the Arts unit ends up consuming the user instead, turning their faces into a blur, their voices garbled.
That's an easy way to contract Oripathy.
War casters can never be Infected, to keep the Ursine army pure.
Whether it happens accidentally or taking a shortcut, you can bet those Infected get tossed down some random mine shaft.
Those who survive and join the army... even a dozen, or just a few of them, have enough firepower to replace a whole division.
That's how strong they are.
Even if you wouldn't usually set up a unit of just war casters, seeing as it would limit their battlefield adaptability.
I thought we had it good then, figured they were a safety net for us. But when we went against the Fourth Army...
I finally understood how they came out of the Great Rebellion unscathed.
Fine! We can't beat them head-on or ambush them, so... what do we do? Sirka—
Don't worry, I won't leave her, or anyone else behind.
I just wanted to tell you all the truth, and then I have something to propose—or maybe I should say, a decision to announce.
I will cut all communication with the base, and falsify the Volnov's location while I stop the ship's operation, for an hour.
During this time, everyone is free to leave for nearby Volniki. Ultimately, this ship will function with a skeleton crew.
We'll cut down on energy use as we continue to Zelgrad to secure the new weapon, which we'll use to negotiate with Kuznetsov and rescue Sirka.
Those willing to stay, throw your tags in the container.
My brothers and sisters: when you chose to leave home, to join me with your passion and hope, I promised you this I wouldn't let anyone die in vain.
We will not die like weeds, like fins, or fowlbeasts pulled, speared, or captured.
Because our lives have value. We are more than food for the monster we call war—
We must be free, and not only living the freedom granted by the worthies above.
We have another choice beyond fighting or dying.
Ugh...
Did you count all the votes?
Here, take a look.
He hands over an open barrel of vodka—completely empty.
Scioppa stares at the darkness within and sighs.
Didn't think I was so unpopular that nobody would want to stay.
Come on! I'm sure you know what it means—no one here wants to leave, not a single soul!
Who would even think of leaving after listening to the sentimental garbage that just came out of your mouth?
Well, some of them will have to leave anyway. The ship doesn't have enough fuel to operate at full speed or reach the satellite city in time.
Why don't you just tell everyone your plan to abandon the Volnov and go back to Kuznetsov to settle the score?
Because we should scatter our numbers to the Volniki, so Kuznetsov won't be able to catch all of us, if things go south.
We can't put everyone in danger just to rescue Sirka, even if everyone's willing to throw their lives away.
Oh, so it's just gonna be me and you?
Come on now. You know most of them haven't spoken to Sirka even once. I can't expect the same of them as I do of us.
Enough. Hand out supplies according to the list, and have them leave once the ship stops.
You stubborn—
—Chief, incoming urgent transmission from command!
(Whisper) Closure isn't in here!
Amiya, don't lean backwards, or you might fall off the truck! Hang onto the frame and shift towards the front.
It's pitch-black here without the streetlights. All we've got is our headlights, but at least we shook our pursuers.
But Closure—

opts: We can't turn back now...
Let's trust in her.
Closure will be fine until the military catches us all.
We need to move fast and find the Sarcophagus.

lines.x: Car's stopped.

lines.loc: Zelgrad Sealed District, Underground Layer Jan 22, 1102, 03:21

lines.x: Where... are we now? I think maybe we're underground—
We are.
How are you feeling, Raidian?
I stopped my Arts when we got near that wall, so I am fine now.
Say, Amiya. I did not notice until now, but there is an issue with this vehicle.
What?
There is an electrical signal from someone besides ourselves and the driver. It is messy, but I'm sure—
(Whisper) Wait, we have to hide!
(Whisper) Keep close to me!
You're late.
(Shieldguards... what are they doing down here?)
Sir, there was an explosion on the other side of the wall, and I don't know what caused it, but please, if you could just say I was on time... I have one more delivery to make...
The man in worker's clothing keeps taking out thin and round objects from his pockets, trying to stuff them into hands of the heavily armored soldiers.
His efforts bear no fruit as the discs silently roll to the ground.
You have broken the rules, so we no longer need you.
Take him away.

What?
No—NO!
I won't be late next time, I promise—
The remaining Shieldguard stands there for a moment before dialing into his communicator.
Cancel the alert.
Have those below haul the goods away.
Six floors underground.
Hm, he left. If they've stationed heavy troops here, this probably means we're close to our target.
If they're gonna get someone to haul the vehicle away, should we hide in the carriage?
We do not know where it might go, so we'd best find the way ourselves.
Raidian, you said you noticed another electrical signal on the vehicle...?
...Hold on...
Not anymore.
What? Really?
I would not lie to you. This might mean that the one I detected before has met with misfortune.
Mon3tr, can you open the door?
It's harder than—
...I thought...
Neatly stacked fertilizer bags fail to conceal two human figures slumped on top of them.
One bears a frightening face, riddled with green scars and festering wounds, but the other has a peaceful expression, body covered in orange stones.
...! That patient—
I'll go take a look.

opts: Is this the patient you were talking about before?

lines.x: I think so. But it seems like his Oripathy has worsened.
The density of the crystals on him too... it may be an acute infection, but to deteriorate this fast...?
Also, wasn't he—shouldn't he be at the clinic?
He's dead, Amiya.
For more than twelve hours at least, too.
How? Wasn't there... a doctor?
As for the other... his symptoms look similar to the one you mentioned earlier.
There are marks on his neck, and the bag was ripped open. Seems like he strangled himself, which is why no one outside heard him.

opts: So our question now is...
Why are they here?

lines.x: ...I'm guessing the Doctor is asking why they're in a 'fertilizer truck'.
Because this place doesn't actually store fertilizer.
Mon3tr moves, and several bags burst open.
No fluids or particulates spill from the bag, only frozen and mutilated... limbs.
Dark yellow crystals encrust the surfaces—Perhaps they were stuffed into these waterproof fertilizer bags according to certain criteria.
No one wants to even consider what they might be.
How—
Raidian steps in, blocking Amiya from looking on any further.
Mon3tr finishes checking the truck carriage interior, and stands up, closing her eyes briefly.
...Infected. All of them.
Blood Originium-Crystal Density levels still climbing. This truck is practically a huge ticking time bomb—

opts: Say no more, Mon3tr.
We get the idea, Mon3tr.
Come back here. Thanks for checking.

lines.x: Amiya, the one with green bruise marks shares symptoms with those infected by airborne Originium dust caused by bio-energy disequilibrium after a Sarcophagus overload.
However, you need loads of energy and extremely destructive usage to overload a Sarcophagus, so an accident like this is extremely unlikely.
This may well mean that the Sarcophagus's basic functions have gone completely out of control.

opts: What are you saying?
That means... it's lost its restorative capabilities?

lines.x: Doctor, I refuse to prepare for the worst.
But my observations so far have indicated the bio-dust is still leaking from the Sarcophagus, with unthinkable consequences if we don't stop it soon.
It could come to a point where we'll have to destroy the Sarcophagus to stop it from spreading further.
...Although that would mean losing the chance to...

opts: Let's not assume we must sacrifice one for the other.

lines.x: Right.
Let's press on, Doctor.
Hey, you—
Ugh...
If you can't stand, stay down.
Reunion... we've met before—
Oh, you're still here.
I'll skip asking how you know.
Are you really with Reunion?
Most certainly.
How many of you are there? Can you help us? There's a weird sickness in the city that isn't Oripathy, and it's spreading!
We need to let everyone know, it's not a problem that will affect just a few—
There's a few things I need to confirm with you. Can you describe its symptoms?
It causes green bruises, and your skin slowly rots! My sister caught it, and I sent her to a clinic to 'isolate', but...
She was taken away, somewhere I don't know. I heard people talking about how they saw soldiers loading Infected onto trucks and sending them to the wall...
Tulin quickly exchanges a glance with Red, as she continues hearing what Tonya has to say without interrupting.
The soldiers don't let us near the wall, but this time I really wanted to go, no matter what.
I was planning to follow a truck in, so I planted a bomb to distract them, and then I saw—
Tonya's eyes flick to and fro, and finally she looks at Closure.
You saw us?
Yes... I didn't know you, but I guessed we shared a similar goal. It was dangerous, so I just decided on the spot to help you...
Then I missed my chance... the gate's closed.
Wow, I really got to hand it to you.
A plan like that... your bravery is commendable.
We planned it properly and all, you know!
Um, thank you very much, for saving me...
Could I ask you all... to rescue... my sister...?
You said you followed the truck to the wall, but where did it come from?
I don't know, I only realized it was heading towards the wall and followed it.
So you don't actually know where your sister is.
I—
I'm sorry, we're willing to offer help to those who need it, but we can't recklessly throw ourselves into danger.
We can't act without concrete information.
Please, hold on. What happened to this young lady's sister is probably not an isolated case in Zelgrad.
Do you have any idea where your sister might be?
You're right, I don't have anything solid...
I just thought... she fell sick because I was helping to wash the white coats of those behind the wall. So that's probably the one place they would take her.
'White coats', you say?
I think they call them 'researchers', although I've never seen any of them in person. The guards never mention them either.
They just go 'these are uniforms from Lab Six', 'these are from Test Lab One'...
Hah... it's like we're a laundromat.
I understand.
What?
To be honest, we've also observed this 'strange sickness', and concluded that it was already killing the people here, regardless of where it came from.
And based on what she's said, this is definitely because of an experiment they're running behind the wall...
—You mean that sickness is really related to the Sarcophagus?
What?
Uh—
So you came for the Chernobog Sarcophagus.
Hey, don't word it like we're just here for that!
Sorry, I didn't mean it that way.
We can hear your story later.
The pressing question now is: what is this 'Sarcophagus' you speak of? What kind of harm could it bring?
It's hard to put together a quick and easy explanation, but as far as I know, it's capable of spreading infectious symptoms.
It might not be the same as last time, but something similar did happen before, and just a few years ago too.
Right. All in all, you want to prevent a similar disaster from taking place?
You could put it that way, yeah!
Is the disaster triggered by this 'Sarcophagus' related to the Infected?
Based on the info we have at the moment, I can't draw any solid conclusions. I can only guess both Infected and non-Infected will be affected.
We're already seeing signs, so we have to look further into it.
Thanks for helping me today, but I'm still going to look for another way to find my friends.
We tried looking for traces of the refugee miners who came here, but haven't found anything. We haven't looked past the wall, though.
Likewise, we have our duty to fulfill.
Then, count me in too.
Hey, your wounds are serious. Careful how you move.
I just knew... the First Army's secret weapon work was suspicious, I knew it would kill more civilians than soldiers before it was dropped onto some random battlefield.
If you plan to cross that wall, then you should let me come with.
You're an Ursine soldier?
Heh... have you ever seen an Ursine soldier fall as low as I have?
These Reunion people saved me, and I'm grateful.
Bring me along, and I swear you have an ally in me... I won't give up, even if you say no.
I have a score to settle with a man in there... a man who should have died long ago.
Uchitel! There's someone at the right entrance with an identification code requesting entry!
It's a complete stranger, so we had her write the code on paper. Here.
I don't know who this is. Don't let her in.
Seems like this place is no longer safe. We need to move as soon as we can.
Can I see the code?
This is an old Reunion code.
Someone from your side?
Everyone who followed me to Zelgrad is already here.
Anyone who shows up outside now...
Talulah.
Yeah, I know. I've heard of her operating in the west.
Let her in.
Her gaze instantly drops to Talulah, but quickly shifts away.

You—you're the one who warned me!
You said you were going to gather more evidence...
And I'm back with that evidence.
Lyudmila—
I don't know what you were talking about, or your plans, but since you've been wandering around the city these past few days—
I take it you're looking for those missing Infected.
You know where they are?
I even know of expansion plates in Zelgrad that aren't on any maps.
On one of those is a factory, where most Infected are sent. As to what the factory is for, I have no clue myself.
It's tightly guarded, so I came here looking for help, since there's no way I'll manage alone.
You say those expansion plates aren't on the maps, but wouldn't the residents here notice all their Infected going to the same place?
When something doesn't concern them or those around them, it's hard for ordinary people to suss it out.
After all, Zelgrad is the 'city of tomorrow' where every 'hardworking soul' can find their own place...
There is no need to worry about those left behind in the cold of winter when you bathe yourself in the warmth of spring.
Regardless, saving as many people as we can is paramount. Before we go past the wall, we need to take a look at that 'factory'.
Having a clear objective simplifies things for us... show us the way.
There are none left. Absolutely none. The entire way here, there have been no Infected who failed to get aid and shelter.
'I made the right decision.'
'I made the right decision.'
As she walked to the treatment center, she told herself this, over and over.
But... what next? What must she do to make this situation a lasting one?
...I see.
Elotta, you should know that the red on an Imperial Guardsman's uniform represents the red of blood.

A soldier who slew countless enemies on the battlefield used his torn uniform to hold his spilling intestines inside his body as he crawled back to camp, all so he could celebrate a momentary victory for his comrades who would not return.
When he died, his blood had soaked through the makeshift bandages, clinging tightly to his stiffening body and sticking to his abdomen.
Correct. Which is why you do not need to worry yourself too much about this matter. You were decisive in your judgment. There is nothing more to it.
But I executed him without a trial, without permission—
Is it not normal for an officer to act first and report later under extraordinary circumstances?
We need not even carry out a court martial. Anyone with eyes would approve of your difficult decision.
Then will Platon's family be implicated?
I can only say that I did not hear anything about his family inciting him to act this way in your report just now.
But this does not mean any guarantees as to their fate.
What do you mean?
Once more, you look only at the 'truth', without making an effort to piece together the cause behind it, correct?

When Count Lunin first began dealing with your father several years ago, he was an honorary citizen who could only support a small workshop, but he has now become a new noble, with textile factories spanning several districts of Grypherburg.
I fear nobody would see this rate of progress and think he did it by his own effort. And when the partner he relied on lost his glory, and could not render more aid—

No matter if he managed to devour the hand that once fed him, or if they fall together, the shift in resources resulting from this commotion will not flow down to those who never had anything to begin with.
This is the greatest problem our modern nation faces. No matter how much bread we may produce in aggregate, we cannot ensure it reaches everyone.
We cannot fill the bellies... of all our people.
Which is why you should not be worrying about whether people will suddenly fall from grace due to your actions.
If you still wish to do something worthwhile, then consider my words carefully.
We must act, before even more people are fed into the insatiable machine that is the empire.
I must...
Eloy...sius.
Y-You're... back. Everyone's... okay. D-D-Don't worry.
Vetochki.
Hmm?
Where is the general?
'The g-general'? Wh-Who is that?
...Is Gospodin Hellagur in?
He's... r-reading books... with some of th-the little kids.
Little kids? Littler than you?
I-I'm... not... little!
In j-just a f-few months... I'll be sixteen!
Sixteen. If you were the daughter of a noble, you'd have the formal right to inherit. A woman grown.
B-But I'm not... and I d-don't want to be one.
Then do you want to go somewhere where you can tell your story, where you can fight for fair treatment for all your friends?
We can... go and... t-testify?
D-Dur-nar said... the courthouse... is that sort of p-p-place.
No, Vetochki. Not this time. I won't lie to you. You will not be going to testify.
There is a bill called The Winter Emergency Resource Allocation Act, to be voted on in Grypherburg's first citizen's forum.
If it passes, it will save the lives of countless people unable to keep themselves warm this winter, countless workers who lost their jobs due to lack of resources.
Before all that, you can go and give suggestions, tell them your story, raise support among the people. You will help the proposal pass. You will help your comrades.
Th-Then... I'll go.
However, it means you will need to get up in front of everyone. There will be no lack of unsightly faces there, ones just like the 'lords' you saw during your time in the mines.
This may also be very dangerous. The Infected are still not allowed to walk the streets unchaperoned, and you will make yourself stand out. Although Hellagur and I will protect you—
I-I'll still go!
I want to go. E-Even if it's d-dangerous, I'll go.
Alright then.
Then let me find a way to make them give you back the identity that should have been yours in the first place.
You're back.
Judging by the look on your face, did you get confirmation about something?
I have... received a whistleblower report.
From Vasily's daughter.
Eloysius?
You remember her.

Because her mother gave her such a rare name.
Why would she report on her own father?
In her own words... 'This all has crossed my bottom line. I had to make a choice to prevent even more people from falling victim to my father's absurd schemes.'

This report—perhaps testimony—exposes his attempts to pull Duchess Volkina and the pro-war faction into an alliance. It is able to force him to be suspended pending inquiry, perhaps even be temporarily detained.
But even if we exploit the fact that he has exposed an entry point into the interior of the pro-wars through his treachery, this will not touch on the root of the issue at hand...
I suggest sealing this report and all other results of related investigations, to be used at a later date.
If we use that evidence to control him, then the vice-chairman's current behavior is no longer important.
Precisely.
How interesting... First the students in Katorga, now the new generation of the Imperial Guard. The vast majority of our youth are awake now.

But what about those stubborn, sundowning old men? Why do they still turn a blind eye to all the contradictions and challenges exposed by our lack of minerals? Why are they so devoted to making trouble for people outside their circle?
Are they not like a chronic illness plaguing Ursus...? When did our nation lose the strength to fight disease within?
Your Imperial Majesty... Though you may see them as disease, they are also the flesh the empire demands.
Fortunately, we are witnessing a new power be born within this nation, even though they are still young sprouts unable to break through the permafrost... We wish them to have more time.
You're right... 'Disease' and 'flesh', who should be the one differentiating them?
How do I ensure that, when this power emerges from the soil, I will not be seen by them as 'the chronic illness plaguing Ursus' myself?
Your Imperial Majesty?
Tell me plainly, Witte. How likely is The Winter Emergency Resource Allocation Act to pass, if things stay as they are?
If we only factor in the possibility of men following their good conscience, then thirty percent, no higher.
As I have said before, there is no man who would willingly give up his own profits. What you aim to do will leave them one last bit of grace, though none of them will thank you for it.
Your magnanimity will be as pearls before meatbeasts.
This will be their last chance.
If these beasts are still ungrateful, then this will be their last chance to use their 'innate authority' to sit at the table.

The signal-blocking mechanism here is very strange...
I can't guarantee that I've found the right place, but there shouldn't be any guards popping out to intercept us when we get out.
Let's focus on getting out first, then. At least we haven't heard any alarms.
We've been walking in the dark for ages now, Raidian. Where's this exit you were talking about?

opts: Do you have night vision, Mon3tr?

lines.x: I mean, yes, but I might as well not have here. It's all just walls and stairs. No sight of even an emergency exit sign.
Can you tell what materials they're made of? Walls and doors have their differences. Even if they appear the same visually, their materials will let us tell them apart.
Look, but don't touch without proper caution. The doors may be electrified.
Hmm...
Ah, found one!
Oh, this is...
Light from outside? But aren't we underground? How did sunlight get through the ceiling?
Though it appears to be a courtyard, that light isn't natural light.
Secret installations such as these cannot simply add a real glass ceiling. It would be far too conspicuous from the surface.
It reminds me a little of that research institute we visited in the Far North. The construction style, I mean.
But the impression I get is completely different...

opts: It's too quiet.
It doesn't feel stifling here.

lines.x: Right...
Isn't that good?
It looked that way from the outside, didn't it? But now we know the truth of the matter inside.

opts: Defenses here are strangely lax.
No Army Shieldguards like the one we saw earlier either.
Stay alert, everyone.

lines.x: I'll find us a route without anyone along it so we can scout this place out.
It's so strange... We can't find any doors leading out.
It's like a maze in here.
I don't think we can keep avoiding places with other people, Raidian.
People may have their own unique body signal frequencies, but I can't rely on just that to determine if they're friendly on first contact.
Then we'll—
Gah!
Amiya!

opts: Let go of her!

lines.x: I've been watching you people for half an hour. A group suddenly appearing in the second floor halls, with some sort of goal in mind, but never actually leaving.
How did you get in here, and what're you trying to do?
Sir... Please, calm down, we're—
I want someone else talking.

opts: We were sent here by the State Council!
We're here to help with Project Zero!

lines.x: Don't be stupid. The scholars the State Council sent over were already assigned to their labs. You really think you can fool us?
I see. You must be spies who slipped in during that explosion outside!

Mind how you speak. We are from Rhodes Island Pharmaceuticals, and have been dispatched by the State Council of the Ursine Empire. We are here to help with research into Project Zero's pharmaceutical applications.
Here is our warrant of appointment with the tsar's seal, as well as our documentation from the legislature. You'll find our Zelgrad immigration stamps there too.
As for why we have been pacing about the halls, it is naturally because—
Because we forgot how to get back.
Which lab are you from?
I'm the director of Lab Six.
Hah, Lab Six has already been dissolved. Even their director got banished. Who do you think you're trying to fool—
Here's my ID.
Alita Valueva...
If I were you, I'd ask others before I pick a theory to believe in.
Someone like your boss, Zina, for example. I believe she's in charge of security for the entire institute. She'd know who all the new staff in Lab Six are, surely?
What do we do, boss?
Hail Zina on her channel and ask her!
Y-Y-Yes, sir!
The blonde researcher turns away from the guards, sweeping her eyes across the Rhode Islanders. Her eyes stop on you for a moment, before finally settling on Raidian.
I can't believe I forgot to get someone to show you the way out. Lab Four's not on this floor. I've been so busy these past few days, I'd forget my own head next.
Once this misunderstanding is all sorted out, I'll lead you there personally.
...We are grateful to you, really. And after you took the time to bring us up to speed on your project, too.
I'll need to bring you around all the labs, then you'll see that New Lab Six's project is the one with the most resources at its disposal here.
Boss, Zina confirmed this is the name of New Lab Six's director.
Hmph!
Amiya!

opts: Once we see the Generalik, he'll know of what happened today.
Random questionings, seizing guests. I see how you treat others.

lines.x: Move it!
Well then... Madam Alita Valueva—
Not in a hurry to go? Come with me then.
*cough*—Suka!
Who the hell are these people? How do they have so much firepower?!
It's all one individual's Arts! Saw it with my own eyes!
You serious?
We need to get out of here right now, sir! They've smashed through everything in their way, none of our emplacements could hold them back longer than half a minute!
Absolutely not! We were ordered to guard this place, and if any of you dare to take even one step back, I'm cutting off your legs—
Before he can finish, a scarlet streak flies past his nose, screeching as it slams into the wall behind him in a burst of flame, illuminating the dark, cramped 'factory'.
The officer locks in place, stiffly turning his neck until ice-cold steel presses up against his sweat-stained skin—
Stop.
If you have even the slightest bit of a conscience, or a slimmer of remorse...
I'll give you one chance. Out of the way.
Crossbow bolts whistle through the sky from all around her. One last volley from the desperate defenders.
Waves of flame flick their way up the bolt shafts, igniting the Originium in the bolt heads in an instant. They explode into amber smoke.
Talulah simply stands there, light and shadow flitting across her face. As the soldiers try to figure out what this expression means, wretched yells come from nearby—
First one, then another... More and more soldiers fall, and the yelling dies out alongside their breaths. Slowly but surely, all that remains is the sound of a sword being sheathed.
...I nearly forgot how you do things.
Forget the soldiers. More importantly, I don't see any researchers here.
Secret facilities like these almost certainly have emergency escape routes installed by the army. They most likely left the moment they heard about our activities.
Gather up the materials and all the clues you can find. They couldn't have taken away all the evidence in such a short amount of time.
I need your help, everyone.
Alright everyone, split up. If you notice anything, report it right away. Time is of the essence.
The miners give her a shout of agreement before they separate into groups.
Closure stands away from them as she surveys the site of the battle just now. Everything has been reduced to piles of charcoal.
(Quietly) Is this what it was like to face her, Amiya...?
Did you say something, Closure?
...Ah, err, nothing.
