Let's help them out, Tonya. The secrets you want to know are most likely going to be here, and who knows, we might find some meds for that weird disease!
Yeah, if it can help my sister—
What?
T-T-Tulin, no...
What is it? Don't rush, take it slow.
Tsar's mercy... I-I, I...
I'll take a look.
Red walks past the dumbstruck miner, pushing open the door behind him.
The smell of rust strikes him in the face. Part of it smells like blood, another part like iron steeped in water, and yet another part like rust heated to the point of burning, all mingling together—
Hand me a flashlight.
What in the—?!
The crowd follows the beam of light with their eyes. The first thing they see is a giant glass vat, shattered in half... and whatever is inside it is leaking out.
Drip, drip... It spills, mixing with the dirt, gravel, and blackened clots of blood strewn across the ground.
There are fingers and toes, mud still staining them. There is a backbone, one that is stooped, hunched and elderly. There is—
An object, gently bumping against their boots before stopping.
Red looks down. It is a swollen, damaged, rubbery body, coated in an ashen gray. Half of a cheek presses against the ground, as two dark, empty sockets stare back at him.
He closes his eyes and stays silent. But even so, he feels something gaze at him from the abyss. It sees him stand there, sees him breathe, sees him live.
Until someone vomits.
Oh... What... What is this?!
How could they... No...
(Crying) Ueargh... *cough* *cough*—
(Crying) Red, please, shut that door, I'm begging you...
The voices of his comrade startle Red. With a tremble of his hand, the light shoots into the darkness... There, there are more vats.
Some are empty, spotless, as if they have been polished, washed, and tidied. Even the metal brackets below shine, reflecting back the light.
Some are not so empty.
Within the oily liquid, glistening Originium crystals shine as they jut out of butchered bodies, cluster by cluster, like bushes growing on sand.
(Weeping) Damn you, Red, you idiot... Damn you!
The man wails as he tries to wrestle the flashlight out of Red's hand, but try as he might, he cannot break Red's vice grip. The swaying light sweeps across the entire room.

Other Reunion members surround him, trying to pull away their comrade after he had lost his wits. But they cannot. More step forward. Everyone helps drag away the one man, his feet leaving two marks on the ground.
More of them sit on the floor in exhaustion, silently watching the scuffle as they let their tears flow freely.
These... What... What are...
Stupefied faces turn towards her, as flashlights illuminate another corner of the room.
Junk?
Personal effects, more like.
Bedding. Broken bowls. Blackened bread as hard as rock, yet still gnawed in half. Even golden dentures. All tossed into the corner.
As the footsteps approach, the pile is covered by the shadow of a frail woman.
Tonya kneels before the pile, her hands sifting through its ice-cold contents—and then she sees it. She knows this blanket... She would never be mistaken about it.
A blanket that was once wrapped tight around a child, the edges of the red cloth a faded white, now covered in a thin layer of dust—
Her little sister's.
She cradles it as if it were alive, pressing it against her cheek.

A blanket with nothing to wrap around, the smell of detergent and sweat still lingering in the fabric. She buries her face in it, her shoulders heaving up and down as the cloth slowly soaks in her tears.
Nina... My poor, poor Nina...

Tonya does not stop calling out her sister's name, as if saying it could bring her back to her. But there is too much spit clogging her throat, too many tears slipping into her mouth, so all she can choke out is a rasp.
Talulah does not turn away. She clenches her fists tight, so tight her arms begin to shake.
The shoulders of her shadow looming against the wall begin to heave as well, as if pressed down by something extraordinarily heavy.
Suddenly, they drop. She feels a rough, strong hand gently holding them down.
Talulah turns, and is greeted by a pair of mauve eyes. They do not look away, as unwavering as the hand on her shoulder.
...Tulin?
They need you, Talulah. Need us.
Tulin nods towards the men. The miners cough as they see Tulin approach, trying to reset their emotions.
The youth gently consoles them, holds their hands, hugs them, helps pull up the ones laying on the ground... Though many of their faces are still stained with tears, they no longer tremble.
Then, Tulin heads towards someone else who is also relatively calm. Someone currently looking at the very first vat, lost in thought.
Have you found anything, Closure?
I noticed all the vats have cables and tubes attached to them... I'm afraid I don't know much about this topic. Do you know what the military might have been doing to the Infected?
I inspected them just now.
These machines are strange, but I can see the readings on the meters...
They were calculating how much Originium these Infected would turn into after they died.
They were turning the Infected into 'fuel' to combat the Originium shortage.
That's... That's my best guess, yeah.
But Tonya's sister wasn't Infected, she just caught that strange disease. But her blanket's here all the same...
I noticed many of the bodies here have the same symptoms.
Look at these remains from the first vat. Ulcerated pustules, covered in green scars. Clearly the disease Tonya talked about, but no signs of Oripathy.
The First Army was obviously researching this new disease, and it just so happened to show up after Zelgrad revised their Infected policy.

You said the Sarcophagus might have released some disease that seems infectious. If they're gathering the Infected to sacrifice them for Sarcophagus research, this 'strange disease' must be related to it.
We need to tell everyone the truth about this 'Sarcophagus' right away.
The First Army let this disease spread freely, which means everyone's lives are in danger. We have to get them out of here.
We can't hide our raid from the army for very long. They'll have a response soon enough.
But if we just need to stall for time and protect you as you evacuate, then Reunion can do that.
Let's not waste time, then. We need to—
Tulin sees Closure give a faint shake of the head. She hesitantly walks to Tonya, still rooted to the floor, before stretching out her hand.
...Closure?
Sorry... I'm really not good at giving pep talks.
Err... Right, you said you never saw a Sarkaz before, yeah? Well I'm a Sarkaz from Kazdel, real old school.
Kazdel's a lot worse off compared to Zelgrad. Maybe only half the kids in the city have a roof over their heads... and only half of the kids ever get to grow up.
But even so, we still call Kazdel home.

Eventually, we built a lot more houses, and planted a lot more crops. There was also one amazing person who got everyone together to research medicine that could actually treat the pain of Oripathy...
When everyone worked together, life really did get better... We all treasure our home.
Tonya slowly lifts her head as she looks at the Vampire before her, meeting her teary gaze.

I'm really sorry that... Zelgrad couldn't be a place like that for you. But there'll definitely be a day you find somewhere you can really call 'home'.
Nina... couldn't make it to that day.
But if you work alongside us, Tonya, there'll be lots of other kids who can.
After a moment of silence, Tonya grabs onto Closure's hand and pulls herself up.
This place... is right by the district I live in.
I can... I...
I'll go with you... and get everyone out of here.

lines.loc: Lab Six, Zelgrad Sealed District LaboratoryJan 18, 1102, 23:07

lines.x: You've been looking at these files for an entire day, director. You should get some rest, at least eat something...
Is this all of the Kushkina file, Gira?
I think... like you, though, I was recently reassigned, so I can't be sure there are no omissions.
I wasn't even given a logbook during the handover.
All research data should be filed in the logbook, whether the data is valid or not. This is a problem.
Look at this. The progress reports jump straight from 03 to 21, the missing files listed as 'data lost'. Not even the raw records remain.
What?
And these audio logs have clearly been tampered with. I took some time to listen to them, but there was nothing but useless noise.
This is not normal. When I went to the security station to obtain security footage of Lab Six from prior to the handover, I found that all footage from the last three days have been deleted.
All that they gave me were some maintenance logs. They said it provided a record of people come to and from Lab Six during these few days.
Guess what I found.
Beats me.

On the day of the Kushkina test, there was a power outage that lasted about thirty minutes. The repair team arrived eight minutes after the outage began, but they were not able to fully mitigate the overload problem.

Following up on the trail, I found that the cooling pool had dried up that day, and all backup systems were destroyed, while the temperature of that thing underground remains at high levels—
It's not going to blow up immediately, but things didn't go back to normal either.
This means there's something else that's cooling it, but we don't know what it is!
Even so, the conclusion in the report was that risk levels were under control.
But the test succeed. The power of Kushkina was witnessed across half of Ursus...
Is that really something worth celebrating?
My research was on how to turn the 'Prototype' into a reliable energy source, not an uncontrollable weapon.
But all we know about Kushkina is that it's powerful, and it cannot be recreated in a controlled environment.
I don't even want to think about where these experiments are going.
Director... couldn't we just focus on doing experiments? If you question the Marshal's decisions—
I'm in no position to defy my orders...
But I need to find out what's going on in this place.
HR records... six from the data team, two from the risk assessment team, seven from the assembly team.
Reassignment... promotion... none of them are in Zelgrad anymore.
I can't reach any of them...
What are you looking for at an hour like this?
Something like notes from the previous supervisor. We ran into a roadblock during the day—
Well, if it's not here, it's probably not anywhere. The whole Lab Six staff was replaced. Surely you know what that means in this industry.
What are you saying?
They must have screwed up somewhere, which means the previous supervisor would be held responsible, which means she wouldn't have left any notes behind.
We have to empty our pockets when we leave the building. If she really left, she wouldn't have been able to take anything associated with the project.
If you can't find it here, you won't find it anywhere.
Director?
Gira? What is it?
I thought about what you said and decided you should have this. It contains some unlogged notes that I found in a cabinet.
I didn't open them, but—I hope they can help you and the project.
Thank you, Gira...
Don't mention it, really!
Diary... blank scrap paper...
The signature of the previous supervisor? Did all this belong to her?
A notebook—
What is this?
Words of despair are scrawled over the last page.

lines.st: With what sanity I have left, I believe we will never find out the truth about this machine, not in the lifetime of Ursus.
It is so complex and contains such massive energy reserves that I can only consider it a work of God, and it is not our place to use it, either as a weapon or Originium generator.
It is a complete black box with no credible theoretical basis on which to study it. Even more terrifying is that it seems to have a mind of its own, resisting our exploration of it.
This time, the explosion occurred in the wilderness. Next time, it could happen at Zelgrad, even Grypherburg.
No one knows where this instrument came from or what it is, but one thing is clear: It is not a blessing to the empire, but a curse.

lines.x: There are numerous graphs and diagrams in the notebook.
Some are smooth and clean, neat and tidy, while other peak and bottom out sharply or terminate suddenly. There appears to be little rhyme or reason to the data.
'Experiment outcome is not reproducible in whole or part. The overall state of Project Zero is...'

lines.st: 'Out of control.'

lines.x: Gosudar-batyushka...
There is no weapon. The successful test was just dumb luck.
(Hushed) All the 'energy'... they've gone into a bottomless pit.
Director Alita Valueva! The Army—the Generalik just had everyone in Lab Four arrested!
Why? What does he want?
No idea. But they haven't been taken away yet. You should hurry!
I—why should I hurry?
Isn't your husband working in Lab Four?
Stop.
I'm the director of Lab Six.
Doesn't matter. You can't pass.
I am Alita Valueva, director of Lab Six. I am demanding that Lab Four and its personnel be reassigned to the critical project at Lab Six.
Communicate this to your superior immediately.
Don't make me repeat myself again.
I don't want to repeat myself either—
Do as she says.
Chief?
A chief of staff who has to take orders from a child who hasn't seen a single battle? Who would believe it?
Open your eyes, soldier.
General Anatoliy Svetlanov Buterin, in his infinite wisdom, has instructed that all requests by Lab Six are top-priority, whether it's the old one or the new one.
Where's the watch your mother gave you?
Lost it.
Are you still taking your meds?
Not for a long time. I would be kicked out of the lab if they found out.
I'm not leaving you, Lita.
Then stop deceiving me, Klim.
I've never...
Your recklessness almost killed everyone in your lab.
Besides, I never told you about my comms channel. How did you find out?
You were still using the system we built together when we were in school. Only I know about it here...
Why didn't you ask me?

You don't—
You don't want to see me, do you?
Oh, I'm not trying to blame you—
I know.
Huh?
I know you wanted to see me, but I didn't want to see you. I don't care about anyone who comes and goes in this place, and you need to know that you're the same to me right now.
The only thing that matters to me right now is completing Kushkina.
Lita—
Don't call me that. You should not have joined a project you were unsuited to, just because of me. You should have gone to Lada and stayed with her.
Even a broken family is home.
Home. Yes, Lita! In the last communication, I heard—
No, don't say it. I don't want to know.
Stay away from the work here. Don't try to send any messages out with my channel.
Go get some cleaning work from Logistics. Stay away from all of this.

lines.loc: 3F Corridor, Zelgrad Sealed District Laboratory Jan 22, 1102, 07:20

lines.x: All of B3 is assigned to Lab Five.
Their work may be more aligned with your company's. Their field of research is the progression of Oripathy infection.
Would you like to take a look?
No, thank you... there's a question I've mean meaning to ask, Madam Alita Valueva—
Go on.
Do we really have to be accompanied by so many soldiers?
Ah, I forgot to explain.
Visitors must be accompanied by military representatives at all times. I informed them in accordance with regulations.
To prevent espionage and leaks concerning secret projects. I'm sure you understand.
...I understand.

opts: Will they intrude on our conversations?

lines.x: There is no need to worry. The security measures only come in play when necessary. Otherwise, you can treat them as though they don't exist.
If you insist, we can stop and develop trust in not having conversations interrupted.
There's no need—
For example, I'm curious about the analysis on the 'Prototype' that you provided. How did you know so much?
'Prototype'?
(Whisper) Maybe she means the Sarcophagus. Let the Doctor handle it.

opts: A Rhodes Island member was involved in its research.
She was an outstanding scientist.
She was an experienced scholar.

lines.x: How much does this researcher know about the Prototype?

opts: No one knows the Sarcophagus better than her.
She knows everything there is to know about the Sarcophagus.

lines.x: Sarcophagus... that's a name I haven't heard in a long time. I've gotten used to calling it the Prototype.
Are you familiar with her research?

opts: I have read all the files she left behind.

lines.x: ...'Left behind', you say. Where did she go?

She...
She is temporarily absent from Rhodes Island. That's why she's not with us today.
I suppose you will do. The research has encountered some obstacles, and there are quite a few things in the files that I don't fully understand, for which I could use your help.

The most pressing issue at present is that the Prototype is in a constant state of overheating and unable to be fully cooled. Certain experiments and operations are unable to be performed, causing the project to grind to a halt.
No one knows how to stop the overheating and return the Prototype's output to normal boundaries.
(Whisper) Sounds like the Sarcophagus has entered a protected state after overloading.
Did you say something?
Amiya—
It's alright. You can tell her.
It sounds like the Sarcophagus has entered a protected state after overloading. How long has it been in this state?
Since I took over Lab Six five days ago, maybe even before that.
That's not right...
If you would like to know more details, we can go directly to Lab Six.
I won't be letting you go to any other project. You have to stay.
We can talk on the way.
...That's how I was reassigned here.
I first heard about the Sarcophagus when I was a student. It seemed like an urban legend, and young people are always bold and curious—
I wrote a letter to the mayor, a youthful plea that expressed my hope to join research on the Sarcophagus when I grew up. I didn't receive a response, of course.
Who would have thought that I would be studying it here, twenty years later?
Are you from Chernobog?
Heh, yes. I was born in Chernobog, as was my daughter... I hope to be buried there when I die.
Why do you say this—
How old are you, child?

I'm not really a child anymore...
I was sent here as, um, a researcher. I'm not so little anymore.
Your generation will always be children in the eyes of mine. Perhaps one day you'll understand, when you find yourself in our shoes.
I left that place because of my work. I've practically forgotten what my daughter looks like.
Has she grown? What is life like for her? Has she made new friends?
All I know is that she's still alive, that she survived the disaster at Chernobog five years ago. Other than that, I know nothing about my proud little girl scout...
I know almost nothing about Lada anymore.
Isolated research project, Chernobog, girl scout, Lada.
Amiya remembers Crownslayer's conjecture in her report to the Grypherburg office.
She looks closely at the woman's golden hair, the shape of her face becoming increasingly familiar.
The conjecture grows more certain by the second, and Amiya could not help but ask.
Could you please repeat your last name?
Valueva.
I know a Lada Valueva. She's around my age, and she's from Chernobog too—
She was in the Ursus Youth Scouts. She joined Rhodes Island as an operator, and is currently continuing her education in Deity Grypherburg.
Lada has been looking for her parents... I'm thinking you might be her mother?
I—
I don't know.
But if I am... that's the best news I've heard in ages.
Maybe you can come with us to Grypherburg, once we settle things here.
Maybe I could. Grypherburg isn't too far from Zelgrad.
Lada would be delighted to see you.
Yes. She wouldn't even yell at us.
She is kind, gentle, a much better daughter than we deserve.
I... I really want to see her again.
Stop, Alita Valueva. You are approaching a top-secret area.
Until this cold, hard reminder, Amiya did not notice that they have journeyed into the depths of the laboratory.
Indeed, the narrow, curved corridor before them seems to lead to a place that few are allowed to step foot in.
They have been sent by the council to assist. They are not ordinary visitors.
Protocol requires that I seek confirmation from my superiors.
You should not proceed any further until permission has been granted.
I am the director of Lab Six, and this is necessary for our operation. You have no idea how much could have been achieved in the time wasted waiting here.
We are simply following orders.
What do we do—
Watch your feet. The corridor leading to the observation room is not connected to the central power supply, and emergency lighting could be fickle at the best of times...
But I'll find it. Give me a moment.
(Whisper) You'll have less than ten seconds. Do not hesitate.
(Whisper) If you have any questions, you should ask them now.
Is the Sarcophagus still in a condition to supply energy to Ursus?
Now is not the time to talk about the theoretical future...
Never mind... I trust in your resolve.
Found it.
Amiya...
I put in your hands the fate of Lada, and of millions more.
This is—
'Emergency lighting.'
Go, Amiya, and take your friends.
What about you?!
Go—
...Valueva has mutinied.
Prepare to attack.
The emergency lighting comes back in a matter of moments. A closing blast door now separates the scientist and the Rhodes Island team.
Valueva—
Alita!
There is no time! Promise to stop the Sarcophagus! You must do it!
It is being fueled by the lives of thousands of kidnapped, dismembered Infected!
Too late... it took too long for me to find out. All the research here was designed to reinforce the profit chain of the First Army...
I was an accomplice. I can never look Lada in the eye again.
No! But you—you wanted to see her again!
The door's closing, Amiya! Get your hand clear!
Why—
Why?

lines.st: ...Perhaps I'm simply tired. Tired of deception, of the passions of love and hate. How could one who has lost the capacity to love go back to those whom she loved?
Fortunately, Lada is not like me. She has always been strong, always true to her word.
She'll miss me, I'm sure. There will be pain and sorrow for her in the future, but there will be even more joy and happiness.

lines.x: There's no message that I need you to deliver. Let me just...
Let me believe it to the end.
A bloody palm mark is painted on the switch, like an immovable seal upon the thick door.
Alita...
Amiya...
Stand up, Amiya.
This door is thick and jams electrical signals. It's unlikely that those on the outside will be able to force it open in short order.
Alita Valueva has bought us valuable time.

opts: We have no time to waste.
We can't let her down.

lines.x: Then...
Let's begin.
This is the core of the Sarcophagus... I've never seen it with my own eyes.
But something feels off about it...
The megastructure feels both familiar and alien. You still remember its faint silhouette, but what lies before you know is different.
It is not a distant memory. Several years ago, Amiya awakened you from this legacy of a previous civilization, which you sealed away together with Kal'tsit.
More memories come rushing back, mixed with memories buried even deeper.

lines.st: Why insist on leaving behind such an inefficient machine, Doctor?
We have more convenient ways of retaining our consciousness... is this part of your obsession with 'life'?
Coming back to the old argument, are we?
But of course, I will not deny you such a small liberty... I will add another entry to AMa-10's mission.
Not satisfied with just touching consciousness? Would you find more comfort to hold my hand like this?
Doctor... I know that you want this, here and now, to be a memory preserved forever.
Not cast into oblivion, when the ultimate destruction comes.Doctor

lines.x: Doctor!
Are you alright, Doctor? What happened?

opts: ...Did you see that, Amiya?
I think I remember something...

lines.x: I saw fragments, snapshots... but nothing clear.
I just felt your pain in that instant...

opts: I guess... I do have a bit of a headache.
Can you assess the current status of the Sarcophagus, Mon3tr?

lines.x: Based on my inspection just now...
The Sarcophagus...
...has been destroyed.
Chief.
...Put him through.
Major Razin, it seems that your progress has fallen behind initial expectations.
You will not arrive at the satellite city in time, at this rate.
We don't have enough power, Your High Excellency. We're already diverting as much as we can from temperature controls. The men can hardly sleep with the cold...
Though I suppose none of that matters to you.
You are correct.
In fact, you're not doing enough.
There's no point in sending an exhausted force to try to steal the weapon for you. We would be easy targets for the First Army.
It seems you have liberated yourself from your concern for Lieutenant Sirka's safety.
You could have earned Sechin's true loyalty, if you did not hold her life and those of the others hostage.
Anyone can make promises. I only believe what I see. I am not in the habit of trusting someone who has already betrayed me once. Besides, you don't deserve it.
You people do not deserve kindness. I should have learned my lesson sooner.
We're behind by a day or two, and you act like we've already surrendered to the First Army.
Let me guess what you're planning to do.
At the next communication, you'll tell me that you've dismissed most of the soldiers from the ship to conserve energy, in order to devote full resources to my mission—
I won't, not while Sirka's still at the base—
Then, you will go rogue once the ship has left communications range.
Whether to seize the weapon and use it as leverage to negotiate with me, betray me again and go over to the First Army, or come back alone to attempt an assassination...
You'll have all the choices in front of you once the Volnov has left my control, and your comrades are safe, won't you?
Did you think I wouldn't know about your foolish plan?
You poor, pathetic Volnik...
Has no one told you that this name, which you use to distinguish yourselves from the rest of Ursus, comes from a promise that has never been fulfilled?

lines.loc: Upper Deck, Flagship of the Fourth Army's main fleet

lines.x: Defender Regiments are in position, sir.
Has the vanguard departed the front lines?
According to the reports, yes. There has been no alarm from the Second Army's outposts. All is quiet... is this normal?
That's not for you to think about.
Report the ships' positions to Marshal Kuznetsov, and tell him...
The Fourth Army is ready—
We will advance upon Zelgrad, satellite city of the First Army.
...That will do. One more thing. Reserve two hours before the citizen's forum starts. I would like to meet with Duchess Volkina in the palace.
Yes, sir.
And tell Witte—
—Your Imperial Majesty!
You are not on duty today, Saveliy. Who permitted you to run amok in the Amber Palace like this?
I will take him away, sir. I assure you that this will not happen again.
...Hand him to the Third Bureau. I don't want to see him in here again.
Do with me as you will, sir, but pray listen to me!
The Fourth Army has left their positions and is proceeding towards Zelgrad!
What did you say?
Insolence! Who instructed you to spread such alarmist talk, when not even the Chairman has confirmed the news?
I didn't believe it at first either, but it's the truth!
I was simply helping to keep an eye on things... I never expected such a thing would happen!
They have crossed the Second Army's lines unscathed! I never thought this would happen!
They crossed the lines without engaging in combat? Do you mean—
The Second Army...
The Second Army has gone over to the traitors, sir!
...Evgeny Andrianov.
You never meant for Sechin to take that weapon from Zelgrad, did you?
We're cannon fodder for you to determine the Second Army's cooperation. The other unit that you were talking about is your main force.
You've gambled everything on something that you hardly know anything about. You're out of your mind.
Pushing all of one's chips in is only madness when the outcome is yet uncertain. I forgive you for failing to understand.
But I'm not negotiating with you. There's no need for me to beat around the bush, now that you've finally realized what's happening.
This is the last time I tolerate your probing. Lieutenant Sirka will not be harmed before you fulfill your duties.
Make yourselves useful while you still have value as a diversion, so that I might yet deign to recycle you.
But if you continue on your leisurely pace, you can expect to be left by the roadside when my flagship catches up to the Volnov and crushes you like an ant.
Why does Anatoliy not want me to go with him?
What is he... going to do?
It's better if you don't know.
Please trust in the Generalik. He will not break his promise to you.
...What a pain...
P-Please, sir, I'm begging you! All our research is here, all of it!
But that door, I don't know... I really don't know how to open it!

None of us have the authorization, except Director Alita Valueva, but she...
But she's dea—
ARGH!

lines.st: Dead. Alita, dead?

lines.x: At the back of the group surrounded by soldiers, Klim cannot stop himself from turning his head, looking back at the corpse tossed away in the dark corridor.
He cannot make out anything, yet still he franticly turns his head over and over, until the hilt of a soldier's sword strikes his skull.
(Quietly) Stop that!
Now, as for the rest of you...
Can anyone here tell me why not even my authority is able to work here, hmm?
Am I, perhaps, lower on the totem pole than a lowly lab director?
Silence. Nobody dares to open their mouth without thought, out of fear of the terrible fate that might pounce on them at any time.
You, in the first row, the closest to the corpse. Speak.
Only a small handful of high-level researchers can open that door, out of concerns for a security leak—
Which means even I am locked out of this door?
AIEE—
Don't kill her just yet. Tell me, where are these high-level researchers?
...Th-They w-were all, you—
Oh, how unfortunate. However, since you know so much about it, then surely there must be some sort of emergency opening procedure?
A laboratory like this must has one.
Or do you know, and simply do not wish to tell me?
N-No, sorry, I-I don't know, I'm just speculating based on past experience, it's my job—
Forgive me, Generalik, I—
Useless trash.
*sigh*...
What a waste of time. Kill them, starting from the right-hand side. Keep going until one of them figures out a way to open this, or until they're all dead.
What about the Marshal's orders?
Mother only told me to bring me back results. She said nothing about bringing back the things underground.

So long as I do my best, she will not blame me.
Look. Are these not the results of my hard labor...
The great effort of enduring this headache?
He points towards the corpses and bloodstains scattered across the floor, an innocent smile upon his face.
Yes, sir... Absolutely correct.
I truly don't understand what people see in this thing. If you don't supply it energy, it turns into a bomb. Why not simply blow it up ourselves and start over?
To think it was something like this that forced Mother to abandon Zelgrad... How wretched.

lines.st: That man over there, what's he saying?

lines.x: The man standing at the very back can no longer hear clearly. Those shrieks, those sounds of escape, capture, and execution, they are like an automated assembly line in a factory, occurring without his input.
He does not try to turn his head again. Instead, amidst all this noise, amidst his memories playing on loop, he sees only a glimpse of the corpse of his wife...
He falls to his knees, oblivious to the chaos around him.
Alita...
Hey, get up!
I said, GET UP!
The young man raises a hand, signaling the guards to stop. A sobbing man is yanked to his feet and tossed aside. Then he walks toward the kneeling man.
The panicking, numbed crowd automatically splits to form a passage for the Generalik.
What are you saying? Why are you kneeling?
Alita...
You know this woman?
I couldn't... leave her.
Merely one of the lab's logistics staff, Generalik, in charge of sweeping and such. He's just scared.
No, he must have some connection with that woman who allowed those people to enter the prototype core.
He might know more than the rest. Pull him up, use your swords or whatever to break him out of his daze—
Anatoliy!
Hierda? Why are you—
You didn't listen to me.
It was you who broke our promise this time.
I did not!
Then how do you explain the bodies on the floor, these trembling, pitiful people... and that man kneeling by you?
You're still... You're still hurting them, and hurting yourself at the same time. When you take the lives of others so easily, you increase the weight pressing down on yourself.
I have no way... I have no way of stopping you. I can only look on helplessly as you slide towards ruin. You can no longer know salvation, Anatoliy.
I can, I can still be saved! I just need you to be by my side—always!
Why... Why does everyone always try to coerce me like this?
Mother is disappointed in me, these servants have no respect for me... They all see me as a useless monster. Are you the same?
Anatoliy.
Hm... hm?
Hierda steps forward, gently holding Anatoliy's hands. He is taller than her, lankier than her. His two hands dwarf hers, far larger than the average adolescent.
She holds them, slowly tightening her grip.
I don't know what this monster you speak of actually is, but a true monster wouldn't care about how others see it. A monster's heart only has space for itself.
You are angry because others mock you, you weep because your friends leave you... You feel pain, don't you?
You are always going against your own intentions to hurt others, to the point you can't see just how much you are hurting yourself.
I believe that deep in your heart, you don't want to do this. Your reaction today proves this.
You say that everyone is coercing you.
But I believe.
You believe... you believe in me? This means you won't leave me, right?
I don't want to leave, but if you keep being like this, without the slightest hint of change, I must leave.
You are so very tired. If you continue on, you will collapse. And all I can do is watch as you doom yourself to this future.
Et tu, Hierda...? Have you joined the others in refusing to save me?
It's not that I don't want to, but I can't. I simply cannot. As I said before, I can soothe the pain in your body, but I cannot soothe the scars on your soul.
It weeps blood. Can you not feel it?
You hurt yourself because of your mother's impossible expectations, but why would a mother be this cruel to her own child?
She has tossed you into such circumstance, forcing you to go against your own desires, to destroy a beautiful city, to end so many innocent lives.
She pushed you in front of all her problems. Maybe she believes you can handle them, but if you never had the right to choose, then does she truly believe in you, or...
Are you just a tool to her?
Tools can be replaced, Anatoliy. But you are not a tool, or a monster, are you?
What... What should I do?
Tell me, Hierda. Tell me—
Maybe all you need to do is give her proof.
Proof that you are not a tool, but instead, a human who lives and breathes.
...We've gathered most of the people in this neighborhood, Tulin. Tonya did her best, but not everyone wanted to come.
Reunion's helping us raid the sentry post. We can't afford to waste any time.
Right. Appreciated.
Tonya, you said this was something important, something to do with our lives. You're not lying to us again, right?
No, I'd never.
A crowd of people stand there, sunlight shining on their faces. Many of them look calm, glancing around in puzzlement.
The miners can no longer hold back their rage. They who have returned from the depths of hell can only see such aloofness as hate. They roll up their sleeves and clench their fists...
It's time, Talulah.
Time for?
Time for you to do what you do best: stand up and give a few inspiring words to everyone.
Red... I'm not sure if I still have the right to do that.
'Bam'—
Someone pats her on the back. Talulah turns, and is greeted by Tulin's smile. The ever-cool-headed leader steps forward, standing in front of the crowd.
My Zelgradian friends! My name is Ivan Tulin, and these are my companions behind me.
I am no different from the rest of you. I too am one of the many workers at the beck and call of Ursus, one who has mined in the Northern Tundra for over a decade.

For all those years, the first thing I do every time I left the mines would be to look up at the sky, memorizing the shape of the clouds, the warmth of the sun, the sound birch leaves make when you step on them.
Every time I was deep in the darkest, most dangerous mineshafts, I only had to close my eyes, and those beautiful things would be at my side.
But I could not do so just now.
What I have seen was a hundred times darker than the deepest pit. Underneath your feet, somewhere you cannot see, your fellow Ursines are being brutally murdered.
You mean...?
Some of you saw how we came from the nearby autonomous district. There, we discovered a military lab, and learned their secrets.
Have you ever wondered why Zelgrad opened its doors to those with Oripathy from the rest of Ursus, why all the Infected are being gathered in one place?
It's because the First Army's Originium supplies have nearly run dry! They are burning the Infected like firewood, then performing evil experiments behind those stone walls!
You do not want to know how those Infected are dying, dying with such indignity—
My nephew only had a mild case, but those soldiers still carted him away!
There is still time. We are fighting against the First Army, but we must first keep you all safe.
Keep us safe? From what? What are these 'evil experiments' anyway?
Their research may have led to the spreading of a mysterious disease. Some of you have already seen it for yourselves. Green pustules, spots all over the body—
Some of you even had family who died of it... This is the First Army's unforgivable sin!

News of this strange disease causes the crowd to talk amongst themselves. They talk and they talk, taking note of their conversation partners' expressions. Some faces turn grave, others look towards Tonya.
Is this the weird disease you were talking about, Tonya?

...It is.
The Army covered it up, taking away anyone who caught it to do research...
But that research came at the cost of their lives!
My youngest sister, Nina... Lots of you have seen her, some of you even cradled her...
She caught that disease, and Doctor Nadezhda Pavlovna took her in for treatment, but she still got taken away by those evil men in army clothes... and now—
Nina... She's gone!
As Tonya lifts the swaddling blanket above her head, the raucous crowd falls silent. Many of the residents know that piece of cloth.
They have seen Tonya carry her little sister, wrapped up in that blanket, as she walked between the factories, a blissful smile always on her face.
But we really haven't seen an illness like this before...
Mark's seen it. He looked after Nina for a little while after she got sick. Where is he—
Are you... Mark?
I... I shouldn't have denied you like that, Tonya. I was really, really scared...
But... I can't keep being scared.
He takes off his jacket as he steps forward, revealing terrifying pustules on his skin. The people around him shriek as they back away.
Tonya quickly helps support him. The man who was once her friendly neighbor is now exhausted and weak. This terrifying, debilitating disease has robbed him of most of his ability to even walk.
You have all seen this poor man.
But what you might not have realized is—
If we do not act, if we instead choose to cover our ears and succumb to the apathy they feed us...
This misfortune could fall onto each and every one of us at any time!
The First Army, those self-righteous liars, said the sound of cannons outside the city was to protect us. They said our missing neighbors had 'gone for treatment'...
Lies! Utterly shameless, despicable lies, all of them! When they are not busy beating prisoners, they are busy thinking up new lies.
Their 'secret laboratory' has no doctors, only butchers. They sealed our brothers and sisters in vats, like chopped up pieces of beastmeat.
Is this the 'kindness' Ursus shows us? Are such pitiful souls the Ursines they want to see?

Those who stand above us, those who point their spears at us, they eat the bread we bake, live in the houses we make, and now they come back to us, wanting to turn us into samples of meat for the laboratory bench...
So long as they require it, they will infect us with Oripathy, molding us into whatever form they see fit. It was through these means that they made us impoverished and downtrodden!
Look at the ground beneath your feet. It is rotten to the core. It has rotted and reeked for decades, centuries even.
But now, two paths lie ahead of us.

You can go and be fuel for those vermin, a path where you return to your 'homes', where you line up and wait to be shoveled into their furnaces and stoves, where you lie down in the graves they prepared for us.
Or you can come with me, and leave this damned place. Yes, this path promises only bitter cold, but it is a path you can walk upon your own two feet, a path we were born to walk!
Come! We shall walk away with all our children, all our family, all our friends!
Let them weep over the ruins, let their hollow souls feel the pain of having nothing!
For the sake of all our tomorrows, come with me, and leave this tomb!
As Tulin yells out the last of the speech, the crowd breaks out into enthusiastic shouting of their own. Several familiar faces step up once more—Reunion has routed the nearby sentry post.
Tulin's gaze sweeps across Red, across Sirka, eventually stopping on the one leading them. Tulin locks eyes with Talulah, until the cheers and applause die down.
Talulah does not blink. She saw the expressions on the residents' faces as they looked towards Tulin. She had seen such faces before.
Many years ago, in another plaza, people looked to her this way, with eyes that said, 'So long as we follow Talulah, we can do anything'. Eyes brimming with hope.
Talulah smiles. A smile of relief, maybe. It is as if after countless days of wandering the endless wastes alone, she suddenly sees another pair of footprints walking alongside her.
But there is not just one pair. Countless others walk with her through the Northern Tundra.
Tulin's people are ready, Talulah. They'll be in charge of mobilizing, organizing and evacuating the residents of other districts, while we draw the army's attention, just like we planned.
How are things on your side, Closure?
Ready to head out whenever. Whatever happens, I need to get past that wall.

I'll also be heading to the wall. Anatoliy must be overseeing the research institute...
He escaped me once through sheer luck. It won't save him a second time.
Right. Don't get too caught up in battle, Red. Protecting the residents while they evacuate is our top priority.
Got it.
...Take care, Talulah.
I still have a few things I need to say to everyone in Reunion. You can head off first.
Sure. Let's go, Sirka.
The crowd slowly disperses. Talulah turns around. A red-haired Reproba sits on some steps not too far away, silently watching her.
It's just us here now, Talulah.
Get started with your excuses already. You could've kept skulking around in the shadows, but you chose to show yourself again and stir up trouble for some reason—
I need to apologize to you, Lyudmila.
...What?
Not just to you, but to everyone from that time, to those who believed that I could bring them into the future...
Even if many of them can no longer hear me.
So you came to Zelgrad to atone?
Atonement is beyond me. I just want to do... the things I did not do back then.
(Quietly) ...Enough.
Are you going to go with Closure to find the Sarcophagus?
The young redhead turns her head to look at the crowd heading towards the edge of the city. The din in the background is formed from their footsteps, alongside cannon fire from who-knows-where.
She understands that there is not much time for a chat right now. Whether they want to talk about the past or the future, there are much more pressing matters when countless lives are on the line—
But she speaks all the same.
No.
I should be investigating it thanks to some intelligence I found, but I figured something would go wrong, so I gave that info to some other people who are also looking for it.
If my guess is right... The answer should be inside.
It's a strange feeling. I only learned recently that there's a lot of things I don't have to take on alone.
Besides, you know how it is. If we have to fight in the alleys, my Arts can stop an entire army. My smoke can screen more people while they get out of here.
Lyudmila, what I meant was, your father once gave everything for the Sarcophagus. I'm not trying to change your mind, but if you still have regrets—
Listen, Talulah. I used to hate you, just like how I hated how powerless I was.
Lyudmila...
I hated all the lies and betrayal, until... I suddenly realized one day, all those memories that chained me, they didn't feel so heavy anymore.
Slowly but surely, I found myself with more things I have to do. Like how I should be heading off with those people over there right now.
Ivan Tulin... An amazing one.
Hmph. I've heard that name before. One who writes good essays, ones as sharp as a knife, but what Tulin's really like, that remains to be seen.
I won't believe in perfect leaders again.
You might be right.
So you see, we don't need to keep working together. We have our own battlefields to fight. I need to help people evac, and you...
You need to do the things you haven't done yet.
...Alright.
I will.

lines.loc: Assault Ship Volnov, Command Center Jan 21, 1102, 16:59

lines.x: Then... I still have... one last request.
Oh? And what do you have left that affords you the privilege?
The fact that the Volnov is the closest Fourth Army unit to Zelgrad.
You know I've got a choice. I can choose to 'help' you declare war on the First Army, trigger some mutually assured destruction, the works.
You would rather go down and be reunited with Lieutenant Sirka than be resigned to your fate? How touching.
Then let me hear her voice one more time.
Just one last time.
After that, Sechin will follow your plan to the letter.
Bring her here.
I thank Your High Excellency for your kindness.
...Scioppa—
It is the exact same voice. The same voice he has heard reporting in over staticky comms countless times.
It is unlike the one he hears when they are together, talking face to face. Only on the battlefield, during drills, during dire circumstances when emotions are hard to read—
Does he hear this calm but cold voice.
...I will find you, Sirka.
Don't, Scioppa. Not for me.
It's not just for you. I'm not letting any of my people get banished because of Oripathy again.
I'll find all of you.
...Arrogant fool.
Now, I set off.
But before that, I've got a question for you. The last words you said to me before we got—
Enough, take her away—
—What was it?
I said, take her away!
I have satisfied your final request, Major Razin. Do not push your luck.
Yes, you have satisfied me, and I've got no further requests.
I'm just a little hurt. Seems she's forgotten them already.
But I still remember. Her last words to me were: 'We will not meet again, not until we hear the call of death herself.'
What a cruel woman.
Cut the call.
Roger!
Scioppa Razin! You—
That actually was Sirka, Scioppa—
I'm an idiot.
What?
That wasn't Sirka. It was never Sirka!
It was just a war caster imitating her, using snippets from open comms as a model! How did it take me this long to notice?!
No wonder he didn't let me take that dagger. Probably another product of Arts, unable to keep its shape...
The only bit I understood was you saying that wasn't Sirka. Are you a hundred percent sure?

They analyzed how she speaks, even compiled the details of how she tried to kill herself after they arrested her for extra believability, but it was all wrong. Now that I look back, every single word was wrong.
War casters can't read minds, so they have no idea what Sirka said to me.
Besides, our noble lady wouldn't kill herself the moment she got captured, she'd take down a bunch of them with her.
Hah. Even you saw right through it, while I only just realized. I really am a complete idiot.
Then do we stick to that old bastard's plan?
No... of course not.
Oleg, get everyone who can use concealment Arts up on deck right now. Use the technique I taught you to wipe the Volnov off the positioning systems for a while.
Test all our equipment, Efim. Once the ship is concealed...
I'll give a ship-wide broadcast.

lines.loc: Assault Ship Volnov, Upper Deck Jan 21, 1102, 21:43

lines.x: Huh? New orders from the boss?
He better not be trying to get us off the ship again! I'll hide in the boiler room if I have to—
All hands on the Volnov, this is Scioppa Razin.
So formal... What's going on?
First, let's forget all the foolish decisions I made earlier. Once everything's been settled, you can turn around and have a good laugh at me.
This next part of the announcement is more important, though.
I've already transferred all command authority to Oleg Khmelnytsky, a fine fellow you all know and love.
What?
Transferring command authority...
Where're you going, Chief?
...Ever since that annihilation operation in December, I've found myself thinking about what 'Volnik'—maybe even the 'Sechin' made up of us Volniki—actually means.
In peace time, we're relatively privileged, looking after the land outside the cities for the tsar, but at the same time, we have to face Catastrophe, along with unending migration and separation.
In war time, we're valiant fighters, the sharpest, nimblest blade in any army's arsenal. But we're forever outsiders, never fitting in, never allowed to die with even a little dignity.
I often wonder, does it really have to be this way? We non-Ursus have been living and dying like this for so long, but is this actually right?
But now I know. It's not right. So we need to get ourselves out of this mess.
...To be honest, I should've realized before we wandered into the clutches of the Fourth Army.

The past exploits of our people have already been forgotten. Even deeds as recent as our parents' generation, where they served as the vanguard for both sides of the Great Rebellion, have been lost to history, their names unrecorded.
And now, will we follow the same road they did, a road that ends only in the blackness of death?
No, no we won't.
You tell 'em, boss...
As your chief, I should be fighting for you all. Even if all I'm fighting for is a chance to break free of our chains.

Upon the deck, inside the control center, in the boiler room, in the corners of the storeroom, countless men and women lift their heads to listen to their chieftain's speech. They silently nod, or they wait in doubt.
They feel ripples echoing across their hearts as they hear these words, even if they do not fully understand their meaning.
Sirka hasn't been captured by Evgeny Andrianov. We were all taken in by his lies.
And the entire reason he used such a despicable scheme was to ruthlessly send us into the front lines against the First Army as cannon fodder—
Well, we're not just going to sit back and let them kill us.
Some people who are already dead said it best. Ursus is burning down, we just never saw the flames.
The mines in the north are shut, and so are the factories in Central. Angry workers march through the streets with weapons in hand. Even students are lifting their skinny fists in resistance—
I say it's time. Time for us to ask Ursus to honor our promise.
Our ship and her crew are no longer in the 'terrorizing commoners' business.
I want us to leave the Fourth Army, leave anywhere that would treat us only as weapons.
I want freedom for the Volniki, true freedom, even if it means meeting with the Viy.
Hah...
I declare that the Volnov will not be heading towards Zelgrad. From now on, the Special Tactics Formation 'Sechin' is no longer a part of the Fourth Army.
I will personally inform Kuznetsov—
—Who?!
Mutineering, instigation, insubordination...
You have violated martial law. You have betrayed your orders.
You all... should die.
The very next moment, space warps around Scioppa. He senses himself being dragged into a free-floating space, apart from the ship.
'Morvan'. This is clearly 'frozen space', a place that leaves the one being interrogated feeling like they are being eaten away by fire, both mentally and physically.
He knows this is only an illusion, but it also means he has to use all his mental fortitude and more to break free of it.
Kuznetsov's personal guard... The war casters.
It's only been a few years, but I don't recognize your uniforms at all now. Did they rework how they make you people, or did Evgeny have other designs for you?
The war caster does not reply. Several streams of Arts fly towards him like arrows without the caster even raising their hand, piercing through his flesh.
His one and only warning.
Gah—!
Major Scioppa Razin, commander of Special Tactics Formation, Sechin.
In the name of Marshal Evgeny Andrianov Kuznetsov of the Fourth Army, I give you your final orders.
'Direct your men to continue onwards. You are not permitted to rest before you reach Zelgrad.'
If the Volnov deviates in the slightest, or slows for even a second, all hands on deck will immediately be executed. Without exception.
The ship will continue on to Zelgrad, carrying your corpses.
Dammit!
Those cowards, hiding behind their bunkers. We don't really know the lay of the land behind the wall, so it's hard to break through their defenses.
How much longer until Talulah gets here?
There's a lot of enemies on her side, I reckon she'll need a little more time.
Like she said, all we have to do is pin down the defenders until she comes to reinforce—
Err... What was that—
As soon as the words leave his mouth, another shell flies over his head, heading towards his comrades behind him.
Just as he thinks about telling them to duck for cover, a drone swoops past him, intercepting the shell in midair. Even so, the resulting explosion shakes the ground.
Wh-What the... Closure?!
Behind him, countless whirring drones rise into the air, whistling as they fling themselves into the incoming shells.
Heh, no need to wait for her to save you.

Thanks to you guys buying time, my EM interference countermeasure's complete.
Bunkers scanned, enemy signals marked, spontaneous combustion safeguards disabled—
Go, show them what you've got!
The drones head towards the stone wall's gates one after the other. Not long after, explosions and the wails of Ursine soldiers ring out from behind the bunkers.
The defenders were clearly caught on the back foot by this chaotic assault. They flail at the flying lumps of iron, unable to conceal their positions any longer.
Since when were drones this useful? If we had this kind of firepower...
Whatever, now's our chance! Charge!

Hehe...
Mission complete!
She lets out an involuntary snap of the fingers.
You...
Heh, we took care of this spot earlier than planned. The side gate is ours.
But there's still plenty of defenders inside, Talulah. I'll need your help.
...Understood.
Go find the Rhodes Islanders, Closure. Leave the soldiers to me. Reunion will make sure they don't get in your way.
I still have quite the score to settle with these people.
...Bzzt... Hailing... Colonel Nikonov...
...The enemy's breached the wall, lighting fires everywhere they go. Nobody's answering when I call the garrisons...

...Need a report on your command center, stat. The fuel factory's our top priority. We need to protect the Infected resources, we can't let them fall into enemy hands! If there's any danger, execute the contingency plan—
A hand reaches out, picking up the communicator on the fallen man's body.
What contingency plan?
...Who are you?
The one who picked up this communicator. Your colonel died by my hand not too long ago.
What do you think you're doing?!
All you need to know is that you're next.
She clenches her fingers. The voice whines as the communicator is crushed, the shattered fragments slipping between her fingers, tinkling as they fall onto the floor.
We've taken care of the remaining soldiers outside, Talulah. Plan said Closure's going ahead to find the Sarcophagus, while Sirka's looking for the Generalik.
As for the 'fuel factory' we're searching for, some of our captives said it's here.
How convenient. One of their officers said the same thing just now.
Open the door.
The steel door slowly swings open, revealing rows of man-sized vats inside. A few people narrow their eyes. They may be veterans of the battlefield, but they still dread what they are about to see.
But they are surprised. This place is not exactly the same as the factory outside. These vats have red lights flashing under them. Talulah steps forward, peering into the first vat she sees.
She sees a young woman, her body intact. Countless slender tubes are attached to her mouth and nose, the Originium crystals on her body glimmering a dark yellow.
These lights are on, unlike the ones in the expansion plate...
I saw it! That girl's eyelids just twitched!
They can still be saved. Turn off the main breaker first.
As the breaker switch is pulled with an ear-piercing screech, a blade flashes.
The glass in front of Talulah shatters into pieces, the oily preservation fluid gushing out and splattering across her feet.
The woman is slowly pushed out the vat by the force of the spilling liquid. Talulah helps her up with one hand, using her other to pull away the tubes all over her.
Still conscious... Quick, save the rest of them!
Got it!

Renewed hope snaps everyone out of their reverie. The dread they felt earlier has become a force propelling them as they charge towards the rest of the vats. For a moment, all that can be heard in the room is the sound of glass breaking and varied greetings.
...I... Am I safe...?
Yes, you're safe.
I swear to you, you will never have to see those people ever again.
Reunion...
What?
You must be... Only Reunion would save us. I knew it, everyone knew it...
When they brought us here, many people cried, especially the children... Until some people told us stories about you. Everyone... began to believe.
But those officers stopped us, saying Reunion was just a bunch of crazy terrorists...
But we're in Ursus. Only madmen care about the Infected in the first place.
Thank... you...
But... where's the white-haired Liberi? Isn't she with you?
What did you say? A white-haired Liberi?
Before you arrived, a white-haired Liberi came by. She told us we had to hold on, that people would be coming to save us soon!
And she said—
Never give up struggling. The meek will become weak.
Only those with strength have the right to survive.
We've gotten the rest of them out, Talulah. We need to be quick, the other factories have Infected waiting for us.
...Right. Help her up, and get her out of here.
I'll take care of this place.
The two leave, her comrade propping up the weakened young woman as they go. Talulah slowly gets up, walking towards the door before turning her head.
The 'factory' now lays still. Spilled fluid coats the entire floor, reflecting the last vestiges of light in the distance.
She stretches out her hand, as if waving goodbye. Flames spring out of every corner of the room, engulfing the turquoise stone.
The endless toil of the Infected stops now.
...Nobody here?
There is not a soul in the giant room, only a fireplace that crackles as it burns.

Sirka approaches the desk. Books and files are scattered all over it. She rummages through them, pulling out a sheet covered in symbols from the bottom of the pile, a shiny fresh signature in the bottom right corner.
...Anatoliy—
Who's there?
Hmm? Strange... I heard a voice just now.
Suddenly, he feels an iron grip around his neck, one strong enough to lift him off his feet. He is flung into a pillar, which breaks with a dull thump.
Before the lone soldier can recover from the head-churning dizziness and pain, a knife is pressed against his back. It slips through his clothes, its tip sticking ever so slightly into his skin.
Anatoliy's whereabouts, or your life.
I... I'll talk!
It was a few hours ago... The Generalik got some news, so he left this place with his bodyguards in a hurry.
What news?

I don't know...
AHH—
H-He said: 'Those degenerates are unfit to have a piece of Zelgrad', then he got really angry, saying he had to take something away.
'Those degenerates'? Where did he go after that? Is he still in the city?
He looped around a few of the labs—they all had something to do with the prototype core—then he headed for the east of the city... Please, I don't know anything about what he was talking about!
...I see.
Just to be safe, you cannot tell anyone that I was here.
Yes, yes, I would never—
Before he can even finish, the knife has pierced his chest, nailing him to the pillar as blood streams down it.
Sirka shakes the blood off her blade as she looks outside the window.
'Prototype core'. Is that the 'Sarcophagus' they were talking about...?

opts: The Sarcophagus was dismantled...?
What's its status?

lines.x: Ursus sees the Sarcophagus as a giant energy source. Nothing beyond that function matters to them at all.
The researchers here had no way of breaking through the lockdown procedure Kal'tsit implemented, so they decided to use brute force to crack it open.
Based on what I can see, we're now in our worst-case scenario. The Sarcophagus's biological restoration function is completely destroyed...

opts: Do we still have a chance?
Surely there's still some hope left?

lines.x: It's still possible if we can restore everything perfectly!
But there's something we need to take care of first. The Sarcophagus's control system is extremely damaged! It's very unstable right now.
I knew it... The researchers had to rely on massive amounts of Originium to just barely keep it stable. Now that the Originium supply is gone, it's about to go critical.
The Sarcophagus is constantly leaking out that infectious bio-dust even now, and its energy output is fluctuating heavily!
If the energy contained within goes completely out of control and escapes, I'm afraid it's not just going to be all of Zelgrad that's razed to the ground...
Mon3tr! Can we still shut it down?
I'm trying my best here!
I can't just flip the switch Kal'tsit installed, I need to begin with a complete control system—Basically, I need time!
It's the soldiers outside! Are they still trying to force their way in?
No, the entire building is under attack.
This is the First Army we're talking about. Were they prepared to completely destroy the place?
Do these damn reckless Ursines ever think about the consequences?!
As the building shakes, countless strange, monstrous creatures gush out of the Sarcophagus's core in an unending stream.
They appear to be lost and afraid, milling about in confusion within the enclosed space.
Those are like that organism I saw that night—
Amiya, Raidian! Do NOT let those things touch you!
Shit, if only I had a hand free—
How much time do you need, Mon3tr?
Around... forty minutes.
...Alright.
Don't get distracted. I'll protect Amiya and the Doctor.
Sorry for making you do this, Dive...
Wait, there's movement outside. The door might not hold much longer!
Get behind me, Doctor, I'll protect you—
No, this signal is familiar—
Whew... Made it! Did I get here on time?
Closure?!
Amiya! I knew you guys could do it! I was still really worried, though!
Eww, the heck are these things crawling on the ground?!
Watch out! Those infected lifeforms are dangerous, don't let them touch you!
Then what should I do? Will they explode or something?
I need you to help limit their movement range. My little Cycle doesn't have enough ammo.
So you're just lacking firepower? This'll be a cinch, then!
Zeroth Order Oil Tank!
An orderly array of drones rises up into the air behind Closure, like an impenetrable wall.
I always thought this move was too unsporting, so I never pulled it out in a real combat situation... but it's finally coming in handy now.
Perfect timing for a field test of those weapon modules I just installed...
Zeroth Order Oil Tank, identify targets, then wipe them all out!

opts: Closure! How did you get in here?

lines.x: A genius hacker-engineer has her ways! Though I did run into a fair few helpers along the road here...
That ID code Gummy got us turned out pretty handy, too. You'll never guess who I ran into outside the wall, Doctor!

opts: As long as you're safe.
Tell me later.

lines.x: I knew you guys would find the Sarcophagus core. So, can we finally—
Closure! Help me!
Okay, coming!
It's rare seeing you this stressed out, Mon3tr. What's the sitch?
THE SARCOPHAGUS IS ABOUT TO EXPLODE!
...IT WHAT?!
Raidian...
I'm... fine...
How long has it been?
About an hour.
Believe in them...
Raidian and Closure's drones work together to form a defensive line, corralling the dangerous infected creatures within a safe zone.
At the other end of the room, Mon3tr and Closure are hard at work at the control panels.
Everyone stays silent. Nobody dares to ask if their labors have borne fruit.

opts: Any results yet?!
...How's it looking?

lines.x: Doctor, we...
No...
Nonononono—
We did so many tests, we should know this thing inside and out, so why—
Closure keeps mumbling. Despite her best efforts, the Sarcophagus does not respond to her, yet she keeps working its controls.

lines.st: Error

lines.x: Doctor... The Sarcophagus is at its limit. We don't have time to shut it down using the proper protocols.
The only thing we can do now, before it goes out of control and unleashes disaster...
Is to destroy it completely.
Doctor... It's time to decide.
If... If Kal'tsit were here, she'd agree to it.
Mon3tr speaks as calmly as possible, rendering the cruelest of judgments.
There is no time.
The Sarcophagus is no longer something that gives you hope you can bring your comrade back, but instead something that threatens to wipe out everything.
Though you harbored the sincerest of wishes, you must now make the decision to abandon your one and only chance. You must decide.
Why are you hesitating?
Ah...
Pretty rare to see you so careless. Distracted by something?
Yeah... I'm worried about the team that went to Ursus.
Having to wait for such up-in-the-air results isn't a very nice feeling.
You've never been like this in front of the Doctor.
I just didn't want to bring down morale, doesn't mean I don't care.
Once you're as old as me, you'll know what this sort of separation feels like.
Not exactly the nicest thing you could wish me...
Whew... And with that, Engineering is now rebuilt! That was one hell of a project!
When the Doctor and Amiya bring Dr. Kal'tsit back, they'll be in for a shock!
It really was quite the project...
Not to be a downer, but are you really so sure the Doctor will succeed?
Of course I am.
I believe in the little bunny and the Doctor. It's that simple.
No particular reason?
If we needed reasons to believe in each other, we might as well quit being elite operators, right?
Fair enough.
We should get their welcome party ready.
Like we always do.

opts: Kal'tsit!
How much longer are you going to keep your secrets?

lines.x: We've discussed this. I thought we had reached an understanding.
You cannot simply ask people to pass your memories like they are a cup of coffee. Anything relayed to you by others lacks objectivity.

opts: Are you planning to just watch as I stumble in the dark?
It's hard for an amnesiac to do their job.

lines.x: Believe me when I say that you are not the only person who has to bear the vexation of not getting what they want.
One day in the future, you will understand my patience.
I will not tell you about your past of my own accord, but I will help you in all other matters when needed.

opts: Sometimes I can't tell...
If you care about me, or if you want to make things difficult for me.

lines.x: I really do care about you, far more than you can imagine.
Like I have said before, I will restrain myself and not allow my hatred towards you—or any other emotion—to cloud my judgment.
But I will always protect you, until you recover your memories, or you find yourself.
Only once that time comes can we discuss what it means for you to exist here.
You've already found yourself, haven't you?
You fully understand your duty, and know the road you insist on walking.
So go, make what you have always believed was the right choice.

'Protect the life on this great land'...
Rhodes Island will not stop because of the loss of any one person.
You will all see a different tomorrow.

opts: Mon3tr...
We'll do as you said—

lines.x: Did you do something just now, Mon3tr?
What...? No, not a thing!
But then why would a backdoor with such high authorization suddenly appear in the system? If it was here all along, how come those researchers never found it?

Waitwaitwait, this isn't just your regular security vulnerability... Why does the Sarcophagus's OS have an independently-operating program like PRTS?!
It's slow-going...
But it's shutting down the Sarcophagus!
Could it be—

opts: AMa-10?
Kal'tsit?

lines.x: I want to fix it too.
Not only does AMa-10 carry our hopes, it has also preserved a record that is very important to me.

opts: Closure!
Can you trace the program?!

lines.x: Already on it! Just need a little more time!
Five minutes... No, three! Just buy me three! I've still got a shot!
But the Sarcophagus is extremely dangerous right now! I don't know how much longer it will hold!
What... What if we can suppress its energy? Will it stabilize?
Amiya?!
Absolutely not! Not even you can hold back its power output by yourself!

If we don't try... then how can we ever know...?
Besides, I can feel... the Black Crown answering my call...
I believe I can do it.
Theresa... Have you come to help me?
Amiya... I have not.
Your request violates the baseline command Theresa installed in me—
No matter the situation, prioritize Amiya's safety. Your safety.
But you also said I shouldn't make a choice I would regret.
Are you sure you wish to do this, Amiya?
This time... I will do everything I can. Everything.
I don't want to lose anyone by my side again.
The ancient superstructure lets out a terrifying whine. You can feel your innards vibrate alongside it, even though all you are doing is standing nearby.
You are unable to comprehend the frightening amount of energy contained by this machine.
Amiya stretches out her hands towards it. Black Arts flow from her fingertips, holding firm as they suppress the sheer force pouring out of the Sarcophagus. Its core begins to calm.
Urghhhh—!
Amiya!
I'm fine... Don't worry...
The day... The day Dr. Kal'tsit shielded me, is a day I'll never forget...
Every time, it's someone else who protects me...
But this time... I won't let go this time—
I can—
Once more, you witness pure power burst out of Amiya's slight frame.
You stretch out your own arm to support her. You too can sense the churning sea of emotion, the font of her strength.
Unwavering determination, countless regrets, the dread of separation... and a warmth that now only exists in memory, a deep reluctance to say goodbye.
You have all walked this long path together. You have all lost so much along the way.
You do your best to prop her up by the shoulder, trying to calm her like you always do, and share in her pain... But all that power, all that roiling emotion, is endlessly deep.
You can clearly hear the sound of some instrument shattering.

opts: Closure!
How much longer do we need to hold?!

lines.x: Soon—No, it's done!
That's enough, Amiya!
It's stopped, but—

opts: What... is this place?

lines.st: If you ever have the chance to leave a snippet of language behind for civilizations to come, a language they can decipher, what would you choose?
Why ask that, all of a sudden? Is this the latest personality test you've found?
Let me give it a proper thought... How about the Esperanta Principle? A complete and universal language might be the best way for a civilization to advance to its next stage.
What about you?
Perhaps... a poem...

lines.x: AMa-10's environmental adaptability test results are very promising. We may soon be able to take this little thing with us for a stroll on the surface.
Doctor... Oh, are you deciding which poetry anthologies to import into its storage module?
I think this might be what that generation, having lived through the age of silence, needed most. The life to come will need something to help them make it through the growing pains of civilization.
I considered installing a star chart consisting of trillions of stars in AMa-10's storage module as well, to show them the cosmos as it should be.
But it would be too large, too distant. The vastness of the firmament cannot soothe an immediate loneliness.
I hope that within these fragments of language, they see the beauty of the world, and hear the instinctual cries of life... and I hope they will recognize that these truly are beauties.
It might not have been part of AMa-10's original purpose, but I am rather fond of romantic plans such as this.
I know you've never hidden your partiality towards AMa-10 out of all our research projects, all because it most closely resembles life's form, correct?
I'm not sure... if this is the form life should have.
You placed your hopes in AMa-10, as well as the distant future. A rather heavy gift for them, is it not?
Perhaps we never had the right to gift anything to the people who come after, and we never will. We never owned the universe. We are simply vagrants in time's flow.
We expended all our time and knowledge, yet all our accomplishments were simply an attempt to demonstrate to our successors the value of life's continuation.
We've already found our own answers. I hope this thing is intelligent enough to understand its mission.
I am also looking forward to seeing how it will praise our poetry when relaying it to civilizations in the far future.
Will AMa-10 understand these poems?
I believe you will, won't you?
Live in hope, AMa-10. This is the greatest wish I can offer you.
We pushed ourselves to our limits, but we were still unable to part the deepest veil of the cosmos, the riddle of life.
We do not know why it arose in this vast universe, or why it is so easily snuffed out, like a candle's flame.
But you and yours may be able to push aside that veil, like the first man who discovered fire.
Live... Live, and you will see that future.

Outside the porthole, a matrix of countless co-orbiting satellites glisten and glimmer. The final beacon of civilization before eternal night descends. Upon this lonely ark, scholars still speak of hope.
But even so, the stars are fading away. Nobody can change this fact.
And then, the dark tide arrives on schedule. A simple streak of spray, and the afterglow of this once glorious civilization is extinguished.
...Then comes a very long wait.
You're still here, AMa-10.
Good, walk with me...
I'm the only one left, correct?
'Lynchpin'...
I cannot deny it. My actions are indeed a form of betrayal.
Is this your punishment for my transgressions? I am filled with regret... but I will accept it.
I have to see the world outside, see the current condition of this planet. I may still be able to find some surprising discoveries.
I'm afraid it will be very difficult for me to return here, but for the sake of giving this body of mine sufficient time to explore...
Maybe... I can find... another Sarcophagus...
The scholar steps onto a road that leads into the unknown.
The scholar is unaccustomed to talking, perhaps because the accompanying machine is similarly silent. A poor conversation partner, all things considered.
The scholar maintains this silence when observing everything across this great land, occasionally jumping in joy thanks to some minor discoveries.
Sometimes, the scholar will habitually shout, shouting at the valleys, shouting at the snowfields, shouting until a seizing up of the throat.
Language has lost all meaning. There is nothing to communicate with here, so naturally there are no people who can understand such actions of despair.
This great land never responds to the scholar's passion. It lies there, as quiet as the universe.
But most of the time, the scholar simply looks up at the star-strewn sky in silence.

The scholar might be able to recite the names of every single visible star. It is clear that the star chart that was unable to be saved in AMa-10's storage module now resides within that erudite mind.
'Look at all these stars, dying and being born. Perhaps we can decipher the poetry of the universe from their rhythm.'
The scholar extends a finger, tracing every journey among the stars with her upon the dark canvas of night. A game to while away time.
But time too has lost all meaning.
Until there comes a day, a day after a hundred thousand million nights on this planet.
A meteor streaks across the northwest sky, leaving a blazing scar across the heavens.
Ah... Ahh...!
The scholar stammers, tears of excitement streaking down weathered cheeks.
The scholar is overcome with joy, trembling while climbing, running, sprinting towards where the meteor fell, but then comes a stumble after a few steps.
The scholar no longer has the strength to complete this journey.
AMa-10... Help me up.
Yes... I'm too tired.
We should be leaving behind proof that life continues to have worth, not a silent gravestone.
I once thought that 'life', this word we created, might have some other definition somewhere else in the universe.
Relieving this confounding loneliness is not the only reason why we want to solve the riddle of life's origin...
'Life' might mean much more than us.
I believe in them. I believe in you, Kal'tsit.
Kal'tsit. I do not have much time left.
Search for traces of life. Search for hope and a future.
Kal'tsit... Go find your own answer.
Find yourself.
And so, the scholar returns to that silent, rigid coffin.
The intricate machine halts by the side of the Sarcophagus. It requires some time to slowly process the scholar's parting words.
It waits, a wait as long as the last one, perhaps longer, until it finally believes the one reclining within the Sarcophagus will not awake within the 'short term'.
It thinks about the task the scholar left it.
And so, its only choice is to set off.
During its wait, Originium spread itself throughout every corner of the planet. What it sees is no longer familiar to it.
From the planet's south it leaves, heading northwards.
It wants to find traces of that meteor that brought hope.
Finally, at the furthest reaches of the land's north, it discovers signs of plant seeds being piled together.
Signs of life.

lines.st: (Unknown language) Hello.

lines.x: (Imitating sound)

lines.st: (Unknown language) I can search for the closest water source with you.

lines.x: (Perplexed sound)

lines.st: Do not be afraid. This is your home.
This is Terra.

lines.x: Kal'tsit! Kal'tsit!
I helped you find these, so you should help us exterminate all those long-furred beasts creeping around!
They seized most of the forest's water, along with the fruit!
You should help us wipe them out!

lines.st: I will do no such thing.

lines.x: Why not?!

lines.st: An intervention from an external force will warp the development of civilization. This runs counter to my mission.

lines.x: But I helped you find lots of bugs you need for your 'research' thing!

lines.st: Thank you, but I still cannot help you. I am sorry.

lines.x: I don't understand a thing you're saying! What's a 'mission'? What's this 'civilization' you mentioned, Kal'tsit?

lines.st: I suppose you can call it... a type of order.
It exists in many forms, with no simple definition.
It is an ordering of life that arises naturally, the objective consequence of life's actions. The word 'civilization' is merely a summary of this transient phenomenon.
