It is everything a community requires to continue on. It can offer life protection, but it is exceedingly fragile in itself.

lines.x: Like a nest that gets blown over in a gust of wind.

lines.st: Indeed.

lines.x: But surely you agree with me that when it comes to building nests, you should ask us fliers to make it, right? That's what we're good at!
I promise you! As long as you help us drive out those furry beasts so we can secure this patch of forest, we'll help you build this 'nest' of yours!

lines.st: All life is equal. I will not deprive any community the chance to multiply and expand.

lines.x: How could those ugly things possibly be equal to us? They haven't even learned your language!

lines.st: I am afraid that is not the only factor I have to consider when making a judgment.

lines.x: You really are a stupid animal, you know?
Wait... What's this? I didn't think there would be so many of these black rocks buried inside the mountain. I've never seen rocks like these before!
What kind of rock is this, Kal'tsit?
It was a day more than two thousand years after Oracle fell into slumber.
In a northern corner of the land, the newborn life upon this planet discovered something Oracle was never able to find...
Another Sarcophagus.
Let's call it here, Kal'tsit.

lines.st: Why?
We agreed to use the Sarcophagus to heal your wounds.
We are close.

lines.x: Even if you do heal me, I'm just an ancient chicken. I've never met a chicken who's lived as long as me.

lines.st: Your flock still needs you right now.
I need you to give them a warning, otherwise this cold winter will kill them all.

lines.x: Is this... my 'mission'?

lines.st: I have no way of forcing you to do this.

lines.x: Save it, Kal'tsit...
I don't want to... become like you.
Don't get me wrong, Kal'tsit. I like you, even though I don't like this four-legged furry form you've taken on.
But... I am very tired. Every single feather on me aches. I don't want to fly anymore.
I hope you never learn what this feels like.
Kal'tsit... Did you ever find that 'nest' of yours?

lines.st: I am not sure.
This land is now marked by the footprints of many lifeforms, but their actions have yet to surpass primitive instinct.

lines.x: If you don't have one, how will you make it through the winter?
It's so cold... Kal'tsit, is there anything you can do to make me feel better?

lines.st: I can recite you a poem.

lines.x: Oh, those 'spells' I don't understand a word of again.
Fine, go ahead... Listening to you beats hearing the wind screaming in my ear.

lines.st: People pour love into life and long for salvation whether in hope or fear. That's why they choose to pray to gods that they've never seen...
—That life may never end.
But how could it come true? Even the most tired river must eventually flow into the ocean.
When the final moment comes, when sun, moon and stars fade... when the swaying waves no longer murmur, when all sound and sights are gone.
When the colors of winter and spring are no more, and the boundary of night and day blurs—
And only eternal slumber in endless night remains.

lines.x: Bye bye, Kal'tsit.
Here, the bird ends its unended journey. The only thing she can do is bury her long-time companion in the tundra, not far from the Sarcophagus.
She was unable to find another in its community she could communicate with, and without a timely warning, the flock did not survive the winter.
Yet another long, long, long span of time passes.
It is a tribe who has learned to wield spears that rediscover this relic.
These Ancients who found it considered it divine, kneeling before it in prayer day and night. But news of the relic spread quickly, attracting other tribes.

People treated this inscrutable artifact as something more precious than water. They argued with each other in languages the others did not understand. The conflict quickly turned deadly, resulting in a massacre.
The first tribe to discover the relic was the first to be driven away, barely a tenth of their number left to take the tribe's children somewhere far, far away.
The last tribe standing paid a bitter price as well. Before they could celebrate their victory, a plague born from the corpses strewn everywhere killed every single survivor.
None of this should have happened... but how was it supposed to be stopped?
Is this the civilization that should be protected?
Perhaps it is not that they are inferior, but that they cannot make rational choices based only on the knowledge they have.
Perhaps the only thing separating them from past glory is time. One should not yet conclude that this young civilization ought to be abandoned.
But why... does all of this feel so sorrowful?
Perhaps... try inscribing all knowledge related to the Sarcophagus on this cliff.
From the most basic of mathematics, to the laws governing the flow of energy through the universe... No, start with the most basic semiotics.
She wants to carve all these knowledge-laden characters onto the rocks.
Once more people discover this relic of the past, they will understand what they must do is study, not engage in meaningless murder.
...But this mountain is far too small.
Far, far too small, too small to contain so long a time.
She has no other choice but to take this heavy gift from the prior civilization, and bury it deep underground once more.
It's close by.

lines.st: Are you sure you wish to do this?

lines.x: Of course I do. I once held the land in the palm of my hand, but now, I have nothing. All I have left is sincerity shining bright.
I believe I now understand. There is no eternal king upon this land. I only seek a long life, long enough for me to ponder the truth of this great land.
O great prophet, eternal sage, my most beloved of stars... Please, tell me...
I have conquered vast swaths of territory, plundered more grain and riches than I can enjoy in one lifetime, and the people of my kingdom shall forever praise my name.
...But why do I still feel so lost? Do our lives have a purpose beyond these things?

lines.st: I am sorry, but I do not know the answer to this question.

lines.x: If even you are unable to answer it, then I fear nobody on this land can.
Then, if I enter this coffin, will I be able to find it?

lines.st: If you enter, you may not obtain the answer you desire.
But you will certainly lose everything you have. You will sever your connection with everything in this world.
You will no longer be able to live as a 'man'.

lines.x: Perhaps that is what I need.
The king enters the coffin without the slightest hesitation.
Not long after, it reopens, and a creature with a pair of great wings flies out from within. The form that life took millennia ago.

The Elder, having gained its freedom, spirals through the sky, peering out over the land beneath its feet for a long, long time. Eventually, it lets out a resounding cry before charging through the clouds, never to be seen again.
It has been a while, Kal'tsit.

lines.st: I came to seek your aid.
The contamination leaking from the northern stargate grows graver by the day. It is an issue the people of today are unable to handle.
If you do not help, this threat from without will extinguish all life in this land.

lines.x: You really have changed, Kal'tsit.
The old you wouldn't have gotten involved in the survival of these young peoples so readily.

lines.st: This land is a cruel land, not affording these immature civilizations the slightest kindness.
Life on Terra needs help.

lines.x: Am I hearing the invitation of a guardian of civilization, or the request of a Terran, Kal'tsit?

lines.st: I am simply a beacon asking for your help, in place of a civilization teetering on the brink.
By this measure, who I am is unimportant.

lines.x: You were always in the habit of standing apart, Kal'tsit... I still remember how you looked when you first set foot upon this land millennia ago. You looked completely different back then.
Your current appearance... Time has molded you, Kal'tsit.
The age-old wanderer lowers her head. A mirror-sheen lake reflects a sky full of stars, alongside a face speckled with hints of weariness.

opts: Quick...
I found her...

lines.x: She broke her connection with that space just now, information flow is rapidly dwindling—
Come and help me out here, Mon3tr! I'm going to cut-and-paste all of Kal'tsit's base-level code out, I can't afford to leave a single line behind!
Data dump storage in position. Now, imagine this is a piece of hundred-percent reliable equipment...
I can't imagine something like that—
Then think of a way to use that telepathic link of yours to help me stabilize this weird code!
What are you even talking about?!
What I mean is, hold it steady!
Within the ad-hoc data dump storage, coded to be transparent, green 'calcite' emits a dazzling radiance.
We did it... I can feel it.
It's amazing, isn't it? Both Kal'tsit and I used to be this small.
Closure does not immediately move to speak.
She does not even blink, staring at the storage's information display as it performs its pre-installed diagnostics, until she can confirm the code's self-cycling thread is still running.
The true end of the code relocation.
Oh, thank goodness! The Sarcophagus's energy output is stabilizing too!
But this is just the first step. This temporary storage has limited separation abilities, we can't keep Kal'tsit in there forever. Next, we need to find a relatively quiet environment—
Why the cluck is it so damn dark in here?!

lines.loc: Zelgrad Sealed District, Sarcophagus's Core Jan 22, 1102, 14:33

lines.x: Ah, I think I can see—
...People?

opts: Is this another infected lifeform?
Can infected lifeforms... speak?

lines.x: I can sense soldiers outside attacking this place, Doctor. And this isn't the space we were just in, we've returned to where we started—
Hmm? What is this?
That's rich coming from a girl with rabbit ears growing out of her head. What, never seen a chicken before?
This thing wasn't here when we came in!
Stop shouting, you're giving me a headache!
Listen, I'm no 'infected lifeform', and I'm no 'thing' either! I'm a chicken, a hen! Is that so hard to understand?

opts: That term sounds rather familiar...
But you look like a little house.

lines.x: Shush!
(Shakes feathers) (Looks around)
Something's not right...
Didn't Kal'tsit bury me outside that black thing? Explain to me both why I'm not dead, and why I woke up inside this thing.

opts: This is the Sarcophagus's 'observation room'.
Welcome to ten thousand years in the future.

lines.x: (Indescribable barrage of clucks) WHAT—

opts: First, we need to think of a way to get out of here.
This miniature house knew Kal'tsit, we need to take it with us.

lines.x: Err...
Did you... stop the Sarcophagus?
Wait, how did you get in here? I thought you stayed up top—
You walked away so fast, I didn't have the chance to ask... That ID code of yours means you must know Lada, right?

Are you... Are you her father? And the one who helped Closure get in?
Then you must know Alita Valueva—
The man shakes his head, letting out a distracted smile.
That's my Lita. I never could keep up with her.
Oh, you were asking about the Sarcophagus, right? Let me see...
It's currently stabilizing. The weaponized modules melted down during the energy offset. Right now, the energy output module is the only one still operating.
Ah, that's... that's great to hear. Lita always made the right choice.
You saved a lot of people. I should... I should thank you.
We should thank you too. Once we sort everything out here—

You should leave immediately. The First Army is about to abandon this place.
When I was outside, their comms often mentioned.. the Fourth Army.

But isn't the Fourth Army still at the borders of the Central Governorate?
Are they coming to take the Sarcophagus?!
I don't know... Nobody knows all the details.

opts: We can't let any of the Armies get their hands on the Sarcophagus.
We need a way to hide it for the time being.
The energy gathered within has one logical outlet.
We can use this outlet to drop the energy reaction to its minimum.

lines.x: ...You've thoroughly gathered information, and you're rather intelligent.
Alright, leave this to me. You should escape, and go do what you're supposed to do.

Are you going to stay here by yourself?!
This place is getting blasted by cannons! We can deal with it together, then get out of here together!
Enough...
My wife died here... At least give us one last bit of alone time.
But—
...I might not look it, but I'm actually one of the researchers here, too.
Now that some are dead and the rest have fled, I must stay and see this place through to the very end...
That is my responsibility.
A large hole has been blasted into the stone wall's gate. First, dozens of people emerge on foot. Then come simple carts and stretchers...
Do a headcount, quick. Make sure all our people and the rescued Infected are accounted for.
We're in luck. The defenders are retreating, so there's nobody who can stop us now.
As the last of the people make it to the other side of the wall, a figure slowly appears from the dust.
That's where the problem lies. They retreated far too easily.
Not to mention the firepower and manpower we faced when we stormed the place isn't up to the standards of what a secret military installation would have. It's like they're deliberately withdrawing.
...And before we entered, some of the soldiers outside didn't even try to attack the evacuating Infected.
I don't know if they're dealing with internal issues, or if they want to scoop us all up at once. We need to leave right away, just to be safe—
An artillery shell nearly scrapes the top of Talulah's head as it screams towards the back of the procession.
Crying and weeping break out all around her. She looks towards where the shell came from—spotting the command bridge of a towering warship, the flag of the First Army raised high above it.
Bombarding their own damn city...
Tell everyone to retreat using the route we planned out! I'll find a way to draw their attention!
Talulah—
Just go already!
A second shell crashes into the ground, then a third... Rubble falls, the wall collapses, and the weakened Infected who just barely escaped death now only have the strength to wipe away their tears.
Members of Reunion rush about, half-dragging, half-supporting the Infected as they leave this place. Only one person watches the distant artillery barrage, stopping in her tracks.
Sirka? It's dangerous here, you need to evac with us, quickly.
No, you all go first.
I have something I need to retrieve, forgot it in the Generalik's residence.
Generalik! Please wait, Generalik! Please check your private channel, the Marshal is looking for you.
Out of the way! All of you!
Before you use my mother to threaten me, you should take a good, long look at your medals! Are useless wretches who quiver at the sight of a few traitors fit to call themselves soldiers of Ursus?!
What are you doing here, Generalik—
Who is manning the cannons? Have your worthless fingers degenerated to the point they can only be used to play cards?
I-I can explain—
Don't think you can hide your dereliction of duty from me. Why are you not concentrating your fire on the gate? Why are the main cannons not yet ready to fire?
We're not being negligent, Generalik. It's only been ten minutes since the order to retreat was issued. If we fire the main cannons now, many of the men still in the sealed district will be—

There's still plenty of traitors in there too! According to the itinerary I drew up, as long as they're not stupid enough to shoot themselves in the foot, any friendly fire will still be within controllable limits.
I am tired of you using your bleeding hearts as an excuse, Lieutenant Colonel Bondarenko.
A shining saber digs into the officer's neck.
Zelgrad is my city, but do not forget that it is also Ursus's city. Each grain of rye you swallowed since the day you enlisted was so that you would obey my every order today.
Generalik, urk—
I'll give you one last chance, Bondarenko. I want to see the main cannons ready in five minutes.
Remember, there's more than one gunnery officer in the First Army!
...Ahem, Marshal, i-it's me... A thousand pardons, I know this is the Generalik's private channel...
Generalik, I dare not hang up on the Marshal. Please, take the call.
...Give it here, then get out of my face.
'Soldier of the First Army', hah, what a worthless honor...
Respect those below you, Anatoliy. This is not the first time I had to remind you.
But there is a more pressing matter at hand. You promised me, did you not? All you were to do was obtain the data on the Sarcophagus, then return immediately.
Mother... I tried my best to get the results you wanted dearly.
But you made me sit back and watch as those marrow-sucking parasites crawled all over my city, made me stand shoulder-to-shoulder with abject cowards, fleeing in disgrace—
You really do want to take my life.
Everything I have done was to keep you away from this meaningless battle, my dear.
The Fourth Army approaches Zelgrad even now. Do you want me to look on helplessly as my own son is drawn into this fetid swamp?

The Fourth Army... Haha, what difference is there between them and those traitors in the city? They have all turned their backs on this great empire, turned their backs on the creed you once taught me.
You were always molding me into a loyal pet, Mother... So why is it you who let go first?
...Bzzt...
Talulah stops mid-sprint, looking at the distant giant as large as a mountain.
At first, she wanted to find an empty yet conspicuous place where she could release her Arts, using her own retreat to provoke the First Army and draw their attention.
However, all sound suddenly disappears from the warship. Not even the deployed secondary cannons make a move.
What is going on...?
...You repeat that?
You didn't mishear me. I am in your residence in the sealed district, using your private frequency to speak with you.
I am the spy dispatched by the Fourth Army—
Y-You're the one who tried to assassinate me that day.
Indeed. That is how Marshal Kuznetsov does things. Every important figure in the First Army is on his list. He has been plotting for three entire years.
So are you begging me to throw you a lifeline now?
I beg that you cease fire for a moment, until the First Army can pick me up on your ship. As you and the Marshal had promised earlier.
Naturally, you will not only be saving my life... I am hesitant to say this, but I harbor a deep-seated hatred for Marshal Kuznetsov.
Young lady, if you have concealed the information I require out of 'hesitance', then I am more than happy to restart the artillery.
Why do you think we can trust a thief and assassin who has barged into our home?
Your High Excellency, I am willing to give you all the details and spend an entire day verifying my identity, but the march of the Fourth Army will not stop.
I have a more effective method in mind: I will directly access Marshal Kuznetsov's private channels, and lead him into saying what you wish to know.
Wait—
...Yevsey? What news?
Marshal Kuznetsov, I am a spy in contact with Yevsey. Due to an emergency, I had to borrow his comms equipment.
I must first verify your identity.
I am the informant he planted in Zelgrad. My identification code was sent to the command center five minutes ago.
'Emergency', you say?
The city is falling into chaos, and I have lost contact with him for the time being.
Civil unrest in Zelgrad?
Very good. Continue your report.
Many rebels of unknown identity infiltrated Zelgrad. They contacted the city's Infected, then launched an attack on the sealed district.
Part of the city garrison seem to be playing along, refusing to meet their challenge. The Generalik appears to be planning to abandon the city.
(Deep breath)
A mutiny is brewing within the troops. A familiar situation, perhaps due to some outside influence.
Do you still remember the mutiny of the Cassian? Those troops who always supported your father to the last, but could not accept your military reforms.
Ancient history. They have already paid the price for their rashness.
Hardly a secret within the Fourth Army. My father left behind many festering boils. Many of our current policies had to be enacted to resolve the mess.
If I may be so bold, are these 'festering boils'... 'debts of love'?
...Surely your intelligence has nothing to do with such flimsy hearsay?
I fear they are related.
The entire Ursine aristocracy knew your father. Marshal Andrian was a model soldier of the empire. Loyal, determined, stubborn, and crude...
But they also knew he was one of the empire's most prolific lovers. The captain of the Cassian was his last sweetheart's nephew.
Right now, rumors are spreading that ten or so years ago, when army officials were in Grypherburg to report to the Tsar, he and General Svetlana Ulyanova Buterina, not yet Marshal—
Enough prattling! Where are you going with this?
(Grits teeth)
Though you have done all you could in the name of your family's honor, even killing your own father with your own hands without hesitation, to prove that such wantonness does not run in the blood...
I regret to inform you that there are still those who do not approve of your methods, who are trying to deprive you of your inheritance, sir.
So much so that you were never able to find the illegitimate daughter that Marshal Andrian carefully safeguarded, a wretched Kuranta... who is now in Zelgrad.
...Who are you?! Your voice—
More importantly, if you do not seize the chance to invade Zelgrad and silence her, she will soon bring proof of those 'rumors' to your loyal troops.
When that time comes, your authority—
ENOUGH!
Distorting facts, trying to rile me into attacking the First Army—I do not know how you found Yevsey, but you have signed your own death warrant.
Hmm...
It is as you heard, Marshal Svetlana Ulyanova, General Anatoliy Svetlanov—
Suka!
Anatoliy—
Enough, Mother! I've had enough! That filthy mongrel spawned by Andrian has dared to slander the Marshal of the First Army.
I swear, I will kill you in the most miserable, humiliating way possible with my own hands! I will drown you in your own blood and see how long a khuyovy bastard like you can last in it!
Oh, Generalik, sir, I've been meaning to ask, have you ever met your father?
Perhaps one day, we will meet again thanks to this shared blood of ours... brother dearest.
Mother...
Do not be so easily deceived, Anatoliy. She merely wanted to goad you, though what her true goal is we can only—
Lieutenant!
...Yes, Generalik?
Relay the order, all men who are able to mobilize are to head to the sealed district to capture that woman.
B-But we no longer have—
You won't live long! YOU HEAR ME?!
Don't rush, elderly and children first!
Raspy throats continue to cry out. Those helping with the evacuation divide themselves between both sides of the road, watching the people walk past them.
Intermittent explosions go off in the distance. The ground beneath their feet shakes. Some of the crowd seem afraid, but most of them stare ahead blankly, clutching bundles of their belongings tight.
Hey, don't go against the flow, that's dangerous!
Also, wear your gas masks as much as possible if you've got one, otherwise cover your mouth and nose with a towel! And don't touch any strange-looking animals—
Hmm? What is it, Lyudmila?
This lady's fainted, got space on your cart?
Should be able to fit one more. Let's try it.
Lyudmila crouches down, passing the unconscious person on her back to them.
Lyudmila! Come over to the front, quick! Tulin might be in trouble!
Got it.
...We meet again, Ratkov.
I shouldn't let you go free.
My orders are to purge the traitors in the city.
By traitors, do you mean the people behind me?
All they want to do is save their own lives, those lives they have devoted to Zelgrad and Ursus. Surely this is not treason?
There is still a chance, Ratkov—
As she speaks, the soldiers in front of her suddenly lift their weapons. Several crossbow bolts fire towards the space behind her.
Tulin subconsciously shrinks back. She turns her head to see Lyudmila standing behind her, effortlessly brushing away the bolts.
I was talking about her... but as you can see, we failed.
A lot of people are saying Reunion's here. The way we see it, the First Army's defenses won't be enough to hold them back.
If the Generalik still has a way to deal with them, then let him think about it.
For us, we've decided to retreat.
The soldier named Ratkov steps forward, grasping a folded-up plan. He shoves it into Tulin's hand.

Then, to the amazement of Tulin's followers, an entire company of soldiers lines up and marches away towards the left of the city gates. They march in silence, and the only sound they make is the tread of their boots.
He just decided that all on his own. Or rather, they did.
...What is it, Tulin?
She sees Tulin unfold the piece of paper, hands shaking slightly as the eyes sweep across the dense mass of characters—eyes that are scattered, unfocused.
The paper tilts, then is straightened up. Tulin blinks rapidly.
Need help?
Ah, Lyudmila...
Could you... help me read what it says here? I'm having some...
...'The control room for the gates is on the east side, needs a standard password, check the appendix'. This is a guide on how to use the gates.
I see. Hand it over to my people. We can leave soon.
Some miners take the paper and leave. Tulin lets out a deep sigh.
Spasibo, Lyudmila. When I saw those letters, and how crowded together they were...
And here I was thinking you were a bookworm.
I really am interested in the knowledge and tales within books, but most of the time, I need someone to help read it out loud. Because of that, I've always learned a little more slowly than others.
But... 'Ivan Tulin'...
Ivan Tulin is a prolific author. Out of all the Ursine writers in the last few years, nobody wrote better than him, or more.
University students in Grypherburg love discussing the complex, finely crafted quotations in his books, always proclaiming how well-read Ivan Tulin is.
You're—
We did it, Tulin!
...Right.
Everyone! Listen well, for we are leaving Zelgrad!
Great cheers echo through the city, as the people rush through the heavy gates.
Some lift their arms in joy, some kneel to caress the soil outside the city, smiling as tears form in their eyes, weeping even as the corners of their mouths turn upwards.
They look back at the road that brought them here, then turn forward once more, their footsteps ringing out in heavy, muffled echoes.
Once everyone has faded into the dusty distance, Tulin's throat quivers with a sigh barely audible to anyone.
Crownslayer sees Tulin turn away, though the hand gripping the pickaxe relaxes a little.
...Lyudmila, I'll need to find some other time to discuss the tale of that author with you further.
Many years ago, he was forced to leave us. Eventually, even I lost all contact with him.
Ursus may have mocked him, banished him, even killed him... but could never destroy him.
Because we are still here, and we still have tomorrow.
Twilight creeps up Tulin's determined face, those quiet words slowly lost to the wind.

lines.loc: Assault Ship Volnov, Command Center Jan 22, 1102, 09:59

lines.x: At least... I made it until the Morvan fell apart.
Hah... Time for you to fight fair for once.
*cough*—
It seems you have no need for your many comrades' lives.
Get away from him!
(Ancient Ursine dialect) 'May his hand misheed its master's will, may his blade strike his own body down.'
Argh—!
The unsheathed chachek suddenly swings towards its wielder's neck, the sharp edge moments away from chopping through bone—

lines.st: Scioppa

lines.x: You—

lines.st: Scioppa

lines.x: I... Scioppa—
Get behind me, Oleg.
And here I thought you merely a dabbler in Arts. I never expected...
You may live, but you cannot escape your fate. This means you need to die, a greater need than ever before.
You should've made those words into one of your spells, 'comrade'.
But I'm not going to give you guys the chance. I know you can use silent incantations, but you're not going to be better than me at old-fashioned swift-casting.

lines.st: Scioppa

lines.x: At nearly the exact same moment, countless vicious bolts of energy burst forth from the war caster, filling the entirety of the silenced space.
Every single piercing note created in an attempt to break the shackles of the spell is swallowed up into nothingness.
Get everyone out of the command center, Oleg.
I can buy you two minutes at most—
—Such... feeble incantations—
Impudent parlor tricks!
(Ancient Ursine dialect) 'I shall have thee suffer, have thee walk an endless road, where even water pure cannot wash the filth off thy body—'
(Ancient Ursine dialect) 'Where even death shall grant thee no peace!'
Quick—
The adjutant quickly blurs in the Volnik chieftain's eyes, turning into stacks of blue, before becoming an endless white.
Extreme pain shoots through every cell in his body. Before his strength to resist is exhausted, he opens his mouth—
The final syllable of the incantation drops into place. Violet flames, so deep as to seem black, suddenly spring up, engulfing both sides of the duel.
—Hey—
Hey, wake up! Scioppa! Chief!
...What...
I thought I was supposed to be meeting the Viy... What are you doing here?
*cough* *cough*! If I accidentally took you and the others with me—
You're not dead, and you didn't take anyone anywhere! I'm fine, feeling a little pain at most, but fine, really.
...I'm not dead?
Of course you're not! You jabbered on a bunch, then the entire khuyovy cabin went up in flames.
But that black fire quickly died out, and those war casters disappeared.
They retreated. Why?
No idea, but it's a good thing all the same. I thought you burned them to death, to be honest.
I couldn't do it.
What're you talking about? You said you met the Viy, but I saw it slam the door in your face because of how much better you are than it!
...Hmph.
What's there left to say at this point? Well, I say, have everyone ready to leave the ship ASAP!
Huh? You still—
That's right. I still need to give Kuznetsov one last parting gift.
Up upon the highest deck of the ship, the Kuranta watches his troops line up in formation in pensive silence.
The canyon chill blows past, blowing away the dust accumulated from days of regret, blowing away the watchman's fluttering thoughts.
You certain about this? There's still time to tell everyone to get back to their posts.
I'm going to teach that man a lesson, so that he'll never look down on us again.
When everything's settled, I'll find you all.
When everything's settled, huh... Will there really be a day when all our affairs are settled?
There will be. There must.
Even matters that have gone unresolved for centuries will finally have their answer.
The sun slants towards the west. Most of the soldiers take the scenic route, all to have more time to call out to the ones on deck.
Almost everyone leaving the Volnov looks for their chieftain to say goodbye, as if this is just their summer vacation, simply a short trip back to their hometowns—
Back to the fields, the forested mountains, the banks of a creek, laden with reeds.
Who's the bad guy you're meeting, who's so bad you can't bring us along, Boss? A giant, Baba, or the Viy?
Well, no matter who it is, I'll sing you a song before you go! The one Oleg said you never finished singing—

lines.st: At the end of the road lies the Viy, not the tsar or any god I know♪
Just a monster of body big, whose eyelids need others to hold♪
Prayers? It hears no such thing, and those that meet it know it makes no sense♪
All they do is plop themselves down, like taking off armor they'll never put on again♪
When the Viy opens its eyes, you it sure won't see♪
All it sees is—♪
How your gift once made you you♪
At times it's war, a hate that spans the ages♪
At times it's a field that paid Catastrophe's wages♪
That wailing and weeping that never end, not even in dream♪
And once its eyelids droop down once more♪
You'll find some things have quietly changed♪
The river dry flows free once more♪
The children dead come home once more♪
All of these are impossible things♪
Which is why we won't sing for those going to the Viy's home♪
And why we won't carve their tale in stone♪
We pour wine on the ground, and with voices low we say♪

lines.x: He's going down to the end of the road, all in our name♪
Up until the second day when the sun shall rise again♪
Still we advance, draw our blades, cut down our foes♪
Still we bleed, fall to the floor, bury our dead with woe♪
Still, history pushes us, back onto our own blades we go!
The Rhodes Islanders, accompanied by one noisy 'miniature house', finally emerge from underground after following Klim's hand-drawn map.
They find themselves within a secluded ornamental forest, where they are greeted by a bright blue sky.
...In short, I don't know how I got there either.
Like you said, this is long after my era, which means I don't really have anywhere to go. But, looking at it another way, it means I can go anywhere.
Hey, Closure, show me that 'mirror' thing, let me get a good look at my current body—

You said you were buried near the Sarcophagus, and there was an Originium mine near the Sarcophagus's excavation site, which was one of the reasons why Chernobog was able to develop so quickly despite being in Ursus's wild east.
Some remains, an Originium mine, the former Sarcophagus... the 'mini-house', some blank Originium I accidentally spilled, and the 'prototype' whose functionality was disassembled...

...I got it. I got it!
Maybe I can try—
No, I need to try.
Closure?
Closure stops, rummaging through her bag before magicking out a foldable screen. She deploys it, then continues pulling out more strange things normally only seen in Engineering's offices.
She sits down on the ground, as the miniature house hops over inquisitively.
What did you figure out? If it's to do with Kal'tsit, then I haven't even mentioned her yet.
I know she's dead, obviously. I knew this day would come sooner or later. Not even someone like her is an exception. But tell me, what bright idea did you stumble on?
Did you figure out what your tests were lacking, Closure?
Yep. I also know how to bring her back.
The Sarcophagus as both energy source and life pod. Memories formed from Kal'tsit's original data. Blank Originium, i.e., Oka, as a structural base... then add the base-level code we just found.
I've been treating the resurrection experiments as a biological problem this entire time. I never thought of life as a long-running program until now. It's not static code.
Maybe what makes Kal'tsit unique is precisely her self-modification command. Rather than just being a structural alteration as designed, it also set up a self-invoking closed loop.

opts: Inside that information flow space, I saw a few things.
If we go with your metaphor—
Kal'tsit chose to maintain this 'closed loop' of her own accord.

lines.x: ...Maybe from the moment she set up the closed loop, she was no longer just an executed program. She began to upgrade herself, to iterate.
Then that very first self-modification command can be said to be the start of her 'awareness'.
I'll admit, I don't really get stuff of the 'revenants'... But if, say, something has been carved onto the deepest part of her soul, or if that something represents her will as a person—
Then it has to be that command.

opts: I understand.
Time to get to work, Closure.

lines.x: Closure takes out the storage containing the data extracted from the Sarcophagus, and attaches it to a hard disk and heat sink.
Black cables stretch out from an ad-hoc computer case, linking to a support rack cobbled together from a glass cabin.
The 'calcite' representing the base-level code cannot be extracted from the data dump storage, so it is pinned to the center of the open space.
Oka is kept within transparent glass tubes, a little less compared to when the team set out.
A portable life pod is deployed, and within the open space, the borders of a simulated Sarcophagus data environment are delineated, like a 'pond' of pure white.
With everything ready, Closure starts the power, and waits for the screen to light up.

lines.st: System booting...

lines.x: Her eyes are locked to the screen as she taps out the last few commands, not hesitating for even a second.
Everything had to be done speedily and smoothly for this experiment to work.

lines.st: Biological model construction—————100%
Physiological function simulation—————100%
Neuron data upload—————100%

lines.x: Did it...
The prompt they had never seen before finally leaps onto the screen. Everyone holds their breath.

lines.st: Initiate life-phase transition?

lines.x: Several pairs of eager eyes look towards Closure.
She presses 'Yes'.
Welcome back.
Kal'tsit.
Slowly, the life pod opens.
There, you see a familiar face, just as you have hoped to see thousands of times.
Once again, you take her hand.
Dr. Doctor?
Slowly, the woman inside gets up.
Dr. Kal'tsit! / Kal'tsit!
Kal'tsit...

I did it?
Woohoo, I did it!
Kal'tsit, is that you? Do you recognize me? If not, you gotta at least recognize the Doctor and Amiya, right?

Amiya suppresses the urge to dash forward to embrace Kal'tsit, as Mon3tr digs her sharp claws deep into the soil beneath. Each and every one of them looks on nervously, as not one of them can so easily believe this outcome.
In contrast, the woman who has just been roused from her slumber looks to each member of the group gathered around her. Slowly, her bewildered expression begins to soften.
Somebody tell me... Why am I here?
It's all thanks to the Doctor—and Closure, too!
We've been racking our brains to recreate the gemini cycle function and use blank Originium to sculpt a body for you!
The experiments haven't been going well, but somehow, we managed to find AMa-10's source code in the Sarcophagus in Ursus—
That's practically impossible, in theory...
Doesn't matter!
Well... Are you feeling okay? Are your memories all jumbled? And, um—
Do you still remember me?
How could I ever forget you...?
Mon3tr...
I really missed you...
Watch out, Mon3tr! Dr. Kal'tsit may still be very weak!
Thank you, Amiya...
Don't worry... I can tell... my condition isn't particularly serious.
What I really want to know is... where are we, and what is the current situation?
(Pants weakly)

opts: You don't need to be in such a hurry to figure out what's going on.
Don't push yourself. We still have time.
I don't want you to worry...
All's well at Rhodes Island.
Everyone is here.

lines.x: Dr. Doctor...
I must say... I really do not agree with how you led Rhodes Island... on such a dangerous operation.

opts: We need you to come back to fight alongside us.
Amiya and I arrived at this decision together.

lines.x: Dr. Doctor, I've never doubted your decisions for a long time. However...
I'm afraid I'll have to reevaluate your decision-making now.

opts: I'll get your whole critique once we're back at Rhodes Island.
Naturally, I had other reasons too.

lines.x: For example?

opts: A promise.
Have you found yourself yet... Kal'tsit?

lines.x: ...I never forgot.

opts: Once again...
Welcome back, Kal'tsit.

lines.x: I hear fighting... I suppose Ursus's many factions are still vying for the Sarcophagus?

opts: This does indeed have to do with the Sarcophagus.
The situation is a little more complicated than that.
We should get ready to pull out.

lines.x: Doctor, I need to know... where is the Sarcophagus?
I still have... unfinished business.
After stopping in front of the bloody palm print on the door for a brief moment, the man starts to slowly walk out of the dark corridor.
The only energy pipeline from the satellite city has begun to operate once more. He has fulfilled his promise.
Nothing following that is of any importance to him.
Alita...
The man slowly falls to his knees and picks up one of the countless ice-cold bodies on the floor.
Had you long since given up the ideals that you talked about as a girl, when you fed fowlbeasts by the pond, would you really have ended up like this?
I never had the courage to tell you... I'd actually completely forgotten the promises I made before the statues of our forebears... those lies I told for the empire's sake.
And I've never really cared about their so-called 'better tomorrow.'
All I know is that, when a soldier leaves home, his family is always there to send him off, yet when we left Chernobog, the entire city was still asleep.
For so many days and nights, all I've wanted is to go back to Lada's bedside.
But I had to keep an eye on you, too.
I have to look after you... so you won't be alone... chasing things and hurting yourself in the process.
Hah...
Klim Valuev... In the end...
You still managed to accomplish nothing.
All clear...
The bodies...
Found a survivor.
Who are you people?
Never mind. Doesn't matter.
If you're here for the Sarcophagus. It's right behind me.
If that's not what you are after...
Then get out. Now.
Assessment complete.
The Sarcophagus weaponization module has been completely destroyed. Only its energy transformation stabilizer module remains, with an external channel still operational.
The Sarcophagus's core structure is massive and complex. It is nigh impossible to neatly dismantle for transportation with such little time. Please advise.
Right, it's irreparable. It cannot be done, even with all of us deploying the strongest evocation-conversion Arts at once.
The weaponization module's damage appears to have been caused by some sort of even greater power.
Furthermore, based on observations prior to entry, the plate housing the Sarcophagus has suffered continual external attack. We can surmise that the First Army has already abandoned Zelgrad.
Acknowledged.
We'll pull out immediately.
From afar, the soldiers, having just received their orders, look upon the sole survivor.
The sound of explosions outside is drawing ever closer, yet it seems he is making no effort to escape at all.
Why waste time on a man who will not live?
Hm...
This is the last time. Forgive my cowardice, Alita.
After all... you've always been the bravest of us.
Even the Second Army... Even the Second Army has turned against me, Witte!
What are we waiting for? For the traitors to march into Grypherburg and Tsarevgrad—for them to breach the palace and impale me on the throne?
Your Imperial Majesty... You must know why the Second Army resorted to such means.
The Winter Emergency Resource Allocation Act.
What?
They think this bill will inevitably hurt their interests, perhaps even the Army's authority independent of the legislature. That's why they chose to turn a blind eye to the Fourth Army's actions.
No... Even suppose they had a problem with that, they wouldn't have gone against the edict like this... Someone must be fanning the flames!
Is it her... or who else would it be? My dear aunt...
Majesty... All things considered, our top priority should be the crisis at hand.
That said, each day that this bill isn't passed is another day that the Second Army doesn't point their spears directly to Grypherburg.
Therefore, strictly speaking, they have yet to form any kind of coalition of mutual interest, and we still have a chance to negotiate with the Second Army.
Moreover—
Witte, Witte! Listen to yourself. What nonsense are you talking?
Even a traitor like Saveliy knows that the Second Army's decision to stand on the sidelines is tantamount to rebellion against us, and you're still making excuses for them.
If I didn't know you and trust you, such words would be enough to brand you a traitor like the rest of them!
If such thinking calms your nerves, then fine, but I also know that you are no tyrant. You want to solve real problems, not emotional ones.
Which is why, no matter how furious you may be, you still have that basic level of sanity. You are not like those wild beasts.
What will you do, Witte? Will you really accede to their demands and postpone the citizen's forum indefinitely?
No, Majesty, I won't. The final deadline that we gave them is tomorrow's citizen's forum.
Why?
If, before the citizen's forum is called, we fail to cut a deal with the Second Army, make no progress on the Sarcophagus's energy, and the Grand Duchess doesn't change her position...

Then we will have no choice but to mobilize the Central Army and stop all these sides from coming to blows, and at the same time put a stop to all this sedition once and for all... There will be no mercy or patience.
Even if none of us know whether the empire can still withstand a civil war of such scale.
Within the fire burns the final urgent letter from the south.
Before the flames can reach her fingertips, Elisaveta lets go of the letter and pulls back her hand.
So the Second Army chose to stand on the sidelines too?
Although this development is hardly unexpected.
Hm...
It's just that the Chairman may have to play his very last card.
My merciful, fledgling, and pitiful liege... Within you flows the blood of the old Tsar, yet unlike your father, you are not fit to be autocrat of all the Ursines.
Nor is there an advisor at your side, as capable as the late Empress was.
If all you're doing is pushing things through, how long can you possibly last?
It's a good thing, then, that an individual more suited to the job has returned...
Her gaze turns to a woman looking at a painting on the wall.
Her features are practically the same as those of a woman in the portrait.
Auntie.
Is this... a painting of me?
No, my love. That is your mother. Your father, too.
It seems I have forgotten their smiles.
It's a cruel side effect that sometimes comes with the pains of life, not to mention that you've been through far too much these past few years.
But I must remember.
You will. I will help you... I will always help you, and stand by your side.
Ever since you were a child, you have been strong and unwilling to concede defeat. You are far too much like your father.
My father... What was he like?

A ruler with excellent foresight, ambition, gallantry. He poured his heart and soul into revitalizing Ursus's territorial expansion and feeding his citizens, never resting even a moment until his death.
One could say that he was the greatest man to ever grace Ursus, second only to Igor Velikiy, who forged this empire.
He sounds very... distant.
Right, he was extraordinarily hard to get close to. Only your mother ever dared to stand near him.
Really? That sounds very lonely.
...I doubt he ever felt that way, other than when your mother passed—
Auntie, what's wrong?
Let's talk about something else, Nastya.
Do you want to go back to Grypherburg?
Grypherburg...
A hesitant expression, one that Elisaveta is all too familiar with, appears on Anastasia's face. After a brief moment, she speaks her will.
I want to see Fedya.
What?
Fyodor, my little brother.
I want to see him.
If I must return to Grypherburg to see him, then I wish to go back.
If he is not there, then I will go to where he is.
No matter where he is?
Yes, no matter where he is.
And why do you wish to see him?
Must I have a special reason? I think he probably wants to see me, too.
If that is the case, Anastasia, then you must know a certain truth first.
I am listening.
While you were missing... no, wandering all over Ursus, Fyodor succeeded your father and tried his best to be a good Tsar.
Unfortunately, he is simply no good at it, and the job is not a good fit for him either.
If memory serves, he loves reading, and he even wrote his own poems. Does he still do that?
His role as the Tsar has no doubt consumed a significant majority of his time. Even if he still does write, it is most likely satirical poems written to vent his anger.
That is just conjecture, though.
It has been a very long time since he spoke to me. Even his letters are penned by others on his behalf.
It seems that he hasn't changed at all... He worries about how others see him, too much for his own good.
My poor Fedya. I can practically imagine how hard he pushes himself to become an unbiased—even ruthless—symbol... because that is what the people want.
But he should never show that facade to you, of all people. After all, you are the only family we have, and we used to be so close... Right?
That was a long time ago.

There have since been certain things that I handled in a less than satisfactory way, even if it was all out of concern for him. The saddest thing is that we share the same name and should be helping one another.
Instead, he trusted an outsider, and one from the bottom rung of society with no foresight, to the point that he dragged all of Ursus into a terrible mess.
Now, this great land faces a hopeless future because of his reckless actions.
If he would turn away a loyal family member and subject like myself at this perilous juncture... then how many do you think still stand by his side?
...I understand now.
What do you want me to do?
Save him, and save Ursus, my dear Nastya.
You are the only one. Only you can do this.
Because... within you flows his blood.
I should never have doubted your loyalty, my dear Witte.
But if worse comes to worst, as you said, then you'll have to forgive my stubbornness, as I will have to take to the front lines.
My most loyal men will be fighting for me, and with the Second Army turning against me, that is the most effective way to rouse my people.
Your Imperial Majesty!
Trust me, Witte. After all, I'm not like those weak tin soldiers in the fortress. I am—
The Emperor and Autocrat of All the Ursines.
Your Imperial Highness, we have news from the Deity Grypherburg Power Dispatch Center.
What have they discovered?
They say that the high-voltage fencing's isolated failure points have been restored. Once the transformer is in place, we will be able to use the node to restore power to some of the affected areas.
Which line did the failures originate in?
The lines connected to the newly built energy pipeline. That said, the power facilities are old.

They were originally intended for use only while the city was stationary, but the lines failed not too long ago, so we temporarily isolated the failure points for investigation. They have been restored now.
Thank you. You are excused.
It's better than nothing, but can this tiny bit of energy really feed the entire empire?
No... This is a sign, Majesty.
One that tells us the worst is yet to come.
Shh. She's asleep. Please, try not to wake her...
(In Sami) So, you got yourself involved.
I know what I am getting myself into.
(In Sami) Says everyone who is willingly deceived.
(In Sami) Despite appearances, its heart is completely empty. Everything you hear and see is a mere projection of your desires.
If you are really worried, then stay here and help me.
Use your Shaman eyes to help me see through this darkness.
(In Sami) No, that is not part of our deal.
(In Sami) The ritual is complete. I shall take my leave.
(In Sami) Before your vulgar and stupid desires backfire on you, do not forget to fulfill your end of the bargain.
Main forces... retreating...
This is your final order... Eliminate... Infected creatures—
Acknowledged.
Staying behind to clean up again...
The soldier tosses his communicator to the side and takes a swig of vodka.
This morning, while he was kneading dough in the field kitchen, he found himself dragged outside by his officer.
This wasn't his first time using Originium bolts, but it was his first time taking a life, even if it was a mutated animal.
Before he left, he stuffed all the spirits he had into his backpack. Ever since, every time he's fired a bolt, he's taken a swig. It is the only way to keep his fingers from shaking.
A cloudbeast, or perhaps something that resembled a cloudbeast.
He thinks back to how the fluffy little things would hop into the kitchen and tug on his pants with their claws, and he would tear off a chunk of bread in exchange for a chance to pat their heads.
Sorry, old friend...
He approaches the creature lying on the ground unsteadily and reaches his right hand out—
Suddenly, the creature violently bounces up and turns into a black shadow. It leaps toward the soldier, causing him to shriek and raise his arms instinctively.
Blyat! How many times have I told you?! Hold your weapon upright, get a bead on your target, then fire!
Once I'm done with these ublyudki, I'll drown you in your vodka!
Right after he reprimands his subordinate, despite the bolt pierced through its body, the mutated creature shrieks and leaps up again.
Before the two are able to react, a scorching hot wave blasts past them. The beast is incinerated, turned to ash, while the pavement beneath it melts into a charred black pit.
Wait! You're—
Slow down, Private. Lower your weapon. Stand aside and stay alert. I will handle her.
He shouldn't stay here. Neither should you.
These creatures are crawling all over this city. No one should be here.
That is not for you to decide, Reunion. My commanding officer says the area is abandoned, but I have not received orders to move out.
And so, I cannot allow these crazed creatures to flee Zelgrad. They would go southwest and spread their disease to the people there.
Somebody has to stay... A few hundred lives for thousands more. It's a fair price to pay.
I've seen many soldiers lay down their arms during confrontation with Reunion, letting civilians leave in peace.
Were those your orders, too?
No, they were decisions we made on the spot. You won... temporarily, at least.

The First Army has had losses before, but even the greenest of our soldiers stood steadfast in the face of Gaulish artillery. They waited where they stood with their stump legs for the Tsar's reinforcements.
Zelgrad belongs to the First Army... From now on, whenever Ursine citizens bring up the city, it will be known as the front line of the empire's glory, where all the monsters were quelled.
Which is why, if you aren't here to kill us, I ask you to let us fulfill our duty as Ursine soldiers.
The woman nods, and the old officer lowers his guard. He signals to the soldier standing nearby and walks away with him in silence.
Hmm...
You're still easily swayed by noble-sounding speeches. Perhaps that will always be your flaw, my dear...
You—!
She unsheathes her blade the moment she hears that familiar voice.
But when she turns, she finds not that familiar individual, but the ruined streets.
The main forces have retreated.
Lyudmila, our Reunion friends are still fighting the army in the city. I can bring a few men with me to help.
Let's just leave this to them. This kind of back alley brawl is exactly Reunion's forte. Besides, you've seen how intense the battles can get in the city.
I'm not trying to sell you short... Anyone who can still hold a blade should stay to protect their friends.
Now that I've had a front-row seat to Reunion's combat style, I must say it's really quite remarkable.
...I haven't been one of them for a while now.
But just to be safe, I'll be heading back to check on things and fill Red in on your situation over here.
Right. For safety's sake, I'll take everyone deeper into the forest. We'll meet up at the western boundary of the forest.
Sounds good to me.
But before that...
I need to know who you really are.
Sure enough...
Ivan Tulin was an incredible warrior. If someone is taking his name, I need to know why.
Isn't that exactly why?
Ivan Tulin. This name is like a banner in the Northern Tundra. I don't want this name to disappear from the public consciousness.
You mean he's—
It was maybe three years ago. In the end, he wasn't able to escape the Patrol Units' manhunt.
I know I'm not the only person to have learned and received help from him, and I may not be the one most deserving of taking up his name. I just believe that somebody has to do it.
I couldn't afford to wait for somebody to step up to the task, so I did.
Perhaps Talulah will be disappointed once she learns the truth... but I believe you.
Could you at least tell me your real identity, your actual name?
...Milana.
A normal miner, the daughter of peasants.
All my miner brothers and sisters know this, but they prefer to call me Tulin, out of habit.
But it'd make me very happy to have a good friend willing to call me Milana.
Alright, Milana—
With a hint of remorse, Milana nods to Crownslayer, bidding her farewell.
Then, she slowly walks toward the source of the sobbing—a young girl, and some broken parts scattered across the ground.
Come on, Yana, don't cry. I'll help you look. We'll put it back together.
No... *sob*... We can't do it. Only Papa knows how.
Um, did something happen here?
*sigh* This young lady here fell and broke her pocket watch.
Her father... Li'l Letov, was the best watchmaker in town. He died this morning under a collapsed beam in their house. It's what he left her.
The young woman nods and drops to her knees to get on the same level as the little girl. She reaches her right hand out, and dusts off the girl's dirty clothes.
Yana, right? Can I call you Yanushka?
...Mhm.
I remember you. You were so brave during the evacuation. You aren't crying just because of the broken watch, right?
Papa... died. Our home... is gone.
I don't know... where we can go...
Perhaps none of us know...
But we need to keep walking until we find our new home.
...Go back, Milana. Your leg hasn't completely healed. This is far enough.
Leithanien is very far, Tulin. I don't know if this might be the last time we see each other.
Maybe it will be... but that place is free of the Ursine military police. I will be able to study and create in peace again, for a while.
Yes, I hear they have towering spires, taller than even the clouds. And their magic and music can bring warmth to even the coldest nights.
But I don't need warmth. I need to find that spark of fire for the people.
I can feel Ursus's harsh cold, but I don't know how to strike at its source... Just like my brother... I can only go to see more, and see for myself all the suffering faces across the lands.

To me, Leithanien isn't a punishment. I will tear up all those arrogant scriptures, and turn even their most complicated spells into language that the workers can understand, to bring an end to this cold once and for all.
A language that even I can understand?
Haha, you're right... Milana, as a friend, I have one earnest request.
After I'm gone, I want to entrust everyone here—all the miners coughing up blood in the mines, and all the children looking for bread in the snow fields, I entrust them to you.
...Tulin, are you kidding me? I'm not like you. I'm an ordinary woman.
No, I'm an ordinary man myself. Every great person out there is actually as ordinary as can be.
Greatness isn't a gift you are born with. It's simply the hope that numerous ordinary folk have placed in those who are willing to carry a burden.
He reaches his right hand out to Milana.
Promise me, Milana. Whether I come back with glory... or send back a broken, blood-soaked chapter... you must live.
Look after them in my place. Don't let them simply bear with the pain. Let them grow roots in the pain.
Tulin... Will I... ever see you again?
As long as I'm still alive, I will do whatever I can to write back.
But the moment we must part ways has come.
Goodbye, my dear friend...
If we will never see dawn again, then light up each and every cold night in your own way.
A lot of times, the roads that we walk are slippery and full of potholes. Even the most incredible men are bound to stumble and fall.
That's not our fault. The fault lies with the place where we run and stand.
It's just like how your papa could fix all kinds of pocket watches, but if a watch's shell was bent, then your papa wouldn't be able to fix it, no matter how much he polished its parts.
All we can do is find a new shell and fit it with parts and make it better than the original. Your papa would be so proud, if you managed to do that.
Milana finishes and lifts her head to find the workers slowly gathering around her and the two children.
All of them are listening intently, with some of them fighting back tears.
Yanushka, everyone... Today, you have no choice but to leave your homes—
Help... Just what is going on?
There are bombs falling from the sky, and the whole town is crawling with monsters—
Why... What happened to the army? Have they given up on this place, on protecting us?
Bozhe moi... We've been abandoned again...
Why wait for anyone to save us?
Why do you always need to rely on others for protection? Why must you keep indulging in the city's false spring?
Don't you have the same strength as those high and mighty men with big names?
Standing atop ruins of the recent past, the white-haired Liberi peers down—Those who are unwilling to leave their homes are gathered in front of her, listening to her speech.
Among them are workers, soldiers, the elderly, and children... Faces you see in just about every city in Ursus. They are confused. They are strong.
Friends of Zelgrad. You have my praise for your resilience and my compliments for your bravery.
But, esteemed friends, do you know which words the empire uses to describe you? 'Restrained,' 'kind,' 'obedient.' Yes...
They kissed you on your foreheads and branded them with the words 'restrained.'
They drained your blood and poured 'kindness' into your veins.
They inflicted your bodies and souls with weariness to make you 'obedient' and easy to bend to their will.
Under the banner of equality, they bestowed upon you equal destitution. And with hatred and envy, they traded for your love of life and courage in the face of fate.
More importantly, they sealed your lips and made you ashamed to speak that sacred word—strength.
Yes, 'strength.' Something that should be abundant in your lives.
For they know that once you think you have strength, you will crush their extravagant palaces and smash their authority.
People of Ursus, you can do this—
...If you want me to do this, Auntie, then I will.
I will make them believe, and my voice will reach them... throughout Ursus, and to Grypherburg.
Yes, dear Nastya. Watch them. They are waiting for you.
The noble princess nods slightly and begins walking down the stairs to the starving men gathered below.

The men are haggard and weary. They are starved to the point that they can't even lift their heads, and their hunched backs appear slight in the darkness. Right now, there is only one thing on their minds—
'Yurodstvo.'
Once, they willingly endured, but now they have desire. Yet before any of them can voice their wishes, a peaceful, unquestionable voice rings out.
My suffering brothers and sisters, people of Ursus... I have returned.
The voice sounds the same to every one of its listeners, as though it is capable of cleansing the lands of all injustice and bringing salvation to all suffering.
I see your tears have run dry, yet you still cry out for mercy.
I see your bodies are covered with scars, yet you still crawl forward in the mud.
Until this day, when you finally look upon me—the Grand Princess of Ursus.
And I shall declare to you the meaning of patience.
All of a sudden, there are bread, cheese, and cured meat... as if they have fallen from the sky.

Everyone in attendance forces themselves to lift their heads and reach their hands out. Though they are battered and bruised, not a single voice carries resentment. The only thing that can be heard is thunderous applause: 'Long live the Princess.'
Each of them clasps their hands for the Yurodstvo.
The Grand Duchess looks to the top of her castle and nods.
Children of Ursus, hear me...
I see your teary eyes—
There is no need to wail simply because your wounds are torn asunder. It will wash away the dust coating your souls.
Do not curse the arrival of your suffering. It will open the door to eternity for you.
Your suffering will from now on be your sustenance. It will bring you boundless strength.
Use this strength to repay those who took joy in your suffering.
There will come a day when we deserve these hardships we suffer, which we will use to measure the weight of our lives.
But we will never sing the praises of our suffering. We willingly let our suffering fade away, because no one should be born to suffer.
All of us will die, but if you will allow me, I guarantee to all of you a brief, transient happiness while you yet walk among the living.
Everything will take a turn for the better. Everything will be etched into your flesh and blood. Each bloody trail you leave in the snow is a red carpet that leads directly to our holy dominion.
Do you hear that? Your souls are calling out to you. They are screaming, thirsting for pillage and conquest.
We will endure no longer. Every show of tolerance is an act of suicide. After all, the only thing that stands eternal above this field of permafrost is the truth that strength reigns supreme.
Now come with me. We will be the vanguard that opens the way.
As long as we cut open a small crack on the surface of the ice, the surging waters within will wash away our shackles.
The bread that fills our stomachs is but an insignificant manifestation of power.
I will make Ursus spread her arms wide. The empire's embrace will be a place where tears are no longer shed.
The future that I see has no golden idols or noble masters. Only the strong will walk side-by-side.
Now go. You are the thunderclaps of this storm. Let our will bring order to Ursus!
Once these seeds break through the snow, the wilderness will be white no longer. This is a future where we won't need to be given bread, a future where we all work the fields for one another.
We will no longer be lonely seeds, but field upon field of golden wheat. That day will surely come, just as the sun will rise tomorrow—
Come, Ursines. Follow in the footsteps of your forebears.
In my eyes, you already stand...
...in the kingdom of heaven.

lines.loc: Assault Ship Volnov, Command Center Jan 22, 1102, 21:44

lines.x: Alright, Oleg is gone too. Ship's all clear!
Operation manual, control panel...
Gah, what a pain.
Let's see...
...Looks like there's a reason why this big girl needs a crew of eight just to keep her trudging along.
But that's just fine. If it's a suicide mission, we don't need a full complement.
As long as we tune the presets right—
Command, right? Any further instructions?
...back...
Oh, I almost forgot. We've been coasting along for some time since we entered stealth mode. Soon, we'll be out of maximum comms range.
If we can't hear each other, then I'll hang up.
In position...
...Sechin, all units...
I can't make that out. You want all Sechin units to report back? That's easy. I'll be right there.
...Razin—
Is that 'all units?' Can't say for sure.
But we can at least return the Volnov in one piece. That's bringing everything to a proper conclusion.
The young man follows the figures in the operation manual and adjusts the buttons and knobs on the control panel one-by-one, taking momentary pauses to observe the corresponding readings.
Once everything is ready and confirmed, he lifts the protective cover and presses the button underneath to lock down on the driving mode.
Ship's log, record. January 22, 1102. The Volnov will turn around in an empty field and sail full speed ahead.
Our objective: The flagship of the Fourth Army's main fleet.
Govno... govno, govno, govno!
Where did those casters come from?
Why can't the guns kill them or even aim at them? Blyat, what are they—
Anatoliy.

Oh, Hierda—
Hierda!
There you are. No, why are you here? Didn't I instruct for you to evacuate first?
It's not safe here. I'll come and find you once I retake Zelgrad. Now, go to the base where my mother is—
I'm not going, Anatoliy.
...Even you defy me now?
No, it's not that. I respect your authority and your decision. But did you forget what we talked about?
You want me to return to your mother's side, even send me away first...
Who will protect you if I'm gone?
My battleship, my glorious soldiers of Ursus—they still hold their ground! Many of them are cowards, but they make good enough cannon fodder.
I'll make Zelgrad great again and prove myself to Mother once I clear those fleeing pests out of Zelgrad—
Prove that I'm worthy of her name.
Anatoliy...
I can't always watch over you on the battlefield. Even though you're not by my side, your protection is always with me, isn't it?
The young man smiles childishly as he points to the golden rocks on his body. Somehow, they have been growing in number.
You told your guards to escort me back to base, but your mother is already leaving it to go to the border.
...What?
Marshal Svetlana Ulyanova is abandoning you and Zelgrad. She doesn't even want to stay at the base near Zelgrad anymore.
There's still time to come with me, Anatoliy—
Time to catch up to your mother's fleet... to get an answer.
The Generalik has reached the base safely. We are ready to depart.
Good. We depart as soon as all units are ready.
Yes, Your High Excellency.
Anatoliy.
I can tell by your footsteps.
You can tell it was me, yet you do not even turn. Do you not want to see my face anymore?
I must say that I am disappointed by your actions in Zelgrad.
Why did you not obey my order to retreat?
That's what I want to ask you... Mother.
Why did you abandon Zelgrad? Why did you leave it to the rebels, when you had promised me the city?
We have gained everything we need from Project Zero. The city itself is worthless.
Our priority is to evacuate with the fruits of the research.
Unbelievable... they were telling the truth...
You have betrayed Ursus.
I'm protecting the First Army, and you.
Grypherburg is the epicenter of strife and intrigue right now. With the fruits of Project Zero in our hands, we'd be putting a target on our backs if we took a side.
I had hoped that you would understand this.
Aren't we glorious soldiers of Ursus? Aren't we fighting for the glory of Ursus?
I swore that I would bring down every last one of the empire's foes!
Enough. You're not in a good place. I'll have someone take over your mission. Go to your room and get some rest.
There will come a day when I leave everything to you, Anatoliy... I only hope that when that day comes, you will not be as juvenile as you are today.
I don't understand... I don't even know who I am, Mother.
I'm not a glorious soldier of Ursus, I'm not an Infected, I'm not a pure-blood noble, I'm not even sure if I'm alive...
Enough! No more such talk—
Why... why do you despise me so...?
Is it because I'm the son of a failure?
...No, Anatoliy, whatever the reasons I might be angry with you, your blood is not one of them.
This is the one thing that you never had any choice in.
But you don't deny that I share his blood.
Does it matter?
Does it not?
Anatoliy.
I'm sure I must have gone mad, Mother.
Ugh—
It doesn't matter? How could it not matter? How else can I explain to myself—
Explain your indulgence and exploitation, your pampering and disinterest?
You never saw me as a son! I've only ever been an object, an object that needed no education, a tool for drawing attention!
*cough* *cough*!
No... that's not true—
Then what am I, Mother?
Something that can be cast aside at any moment... right?
Tolya, my child—
You're driving me mad.
Ah... so your blood runs hot too...
Ugh... argh—
Tolya, no...
Why...
Why couldn't I just be your son, a son you could be proud of?
I don't understand... why do things have to be so complicated?

lines.loc: Assault Ship Volnov, Command Center Jan 23, 1102, 00:32

lines.x: Our previous campaigns were like picnics compared to the pace we're making right now.
This is what a high-speed battleship is like... max speed is usually not achievable in combat scenarios, but now—
Let's see what you can do.
Unknown assault ship...
This is Fourth Army Command. Identify yourself.
...It might be the Volnov...
Repeat, identify yourself.
Thirty.
Stay on course.
Unknown ship, you are approaching a frigate of the Fourth Army. Identify yourself.
This is your first warning. Identify yourself immediately to prove that you are not hostile and that you have not been hijacked.
The target is not slowing down.
Have deck artillery on standby.
Roger.
Forty-two.
Continue.
Unknown ship, this is your second warning. Identify yourself immediately.
The assault ship is on a direct course for the frigate, the only thing standing between it and the flagship.
Deck artillery standing by.
Fifty-five.
Steady.
Unknown ship, you have entered a restricted area. Identify yourself immediately!
Under fifty klicks.
Artillery positions, begin tracking target.
Maintain radio silence.
Unknown ship, this is your final warning! Identify yourself immediately!
Thirty klicks.
Get a firing solution.
Seventy-eight.
Steady as she goes.
Twenty klicks!
Unknown ship, you are now within firing range!
Open fire. Disable the ship, but do not destroy it.
Keep firing.
Ninety-one.
Stay on course.
...Blyat, it's the Volnov... why is it still accelerating?
Keep firing!

lines.st: Scioppa

lines.x: ...Bzzt...
...Confirm hit—
Confirm speed...
Crazy zhopa!
Stop your reckless action now, Scioppa Razin, and I will forgive Sechin's previous transgressions.
Take your men and return to your station.
Pfft...
I gotta give you credit. You're trying to negotiate, even when the other side's practically shitting on your face.
Don't worry, I'm just here to return the Volnov.
Besides, Sechin's no longer part of the Fourth Army, as of yesterday.
Any more stupid questions?
Mudak! You absolute fool—
First zhopa, now mudak. Well, I guess I'll let it slide for old time's sake.
By the way, the navigation system of the Volnov is on lockdown and not even I can turn it off. I suggest you send your men to stop it quickly, otherwise...
Who knows what might happen?
Proshchay. Razin out.
The second-floor deck is closest to open ground.
I'll count myself lucky if I don't fall to my death. I wish I had listened when Oleg was telling me about those safe-fall positions.
Oh, screw it—
'Stand up, they say.'

lines.st: He's going down to the end of the road, all in our name♪
Up until the second day when the sun shall rise again♪
Still we advance, draw our blades, cut down our foes♪
Still we bleed, fall to the floor, bury our dead with woe♪
Still, history pushes us, back onto our own blades we go♪
For those who passed through the darkness and saw the face of death♪
One more day the land shall live♪
One more day we will be free♪

lines.x: Hah... singing by myself is boring!
In Baba's name, what I should really sing is—
Durak politics, durak death —
Tupoi, Viy!
Hierda... there you are. I've been looking all over the place for you.
Why didn't you wait for me—*cough* *cough*!
...I'm leaving, Anatoliy.
What?
I said, I'm leaving. I'm going to find my companions, whom I had entrusted to some people who could be trusted.
I should have been devoting myself to helping people who suffer...
What about me? What about me?!
Come with me, Anatoliy.
You will not find salvation here.
Hah... yeah, of course! I stabbed my own mother because of you and that woman—because of what you said!
No, it's not that. That was the right thing to do.
Your mother brought you pain, and brought war to the city, causing countless people to lose their homes. But your actions will bring life to even more.
...What?
You have atoned for your sins, Anatoliy. You have done well.
You—*cough*—ugh!
Anatoliy...
Hierda leans forward to examine the young man once more.
The yellow rocks have spread across his body, creating irregular lumps under his clothes.
It is the end for him.
What you think... doesn't matter anymore. Just...
Help me, one last time.
You can do it. Only you...
But I don't want to, not anymore.
...Hierda?
If this is to be your end, I will accept it. I don't want you to continue to devote yourself to a painful, meaningless life.
This time, I won't help you anymore.
It's almost ten. Everyone who walked in since nine-thirty was a noble.
Most of their faces are unfamiliar to me... but they aren't even trying to hide it, the way they behave themselves.
Has the time changed?
No. I think they just decided they wouldn't bother to hide it anymore.
We've reached the point where a show of force feels better than to continue to deceive the Tsar, as one might play pretend with a child.
Is the Duchess Volkina not here yet?
The Central Army has not received any orders. The Capital Guard's assignments at the venue are within reasonable boundaries.
Perhaps she has chosen to stay on the sidelines, again.
As expected... five minutes until it starts. Let us go in, Vice Chairman.
You go first... I'm waiting for someone.

lines.loc: Great Hall, The State Council of the Ursine Empire Jan 23, 1102

lines.x: Every seat in the hall is filled beneath the great dome of the State Council.
The ushers have led the attendees to their respective seats in an orderly manner, except—
The seats that should have been occupied by citizen's representatives from their respective raions are now occupied by taciturn nobles.
They wear neatly-ironed military uniforms or the latest fashion, wearing medals and luxurious fur shawls.
Clothes of every color surround skin and flesh, while the eyes follow the Tsar's steady steps.
No one stands, no one salutes. There's only a slow and stiff applause that seems intended to delay his speech.
(Whispers) Sir, I have sent hands to check on the representatives—
Ensure their safety.
(Whispers) I will. This is not unexpected. All you need to do is commit to pushing the Act through.
(Whispers) The vote is simply a formality.
Fyodor nods wordlessly and passes Witte by, proceeding towards the podium on his own.
Suddenly, a young noble sitting in the front row stands up and salutes the Tsar with a smile.
All eyes are now upon this interlude.
There is no need for formalities. This is a special day.
Sit down and watch.
Your Imperial Majesty, we came because we heard about the 'citizen's forum' being held today.
I did not prohibit spectators.
Of course, though it seems Your Imperial Majesty has made a small mistake.
We are not here as spectators. We are here as representatives of the 'citizens'.
After all—
She gestures at the room full of nobles.
Are we not the most important citizens of Ursus?
Before you continue your grandstanding, return to your seat.
You are in my way.
Majesty—
And if you claim to represent the 'citizens'...
Then hear what the citizens of the Empire of Ursus truly need now.
Are you ready, Vetochki?
I-I'm ready!
Don't worry about not being heard. You may stutter a little bit, but you know exactly what you're saying.
You've already said it once in the Far North under fire. These people have no weapons, only their tongues.
All you need to do is reveal the truth...
To say what you truly want to say.
Has the one you were waiting for arrived?
No, she hasn't...
Then perhaps she won't. As you said yourself, she may have chosen to stay on the sidelines again—
Ah, it's about to begin.
The Tsar unrolls a piece of paper.

In recent days, he has spent long hours consulting Witte and his other trusted advisors, scrutinized the details with the Supreme Court, and discussed with the citizens' representatives to arrive at the final draft that he is now holding.
Even he is surprised at how calm his voice is.
On my way here, I saw fire pots set up along the roads to provide illumination at night.
Yet we all know that Deity Grypherburg had long stopped using oil lamps and bonfires to illuminate our streets, well before this became a nomadic city.
Perhaps the Grypherburg's nights are as they were a century ago, a situation that has carried on for two months.
When the Originium mines closed, a once-affluent household in Grypherburg began burning furniture to stay warm.
This was when I resolved to exploit the national Originium reserve, so we would not lose people to this harsh winter.
...Even that seems too little, too late.
Too late to prevent the Katorga Incident, and the reallocation of energy from Tsarevgrad to the residential districts can do little to stem the tide.
